scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
scholarships.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are high-level, integrated transnational study programmes at master's level designed and delivered by international partnerships of higher education institutions. An EMJM involves at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, and includes periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence. Each edition runs 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits) and awards either a joint degree or multiple degrees. A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year, and students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme.
scholarships.deadline: Varies by consortium/programme - typically Dec-Feb for a Sept/Oct intake; no single central deadline
scholarships.deadline_display: Varies by consortium/programme - typically Dec-Feb for a Sept/Oct intake; no single central deadline
eligibility: Bachelor's degree (first degree) completed, or the candidate is in the final year of a bachelor's programme
Graduation before the master's programme starts
Officially recognised bachelor-equivalent level of learning (recognised under the legislation and practices of the degree-awarding country) is also accepted
benefits: Full tuition, approx. EUR 1,400/month stipend, travel allowance, installation allowance (exact figures vary slightly by consortium)
scholarships.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits)
scholarships.application_period: Varies by consortium/programme - typically Dec-Feb for a Sept/Oct intake; no single central deadline
scholarships.selection_notes: Highly competitive. Selection depends on academic background, motivation, recommendation letters and programme-specific requirements.
scholarships.program_type: Joint Master Programme
scholarships.image_alt_text: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters students on a European university campus
scholarships.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)

scholarships.title: ICCR Scholarship (Suborno Jayanti Scheme)
scholarships.description: The Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme is the ICCR scheme for nationals of Bangladesh, subsuming the earlier Bangladesh schemes previously offered by ICCR. Under it, the Government of India through ICCR provides scholarship at UG, PG and Ph.D level in Indian universities. Applications are made online on the ICCR A2A Scholarship Portal and must be submitted through the Indian Mission in the applicant's country, which then forwards them to empanelled Indian State and Central Universities. Registration for the 2026-27 academic year is closed and the portal currently lists 2026-27 as the only registration year.
eligibility: 18-30 years old for UG/PG (as of 1 July of the academic year)
PhD applicants must be under 45 (as of 1 July of the academic year)
Must submit SSC/HSC-equivalent mark sheets and transcripts in English
Excludes Medicine/Paramedical/Nursing, Fashion, Law, and integrated 5-year programmes
benefits: Full tuition at an Indian govt./public university
Hostel accommodation (subject to availability; campus hostel mandatory if available)
requirements: Mandatory 500-word English essay on a topic assigned inside the A2A portal
IELTS/TOEFL scores are additional proof, not a substitute for the essay
Passport must have minimum 2 years validity as of 1 July of the academic year
Medical insurance policy with minimum INR 5,00,000 sum assured required
scholarships.duration: Up to 3 years for PhD (extendable up to 2 years at discretion of university); varies by programme for UG/PG
scholarships.application_period: 27 February - 22 April 2026 (AY 2026-27)
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection by Indian Missions/Posts. Offer letter issued by Indian Mission; applicant must accept/reject within 7 days on A2A Portal. Medical fitness upload required within prescribed time limit after acceptance.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (500 seats for Bangladesh under Suborno Jayanti)
scholarships.image_alt_text: ICCR Scholarship banner showing international students
scholarships.name: ICCR Scholarship (Suborno Jayanti Scheme)

scholarships.title: DAAD Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Mostly Master's/PhD (a few UG-eligible programmes exist but are rare)
scholarships.description: The DAAD scholarship database is the German Academic Exchange Service's official listing of its own funding programmes for international students and researchers, together with offers from other selected funding organisations. At the time of verification it returned 150 scholarship options, searchable by country, applicant type, scholarship purpose, subject and programme title. Applications are submitted to the specific programme rather than to a single central DAAD form, and each programme sets its own eligibility, deadline and award conditions. The database also links to the external funding guide www.funding-guide.de.
scholarships.deadline: Varies by programme - Master's typically ~30 Oct; PhD programmes vary (3 Sept or 21 Oct for 2026/27 cycle). Deadlines updated annually in Q2.
scholarships.deadline_display: Varies by programme - Master's typically ~30 Oct; PhD programmes vary (3 Sept or 21 Oct for 2026/27 cycle). Deadlines updated annually in Q2.
eligibility: Most recent degree completed no more than 6 years before the deadline
No general age limit
Exact GPA/academic requirements are set per individual programme, not centrally by DAAD
benefits: Monthly stipend: EUR 992 (Master's) / EUR 1,300 (PhD/doctoral) - figures current as of 2025/26
Health, accident, and personal liability insurance
requirements: Depends on programme - many require IELTS/TOEFL for English-taught programmes
Some require German proficiency instead or in addition
scholarships.duration: 10-24 months for Master's programmes; up to 4 years for PhD (initial award up to 3 years, extendable)
scholarships.application_period: Varies by programme - typically Sept-Nov for a Oct/Nov deadline; check DAAD database per programme
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection by independent committees assessing professional qualifications, study/research project quality, and applicant potential. Special circumstances (e.g. disability) may be considered.
scholarships.program_type: Scholarship database (100+ individual programmes)
scholarships.image_alt_text: DAAD scholarship recipients at a German university campus
scholarships.name: DAAD Scholarship

scholarships.title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS)
scholarships.description: The Global Korea Scholarship is the Republic of Korea's representative government-invited scholarship programme, administered by the National Institute for International Education (NIIED), which invites outstanding students from around the world to study at Korean universities. It funds Korean language training plus associate degree, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programmes across more than 80 GKS universities, and also runs an exchange students programme and Korea-Japan exchange programmes. Applicants apply either through their Korean embassy (Embassy Track) or directly to a GKS university (University Track), and the scholarship covers airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances.
eligibility: Citizen of an NIIED-designated country; parents must not hold Korean citizenship.
High school graduate or expecting graduation.
Undergraduate applicants usually have age and CGPA requirements that change each cycle.
benefits: Round-trip airfare; tuition support; Korean language training; monthly stipend; settlement allowance; medical insurance and other official benefits depending on track.
requirements: English test scores are not mandatory.
TOPIK or TOEFL/IELTS scores may provide additional evaluation advantage.
scholarships.duration: Korean language training (1 year) + associate degree (2-3 years), bachelor's degree (4-6 years), master's degree (2 years), doctoral degree (3 years)
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle: NIIED announces in September, Embassy Track applications are submitted in September and University Track applications in September to November, screening runs October to December and final results are announced in December.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection runs in stages: the recommending embassy or university performs the first screening, NIIED performs the second, and Embassy Track candidates go through a third university screening to confirm final selections. Assessment separates eligibility screening from aptitude screening, which evaluates academic ability, language ability, academic activities, social contribution and international exchange competence, potential for development, and the completeness and authenticity of submitted documents.
scholarships.program_type: Government-invited scholarship degree programme (NIIED, Ministry of Education)
scholarships.image_alt_text: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) students at a Korean university
scholarships.name: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS)

scholarships.title: MEXT (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship
scholarships.degree: UG/PG/PhD - separate application tracks: Undergraduate, Research Student (leads to Master's/PhD), Teacher Training, Japanese Studies, College of Technology
scholarships.description: The Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship is MEXT's scholarship programme for international students, offered in seven types: Research students, Teacher training students, Undergraduate students, Japanese studies students, College of technology students, Specialized training college students and Young Leaders Program students. There are two application routes: a recommendation from a Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission, or a recommendation from a Japanese university. The scholarship pays a monthly stipend, exempts tuition and provides a round-trip travel allowance (airfare), and in most tracks includes Japanese language training before or during study.
scholarships.deadline: Varies by track - Embassy Recommendation (Research Students): April-June annually; varies for other tracks. For 2027 cycle, recruitment is April-May 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: Varies by track - Embassy Recommendation (Research Students): April-June annually; varies for other tracks. For 2027 cycle, recruitment is April-May 2026.
eligibility: Research Students: Bangladeshi citizen, born on or after April 2, 1991 (for 2026 cycle), Bachelor's degree or higher, study in same or related field
Undergraduate: age 17-25 as of April 1 of scholarship year, completed 11-12 years of schooling
benefits: Full tuition, monthly stipend approx. 117,000-148,000 JPY (undergraduate is at the lower end), round-trip economy airfare Dhaka-Japan, 6 months-1 year Japanese language training included
requirements: Application Form (use current year's MEXT form)
Placement Preference Application Form
Field of Study and Research Plan
Academic transcript for all academic years of university attended
Certificate of graduation or degree certificate
Recommendation letter from the president/dean or academic advisor at current/last university
Medical Certificate (filled by a professional medical doctor)
scholarships.duration: Research Students: 2 years for regular course (6 months preparatory education added if needed). Undergraduate: 5 years including Japanese language training (7 years for medicine/dentistry/pharmacy/veterinary science). Standard: Master's 2 years, Doctoral 3 years (4 years for some fields).
scholarships.application_period: Embassy Recommendation (Research Students): April-June annually
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection by Embassy of Japan Dhaka (written exam + interview) for Embassy track; by MEXT Tokyo for University track. Candidates who pass first screening must request provisional acceptance from Japanese universities by September 1.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (multiple tracks: Research, Undergraduate, Teacher Training, Japanese Studies, College of Technology, Specialized Training College)

scholarships.title: France Excellence Charpak Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: France Excellence Charpak is the French government scholarship programme in India, divided into four sub-programmes that allow Indian students to study at undergraduate or postgraduate level in public and private institutions in France. The Master track is designed for one to two years of study at Master's level across all streams and fields, and awardees receive the status of Boursier du Government Français. The Master track pays a monthly living allowance of EUR 860 and covers visa and Campus France procedure fee exemption, student social security and complementary health insurance, accommodation assistance through Campus France in France, and reduced university restaurant meals at EUR 1. The scholarship does not cover travel expenses from India to France or within France, or any other expenses related to the awardee's stay.
eligibility: Indian citizen or hold OCI card
Bachelor's: age 23 or younger at time of application; currently enrolled or completed studies at Indian senior secondary school
Bachelor's: admission to French institution required before applying
Master's: age 30 or younger; currently enrolled or completed studies at Indian institution of higher education
Master's: full-time master's degree in France (semester exchange, internships, research projects not eligible)
Master's: must not have previously been awarded Charpak Master scholarship
Master's: must not be a PhD student or intend to complete master's thesis/training/research in France
Course must take place in France (if part takes place in another country, scholarship will not cover that period)
benefits: Exemption of visa and Campus France procedure fees
Student social security and additional health insurance (mutuelle)
Assistance finding affordable student accommodation (priority CROUS access)
Meal discount at university restaurants (€1 meals)
Access to social and cultural activities organized by Campus France
Travel expenses from India to France NOT covered
requirements: Passport size photograph
Copy of passport (first page with photo and expiry date)
Curriculum Vitae (maximum 2 pages)
Copy of admission/acceptance letter from French higher education institution
Mark sheets and degree certificates (XII, Bachelor's, Master's - including ongoing semesters)
French language certificate, if any (DELF/DALF)
Document of employment/internship record, if applicable
Letter(s) of recommendation from current Indian university/employer or last attended institution
scholarships.duration: Bachelor's: duration of the bachelor's programme in France. Master's: 1-2 years (renewable once for second year based on results).
scholarships.application_period: Varies by track - typically spring/summer
scholarships.selection_notes: Round 1: Complete applications evaluated by selection committee on academic excellence, consistency, quality of statement of purpose, and overall profile. No minimum CGPA or percentage required. Round 2: Shortlisted candidates called for Online Interview (typically April). Plagiarism check on SOP; AI-generated content discouraged and may result in disqualification.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (French Embassy in India / Campus France India)
scholarships.image_alt_text: Campus France India (French Embassy in India) official logo
scholarships.name: France Excellence Charpak Scholarship Program

scholarships.title: MOPGA Visiting Fellowship Program
scholarships.description: Since 2018 the Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA) initiative has been a flagship programme for postdoctoral mobility in France and one of the leading fellowship programmes of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. The 2027 call is the tenth edition, funded by MEAE in partnership with MESRE and implemented by Campus France, and enables young international researchers to carry out a research project in France. Each fellowship runs for 12 months and provides a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance and health coverage including health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance. Successful applicants receive the status of French Government Scholarship holder (BGF) and the fellowship is paid directly by Campus France.
eligibility: PhD obtained within the last 5 years
Non-French citizens (foreign nationals)
Must not have resided in France for more than 90 days during the 12 months prior to application

Research project must align with MOPGA themes: Earth systems, climate change and sustainability, energy transition, societal challenges of environmental issues, or One Health (human, animal and ecosystem health)
Must secure a hosting agreement with a French research institution/laboratory
Early career researchers (post-doctoral) preferred
requirements: CV (max 4 pages)
PhD diploma
Research project description aligned with MOPGA themes
Host laboratory agreement
1–3 recommendation letters
scholarships.duration: 12 months
scholarships.application_period: Calls for application launched yearly in September; applicants notified by email in May; fellowship starts between September and December
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection based on scientific excellence of the project, relevance to MOPGA themes (Earth systems, climate change, energy transition, societal challenges, One Health), quality of the host laboratory, and potential for future collaboration. Applicants notified by email in May.
scholarships.program_type: Government research fellowship (French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, implemented by Campus France)
scholarships.image_alt_text: Campus France (French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs) official logo
scholarships.name: MOPGA Visiting Fellowship Program

scholarships.title: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Undergraduate, Graduate, Japanese Language Institute, College of Technology, Specialized Training College
scholarships.description: The Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a JASSO programme for privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who are already enrolled at a Japanese educational institution and are facing financial difficulties. It pays a monthly stipend of 48,000 yen at graduate or undergraduate level and 30,000 yen at Japanese language institutes, for 12 months from April or 6 months from October. Applications are made through the enrolled institution rather than directly to JASSO, so timing and eligibility are institution-specific.

Excellent academic and character records
Facing financial difficulties

Language requirement: JLPT N2+ OR EJU Japanese 200+ points OR B2 CEFR English (exempt for Japanese language program students)
Other allowance (excluding tuition) must not exceed ¥90,000/month
If financial supporter in Japan exists, their annual income must be less than ¥5 million
Must not receive incompatible scholarships (JASSO Student Exchange Support Program, etc.)
benefits: ¥48,000/month for graduate/undergraduate level; ¥30,000/month for Japanese language institutes
requirements: Application form
Academic transcript
Proof of enrollment/admission
Income certificate
Recommendation

scholarships.title: POSCO TJ Park Foundation Global Scholarship
scholarships.description: The POSCO Global Scholarship in Korea is the inbound component of the POSCO Global Scholarship operated by the POSCO TJ Park Foundation, and it is described by the Foundation as 'The Global Future Leaders Scholarship Program'. It funds non-Korean nationals admitted to Master's or doctoral programmes at designated Korean graduate schools, who must be recommended by their admitting institution. Master's students receive full tuition for four semesters plus living expenses of KRW 1,000,000 per month for 22 months, while doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral students receive full tuition for six semesters plus the same monthly living allowance for 36 months. A one-off KRW 1,000,000 settlement fee, National Health Insurance premiums and Korean language and cultural programmes are also provided.
eligibility: Holds or is expected to hold a Bachelor's degree
Non-Korean nationality; Korean citizens including dual citizenship holders are not eligible
Admitted to a Master's or Doctoral programme at a Korean graduate school
Recommended by the admitting graduate school
Eligible applicant country as listed in the Foundation FAQ
Enrolled at a designated eligible university
benefits: Tuition fees; living expenses; arrival allowance; language excellence scholarships (specific amounts vary by sub-program)
scholarships.duration: Master's: 4 semesters of tuition support and 22 months of living expenses. Doctoral or integrated master's and doctoral: 6 semesters of tuition support and 36 months of living expenses.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle running from Korean graduate school admission in about November to the certificate award ceremony in March; candidates enter by being admitted to and being recommended by a Korean graduate school.
scholarships.program_type: Private-sector foundation scholarship (POSCO Group) administered by the POSCO TJ Park Foundation
scholarships.name: POSCO TJ Park Foundation Global Scholarship

scholarships.title: ETH Zurich Excellence Scholarship & Opportunity Programme (ESOP)
scholarships.description: ETH Zurich's ESOP supports excellent Master's students with a scholarship, mentorship and a network of the ETH Foundation. The page states that the scholarship covers the full study and living costs during the Master's degree course, and that the award consists of a scholarship covering living and study expenses of CHF 12'000 per semester (13'500 CHF per semester from HS27 onwards) plus a tuition fee waiver. The scholarship and the waiver are both awarded for the regular duration of the Master's programme (three or four semesters). Approximately 60 ESOP scholarships are assigned for the 2027/28 academic year, and the exact number depends on the availability of funds.
eligibility: Very good result in Bachelor’s degree programme (top 10% of Bachelor’s degree programme = grade A; this is based on self-assessment)
For an ESOP Scholarship you must apply within the first application window (November 1 - 30)
The next application window is the first window, Nov 1 - Nov 30 2026, for a start in the Master programme in HS27
This also applies for ETH Bachelor students for a consecutive Master programme
benefits: CHF 12,000 per semester for living and study expenses
Full tuition fee waiver for regular program duration (3–4 semesters)
requirements: Submit the ESOP application via eApply (the online Master application)
Upload a pre-proposal for the Master thesis in addition to the documents for the Master admission (guidelines published as PDF, 86 KB)
The pre-proposal for the Master’s thesis must be developed by yourself and use established scientific citation practice
Please make sure to be reachable under the telephone number specified in your CV as the selection process might include a phone/VC interview in February
If you are not available during that time, please inform the study programme coordinator

If your study programme does not ask for references you must name two reference persons (professors) for your ESOP application; these persons should upload (after an email from the system) a reference letter
Plagiarism, negligent or intentional misinformation will lead to exclusion from the admission process or - if discovered later - to the revocation of the admission and of any scholarship
scholarships.duration: Regular duration of the Master's programme (three or four semesters)
scholarships.application_period: Applications open 1 November 2026 and close 30 November 2026 (11:59 MEZ as published in the headline; 12.59 MEZ in the section body). Decisions are communicated at the end of March for a start in the Master's programme in HS27.
scholarships.selection_notes: The applications are evaluated by the Admissions Committees of the respective Master’s programmes. The final decision for awarding scholarships in the Excellence Scholarship & Opportunity Programme rests with the Rector of ETH Zurich. The exact number of annual scholarships depends on the availability of funds. The holistic evaluation of a Master application takes into account the performance in the undergraduate programme, the ranking of the university, the background in the chosen field of study, the scores in standardized tests (like GRE, if required), the letter of motivation and the letters of recommendation. The selection process might include a phone/VC interview in February.

Selection weighs remarkable academic results together with extracurricular achievements in research, entrepreneurship, sport, arts or civic activity. scholarships.title: Erasmus+ Student Exchange (Studying Abroad)
scholarships.description: Erasmus+ helps organise student and doctoral candidate exchanges within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from countries associated to Erasmus+. It is open to short-cycle, Bachelor's and Master's students and to doctoral candidates registered at a participating higher education institution and enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree. There is no central application form: students apply through the international or Erasmus+ office of their own institution, which selects applicants fairly and transparently. The grant contributes to travel and daily living costs with amounts varying by destination and demand, and Erasmus+ students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory or library fees at the receiving institution. Mobilities run from 2 to 12 months for long-term study, or 5 to 30 days for short-term blended mobility, with up to 12 months in total per study cycle.
scholarships.deadline: Varies by university (typically 1–3 months before departure)
scholarships.deadline_display: Varies by university (typically 1–3 months before departure)
eligibility: Student at short-cycle, Bachelor's or Master's level, or a doctoral candidate
Registered at a higher education institution that participates in the Erasmus+ programme and holds an Erasmus Charter for Higher Education
Enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree or tertiary-level qualification
The study period abroad must be relevant for degree-related learning and personal development needs
The study period abroad must be part of the study programme the student is following
The sending and receiving institutions must have an inter-institutional agreement, and both must hold the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education where applicable
benefits: Tuition fees waived at host institution
Monthly living grant (amount varies by country)
Additional support for students with disabilities
scholarships.duration: Long-term mobility: minimum 2 months to maximum 12 months abroad, including blended mobilities with a virtual component. Short-term mobility: 5 to 30 days abroad, which must be blended mobilities; only doctoral candidates can do a short-term mobility without a virtual component. Maximum total duration is 12 months within one study cycle, with more than one exchange possible within that limit. For one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture, up to 24 months.
scholarships.application_period: Year-round through the sending institution, which publishes its own Erasmus+ selection deadlines for each academic year.
scholarships.program_type: EU exchange and mobility programme (Erasmus+ Key Action 1), funded by the European Commission
scholarships.name: Erasmus+ Student Exchange (Studying Abroad)

scholarships.title: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Networks
scholarships.description: MSCA Doctoral Networks implement doctoral programmes through international, intersectoral partnerships of universities, research institutions, businesses including SMEs and other socio-economic actors, in order to train highly skilled doctoral candidates. Besides standard Doctoral Networks, the action promotes Industrial Doctorates, which place PhD candidates largely outside academia, and Joint Doctorates, which lead to a joint or multiple doctoral degrees. Each beneficiary must recruit at least one doctoral candidate, who must not already hold a doctoral degree at recruitment, may be of any nationality and is funded through a living allowance, mobility allowance and applicable family, long-term leave and special needs allowances. The 2026 call is currently open, having launched on 28 May 2026 with a deadline of 24 November 2026.
eligibility: For the applicant consortium: at least three independent legal entities, each in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, with at least one in an EU Member State
Additional partner organisations from any country in the world may join the consortium

For the recruited researcher: any nationality
For the recruited researcher: must be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project
For Industrial Doctorates: at least 50% of time outside academia
For the recruited researcher: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in the recruiting organisation's country in the 36 months immediately before recruitment
Each beneficiary must recruit at least one doctoral candidate
benefits: Gross salary (approx. EUR 4,000-5,000/month depending on country and experience)
scholarships.duration: Doctoral Networks can last up to 4 years, up to 5 years for Joint Doctorate projects. Each individual fellowship is between 3 and 36 months, or 3 to 48 months for Joint Doctorate fellowships.
scholarships.application_period: Call opens May, deadline November annually
scholarships.program_type: EU doctoral training programme under Horizon Europe (MSCA Doctoral Networks), administered by the European Research Executive Agency
scholarships.name: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Networks

scholarships.title: France Excellence Europa Scholarship
scholarships.description: The France Excellence Europa scholarship programme, developed by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and managed by Campus France, lets students from 26 EU Member States study at Master's level at a French higher education institution. It pays a semi-annual maintenance allowance of EUR 6,850 and a one-off installation allowance of EUR 1,700, exempts holders from administrative registration fees for a national degree in public institutions and from the CVEC, and arranges social protection and complementary health insurance. The award lasts up to 12 months for a Master 2 enrolment and up to 24 months for a Master 1 enrolment, and applications are sent electronically to the French Embassy in the applicant's country of nationality.

scholarships.title: France Excellence Major Scholarship
scholarships.description: France Excellence-Major is a French government scholarship run by AEFE for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs that supports the best non-French baccalaureat holders from the network of French schools abroad to continue their higher education in France. Around 800 foreign students are supported at any one time over five years of study, and about 200 new holders join each year. Applications require pre-selection by the head of the French school abroad and online entry on the dedicated Cascade application, followed by assessment by the French embassy's cultural cooperation service and a selection commission convened by AEFE each May. Selection weighs school results, a coherent orientation project, involvement in school life and extracurricular activity, and motivation for demanding French higher education. Holders receive a family-need-rated monthly allowance of EUR 280 or EUR 860, complementary health cover, and, at the higher rates, round-trip travel and CROUS housing.

scholarships.title: Humboldt Research Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.
scholarships.deadline: Three calls annually: March 15, July 15, November 15 (2026 schedule)
scholarships.deadline_display: Three calls annually: March 15, July 15, November 15 (2026 schedule)
eligibility: Postdocs: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last four years?
Experienced researchers: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last twelve years?
Postdocs: have you been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards?

Experienced researchers: is your academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and do you hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)?

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. If you are a German national, or if you obtained your university entrance qualification and university degree, or your university degree and your doctorate, in Germany, you can apply if you have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term. Have you lived and worked abroad for more than five years? You can still apply if there is a strong connection to your current country of residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship etc.).
For your application to be successful, you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.

A researcher from an academic institution of your choice in Germany will provide you with a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and will compile a detailed review for you.

You can provide two expert reviews. For postdocs: your doctoral supervisor and one other researcher - outside of your institute, if possible. For experienced researchers: important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute as well as other institutes - outside your country of origin, if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice.
You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).
benefits: Monthly fellowship amount EUR 3,000 (postdocs) or EUR 3,600 (experienced researchers)
Family allowance for accompanying spouse/children under certain circumstances
requirements: Submit the necessary documents to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation online only
You may only submit your application once you have uploaded all required documents in the application form
Two expert reviews must be uploaded in a protected area by the expert reviewers personally; you can only submit once these have been uploaded if the portal is open at that time
Your host will receive a link to upload a host's statement and mentoring agreement; the application is only forwarded to the Foundation once the host has uploaded all necessary documents
Applications that fail to include important documents or information, or that diverge substantially from the specifications, will be formally rejected without further review
scholarships.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months, divided into up to three stays within three years. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months, divided into up to three stays within three years.
scholarships.application_period: Three selection rounds per year (March, July, November)
scholarships.selection_notes: The decision to award research fellowships is taken by a selection committee consisting of 60-70 researchers from various fields. Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.

scholarships.title: Pearson International Scholarship (University of Toronto)
scholarships.description: The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is the University of Toronto's most prestigious award for international students and one of the largest scholarship programmes for international students in Canada. It covers tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years and is tenable only at the University of Toronto for first-entry undergraduate programmes. Around 37 scholars are named each year from a pool representing 188 countries, with more than CAD 12 million of funding in 2024. Candidates must be nominated by their secondary school, which can nominate only one student per year, and must also apply for admission to the University of Toronto through the Ontario Universities' Application Centre. The scholarship is restricted to the applicant's top-choice programme at the time scholarship decisions are made.

scholarships.title: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program
scholarships.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is a U.S. Department of State fellowship, administered by the Institute of International Education, for mid-career professionals from eligible countries. It is a non-degree program: fellows may take academic coursework at a U.S. host university but do not earn a degree. The package covers host-university tuition and fees, a maintenance allowance with a one-time settling-in allowance, accident and sickness insurance, a book allowance, a one-time computer subsidy, international and programme-event air travel, and a professional development allowance. Applications go through each applicant's Binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section, so deadlines vary by country and nominations must reach IIE by mid-September.

scholarships.description: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) funds up to four years of PhD or EngD study at an autonomous university in Singapore, jointly supervised by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member, with research conducted at an A*STAR Research Institute. Support published for up to 4 years comprises full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment. Monthly allowance is a published matrix by track and residency status: AGS (STEM) $4,500 for Singapore Citizens, $4,100 for Singapore Permanent Residents and $3,600 for International Students; AGS (Specialised Tracks: Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing) $6,200, $5,600 and $5,000 respectively.

There will be at least 2 rounds of interviews involving the senior management of the Biomedical Research Council or Science & Engineering Research Council, and researchers from A*STAR's Research Entities. The nomination of supervisor(s) has to be approved by A*STAR; in most cases the main and co-supervisors should hold at least the designation of Principal Investigator or Principal Scientist at an A*STAR RI. Final approval of the PhD supervisor(s), research project and university for successful applicants is subject to A*STAR's approval. A*STAR makes a holistic assessment of each application and takes into consideration factors such as achievements in science/maths related competitions and CCAs; prior research experience helps but is not mandatory. The application process typically takes about 5 months from submission of a complete application to notification of results.

scholarships.title: NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: The NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship is a University-level scholarship offered by the National University of Singapore to support exceptional students from all countries except Singapore who apply as freshmen to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS. Candidates are considered and shortlisted through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS, and selection interviews are held from January to July with outcomes notified by mid-July. It is described as the premier scholarship granted by NTU's President, recognising PhD students who exemplify exceptional academic, research and leadership qualities. Open to all nationalities, it requires an Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent at Bachelor's level, or official documentation confirming the candidate is on track to achieve it.
