scholarships.selection_notes: The admissions process is holistic, weighing the completed application, official academic records, test scores where submitted, financial eligibility, recommendations and endorsements, conversations with an admissions counsellor, extracurricular and co-curricular activity, community service, character and personal qualities, and demonstrated interest in the College. Admitted students average a 3.65 high school GPA and qualify for federal Pell Grants, and Berea is academically competitive with an average ACT of about 25 and more than half of first-year students ranked in the top fifth of their high school class. Well qualified applicants may be accepted for fall admission as early as December, though an early application alone does not ensure admission.
scholarships.program_type: Need-aware tuition promise awarded to all admitted students, not a competitive merit scholarship
scholarships.name: Berea College Tuition Promise Scholarship

scholarships.title: Karsh International Scholars Program — Duke University
scholarships.description: The Karsh International Scholarship was founded at Duke University in 2010 through a donation from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh. It brings together a cohort of international undergraduates who promote interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research and scholarship in the service of society. International applicants must have demonstrated financial need to be eligible. The award covers tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need beyond those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships and other career-advancing opportunities. There is no separate application: candidates apply to Duke University and request financial aid.
eligibility: Citizen of a country outside the United States
Not a dual U.S./other-country citizen
Does not already hold a B.A. or B.S. degree
Demonstrated financial need for financial aid
Strong academic preparation
Must apply to Duke University; there is no separate application and nominations are not accepted
requirements: Submit the Duke University application
Complete the Duke financial aid forms
Demonstrate financial need
scholarships.application_period: Tied to Duke University's undergraduate admission cycle; the programme page publishes no separate window.
scholarships.selection_notes: Strong academic preparation and documented need for financial aid are the stated selection criteria; there is no separate scholarship application, essay or nomination route.
scholarships.program_type: Merit and need-based university scholarship for international undergraduates, awarded by Duke University's Office of University Scholars and Fellows
scholarships.name: Karsh International Scholars Program — Duke University

scholarships.title: Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program — Boston College
scholarships.description: The Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program is Boston College's premier undergraduate academic merit programme. Each year it awards full-tuition scholarships together with fully-funded, programme-sponsored summer programmes to 18 incoming freshmen. Scholars enrol in a University departmental honours programme and take part in summer experiences in service learning, international study and professional internships. There is no separate application: Early Decision and Regular Decision candidates who file their BC application by the November 1 priority scholarship deadline are considered.
eligibility: Applying for fall admission to Boston College
Submitting an Early Decision or Regular Decision application by the November 1 priority scholarship deadline
Academic excellence, demonstrated leadership ability and significant community service (programme history)
benefits: Fully-funded summer programs (international travel, service learning, internships)
requirements: In addition to the Common Application, Boston College requires that you also submit the following materials:
Enrolled students will be required to submit official test score reports for all self-reported scores upon matriculation. At that time, students' results will be verified.
scholarships.duration: Are there activities for Scholars during the summer months?
scholarships.application_period: Considered only for fall admission; applications must be submitted by the November 1 priority scholarship deadline.
scholarships.selection_notes: No separate application; only candidates for fall admission are considered, and consideration follows submission of the BC application by the November 1 priority scholarship deadline.
scholarships.program_type: Undergraduate academic merit scholarship with an honours programme and funded summer experience
scholarships.name: Gabelli Presidential Scholars Program — Boston College

scholarships.title: Harvard University Financial Aid (International)
scholarships.description: The Griffin Financial Aid Office at Harvard College provides need-based aid that allows Harvard to bring the best students regardless of their ability to pay. Financial aid is available to foreign students on exactly the same basis as for American students; because international students are not eligible for federal funding, the College applies its own job and scholarship money. For families with income of $100,000 or below and typical assets, aid covers all billed expenses including tuition, fees, food, housing, health insurance if needed, travel between campus and home, and $2,000 start-up and launch grants. Families with income up to $200,000 receive free tuition plus aid for additional costs. Aid is need-blind with respect to admission.
eligibility: Any applicant or admitted Harvard College student, regardless of country of residence or citizenship status
International students are eligible on the same basis as American students
Admitted students may apply for aid; Harvard states it cannot track aid materials for prospective students until admission
Current students reapply each academic year
requirements: Apply for financial aid at the same time as applying for admission
Provide information about family income and assets, outside awards and any unusual or changed financial circumstances
File the CSS Profile; international families may use the alternate paper process in exceptional circumstances
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle tied to Harvard's Restrictive Early Action (November 1), Regular Decision (February 1) and Transfer (March 1) admission rounds; current students reapply by May 1.
scholarships.selection_notes: All Harvard financial aid is awarded on the basis of demonstrated need; there are no academic, athletic or merit-based awards. Applying for aid does not affect admission chances.
scholarships.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid programme (not a merit scholarship)
scholarships.name: Harvard University Financial Aid (International)

scholarships.title: Princeton University Financial Aid (International)
scholarships.description: Princeton University operates a strictly need-based financial aid programme that it applies identically to international and domestic students. The full need of every admitted international student is met with grant aid, and Princeton's admission process is need-blind, so applying for aid carries no admission disadvantage. Since 2001 Princeton has replaced student loans with grants in the aid package, so no student is required to borrow. Aid covers tuition, room, board and other assessed costs of attendance. The Princeton Financial Aid Application is due November 9 for single-choice early action and February 1 for regular decision.
eligibility: Admitted Princeton undergraduate student, international or domestic
Same financial aid policy regardless of citizenship, citizenship status or ability to pay
Must complete the Princeton Financial Aid Application to be considered
Princeton does not offer academic or athletic merit scholarships
requirements: Submit the Common Application with Princeton-specific Questions
Submit the Princeton Financial Aid Application by Nov. 9 (single-choice early action) or Feb. 1 (regular decision)
Submit the Graded Written Paper in English
Submit an English proficiency test if applicable
Have school officials complete the School Report, School Counselor Letter and Final Report
Provide two teacher evaluations
Officially translate any non-English recommendation or school report
scholarships.duration: Four years of English (including continued practice in writing).
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. Single-choice early action application Nov. 1 with the financial aid application due Nov. 9; regular decision application Jan. 1 with the financial aid application due Feb. 1. Applications open in mid-August.
scholarships.selection_notes: Financial aid is awarded on demonstrated need only. Princeton states that if an applicant is admitted and has completed the Princeton Financial Aid Application, they will be notified of any aid award at the time admission is offered.
scholarships.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid programme (grant aid), not a merit scholarship
scholarships.name: Princeton University Financial Aid (International)

scholarships.title: Brown University Financial Aid (International)
scholarships.description: Brown University confirms that international students are eligible to apply for University financial aid and that it meets full demonstrated need for admitted students who apply for aid at the time they apply for admission. Aid is entirely need-based and Brown offers no merit awards. Through The Brown Promise, Brown has replaced all packaged loans in all undergraduate aid packages with scholarships. Brown will be need-blind for international students beginning with the Class of 2029. Aid is normally credited directly to the student account against tuition, fees, room and meals, and also helps with travel, books and personal expenses, but not with vacation and summer expenses. Financial aid documents are due November 2, 2026 for Early Decision and February 1, 2027 for Regular Decision.
eligibility: International student applying for admission to Brown
Must apply for financial aid at the time they apply for admission
No academic merit awards exist at Brown
Transfer students' financial need is considered in admission decisions
requirements: Indicate on the admission application that you are applying for financial aid
Submit the CSS Profile by the applicable deadline
Submit the FAFSA by the applicable deadline if a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
Provide supporting income tax forms if prompted
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. Early Decision financial aid documents due November 2, 2026; Regular Decision financial aid documents due February 1, 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: All Brown financial aid is need-based; the University does not offer merit awards. If aid is applied for and the steps are completed by their deadlines, Brown includes financial aid award details with the admission decision.
scholarships.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid, international applicants
scholarships.name: Brown University Financial Aid (International)

scholarships.title: Dartmouth College Financial Aid (International)
scholarships.description: Dartmouth College meets 100% of the demonstrated need of all admitted financial aid applicants, regardless of citizenship or entry round, and its financial aid packages never include a required student loan. Need is calculated as cost of attendance minus family contribution, with direct expenses of tuition, fees, food and housing and indirect expenses such as travel, books, supplies and laundry. Families with total annual income below $125,000 with typical assets can expect no parent contribution, while families earning between $125,000 and $175,000 with typical assets can expect a scholarship or grants covering the full cost of tuition. International applicants file the CSS Profile with school code 3351, or the International Student Financial Aid Application if the CSS fee is a serious hardship. Financial aid deadlines are November 1 for Early Decision and February 1 for Regular Decision.
eligibility: Admitted Dartmouth undergraduate student, international or domestic
Policy applies to all students regardless of citizenship or entry round
International applicants may use the ISFAA instead of the CSS Profile without changing eligibility
No income cut-off for scholarship consideration at Dartmouth
requirements: Submit the CSS Profile by the financial aid deadline, or the ISFAA where the CSS fee is a hardship
Submit parents' income tax statements in English, keeping amounts in home currency rather than converting to USD
Submit the FAFSA if a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
Meet the expected student contribution, part of which comes from leave-term earnings of roughly $1,000 to $2,500 per year
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. Financial aid materials due November 1 for Early Decision and February 1 for Regular Decision.
scholarships.selection_notes: Once the Admissions office has selected students to admit, the Financial Aid Office determines each student's need and awards aid accordingly, so financial need plays no part in the admission decision for admitted students. Aid is evaluated individually and annually.
scholarships.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid programme
scholarships.name: Dartmouth College Financial Aid (International)

scholarships.title: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme
eligibility: have excellent academic records;
hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent training/professional experience;
demonstrate genuine financial need;
demonstrate a thoughtful, reliable, multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study;
be admitted to a reputable postgraduate institution;
be starting the first year of the programme; and
have strong leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular and/or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Note: preference is given to young professionals under 30 years of age.

The programme is available in Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, and Uganda. In countries such as Canada, Portugal and the USA, applications are accepted from those who are originally from one of the countries listed above. At this time, AKF ISP is not available to students who wish to study in the United Kingdom or Russia.
benefits: Tuition and living expenses (50% grant, 50% zero-interest loan)
requirements: Awards are provided according to need, but the AKF ISP should be considered a resource of last resort; applicants should secure multiple sources of funding to reduce the amount requested.
Applicants must be entering their first year of study in a postgraduate programme. Students who have already enrolled in, or have commenced their postgraduate studies, are not eligible.
Applications for part-time programmes and short-term courses are not considered.
A guarantor is required to co-sign the award agreement.

Repayment of the loan component, which includes a service charge, begins six months after the first of the following events: a) graduation, b) termination of studies, or c) withdrawal of support following failure to meet the academic standards expected of ISP students.
To maintain an AKF ISP award, the award holder must demonstrate good academic standing as well as ongoing financial need during the course of the postgraduate programme.
scholarships.duration: Master's scholarships are granted for the entire duration of the degree course; PhD scholarships are awarded for the first two years
scholarships.application_period: The 2026-2027 cycle is closed. The next cycle opens in early 2027; the programme is run through a global, annual and competitive application process, with applications handled by contacts in countries where AKF ISP is available.
scholarships.selection_notes: Award recipients are selected through a global, annual and competitive application process. The AKF ISP offers a limited number of new awards in each cycle. The published criteria are academic record, financial need, quality of the funding plan, quality of the admitting institution, first-year status, and leadership and achievement profile, with preference given to young professionals under 30.
scholarships.program_type: Private foundation scholarship (partly repayable)
scholarships.name: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme

scholarships.title: Rotary Peace Fellowships
scholarships.description: The Rotary Peace Fellowship is funded by The Rotary Foundation and awards up to 170 fellowships a year for leaders with work experience in peace and development to study at one of eight Rotary Peace Centers. Each year up to 50 fellowships fund master's degrees and up to 120 fund professional development certificate studies at partner universities. Fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses. Master's programmes run 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study, while the certificate programme is a one-year blended learning course for working professionals that includes field studies and a social change initiative. Fellowships cannot be used for doctoral study. Applications open in February and the global deadline is 15 May; the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the 2028-29 cycle opens in February 2027.
eligibility: Work experience in peace and development
Commitment to community and international service and the pursuit of peace
Not pursuing doctoral study
Not a spouse, lineal descendant, spouse of a lineal descendant, or parent or grandparent by blood of a living Rotary member in those categories
Not a former Rotary member, or a relative as described, within 36 months of that member's resignation
Rotaract club members who are not also Rotary club members are eligible to apply
Must wait three years between the end of a Rotary Peace Centers certificate or master's programme, or a Global Grant Scholarship, and the intended fellowship start date
requirements: Submit an online application to The Rotary Foundation by 15 May
Submit all materials in English
Demonstrate work experience in peace and development
Obtain a club or district recommendation where available
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. Applications open in February and close 15 May; the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the 2028-29 cycle opens in February 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Rotary members and clubs are central to recruiting candidates. Clubs and districts are not required to fund candidates. Applications are reviewed by Rotary Peace Centers staff and all qualified applications move forward for further consideration.
scholarships.program_type: Fully funded postgraduate fellowship in peace and development studies
scholarships.name: Rotary Peace Fellowships

scholarships.title: University of Bologna — International Talents @Unibo
scholarships.description: The University of Bologna awards 30 International Talents @unibo study grants each year to international students who matriculate for the first time in the first year of a Second Cycle (Laurea Magistrale) degree programme. Each grant is worth EUR 6,500 gross per academic year and is awarded for two academic years, and successful applicants also receive a full tuition fee waiver, paying only EUR 157.04 in regional taxes, stamp duty and insurance premium. Selection is based on GRE General Test scores, with minimum scores of 290 in the combined Verbal and Quantitative Reasoning sections and 3.0 in Analytical Writing, together with a family economic situation within an ISEE band of EUR 16,000 to EUR 35,000. Applicants must be under 30 years old at the deadline and must not already be a student of the University of Bologna.
scholarships.deadline: 30 May 2025 (for A.Y. 2025/26; check site for updated 2026/27 call)
scholarships.deadline_display: 30 May 2025 (for A.Y. 2025/26; check site for updated 2026/27 call)
eligibility: Holds a qualification valid for admission to the chosen Second cycle degree programme, awarded by an institution outside the Italian education system (San Marino qualifications do not qualify); citizenship is irrelevant
Is not, and has never been enrolled as, a student of a First, Single or Second cycle degree programme at the University of Bologna, including a career closed after A.Y. 2023-24
Has an ISEE (Equivalent Economic Situation Indicator) between EUR 16,000 and EUR 35,000, or an equivalent economic situation certificate
Has not previously applied for and received an Unibo Action 2 study grant
Is less than 30 years old at the application deadline
Matriculates for the first time in the first year of the degree programme; later enrolments, course changes and transfers do not count
Is not enrolling in a multiple or joint degree programme where fees are paid to a partner university other than Bologna
benefits: Renewable for a second academic year
requirements: Applications are submitted exclusively through Studenti Online (studenti.unibo.it); paper, fax and email applications are not accepted
International students without an Italian tax code must register through the 'International students registration' section of studenti.unibo.it
Personal details registered must match the passport or identity document exactly, and the PUK code must be replaced with a personal password
The official GRE score report must reach the University through ETS by the deadline; later scores are not accepted
All uploaded documents must be in PDF format
The 30 October-style application status messages displayed in the portal do not mean the application is complete or eligible
scholarships.duration: Two academic years (a standard Second Cycle degree programme)
scholarships.application_period: Annual call, opening in mid-January and closing at 12:00 CEST in late May (17 January 2025 12:00 CET to 30 May 2025 12:00 CEST for the 2025/26 edition); results published in July
scholarships.selection_notes: Grants are ranked on the summed GRE General Test score, with equal weight to each section; applicants below the minimum scores are excluded. Ties are resolved in favour of the younger candidate. Results are published by a managerial decree on studenti.unibo.it. Winners must send an unconditional acceptance declaration to internationaldesk@unibo.it within 10 days of the award notification.
scholarships.program_type: University merit and needs-based study grant for international students matriculating in a Second Cycle (Master's) degree programme
scholarships.image_alt_text: Alma Mater Studiorum – Università di Bologna
scholarships.name: University of Bologna — International Talents @Unibo

scholarships.title: Politecnico di Milano — Merit Based International Scholarships
scholarships.description: Politecnico di Milano runs an annual merit-based scholarship scheme for international candidates applying to the first year of an English-taught Master of Science programme. The 2027/2028 call offers 64 awards: 10 Platinum (Milan), 18 Gold (Milan), 16 Gold Piacenza Campus, 10 Bronze Piacenza Campus and 10 Silver scholarships for the Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza campuses. Every award includes a full tuition-fee waiver for the academic year, and the cash tiers add a gross allowance of EUR 10,000 (Platinum), EUR 8,000 (Gold), EUR 5,000 (Gold Piacenza) or EUR 2,500 (Bronze); the Silver tier is a waiver only. Recipients must pay a non-refundable administrative fee of about EUR 170 on acceptance, and the awards can be renewed for a second year on academic points.
eligibility: International student (foreign citizenship plus a qualification obtained abroad) applying to the first year of a Master of Science programme taught in English
Must have submitted the admission application and paid the application fee in the Early Bird period, between 1 October 2026 and 1 December 2026
Must be admitted to the chosen study programme and accept the positive evaluation outcome
Must submit a valid certificate of English language proficiency by 4 March 2027

Must choose a programme and campus matching the tier applied for (Milan Leonardo or Milano Bovisa for Platinum and Gold; Piacenza for Gold and Bronze Piacenza; Cremona, Lecco, Mantova or Piacenza for Silver)
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver + cash allowance
Renewable for the following academic year based on academic merit
requirements: The application must be submitted through Politecnico di Milano Online Services at the path Benefits and Agreements > Economic benefits > Scholarships for International Master of Science Students
Only candidates who have already applied for admission to the MSc programme may participate in the call
The admission application fee must have been paid in the Early Bird window from 1 October to 1 December 2026
The candidate must pay an administrative fee of approximately EUR 170 by the deadline in the assignation email, or the scholarship is treated as not accepted
The candidate must enrol in the academic year the scholarship was assigned for, by the deadlines set by the Student Affairs Unit

Payment requires an IBAN linked to an Italian bank account, or a prepaid card linked to an Italian or SEPA account, headed only to the student and with a credit limit at least equal to the scholarship amount
scholarships.duration: One academic year, renewable for a second year on academic points
scholarships.application_period: Applications open 1 October 2026 and close at 12:00 noon Italian time on 15 December 2026, for admission application and scholarship for academic year 2027/2028. Eligibility is restricted to candidates who paid the admission application fee during the Early Bird period from 1 October to 1 December 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: Scholarships are assigned by a Commission nominated through an Executive Decree of the Head of the Campus Life Area, including the Vice Rector for International Relations and the Heads of Schools or their delegates. To be considered, students must be admitted to the programme and accept the outcome. The Commission takes into account gender equality, country of origin and age, prioritising the youngest candidates where requirements are equivalent. The published assignment criteria on the scholarships page state that selection is based on the evaluation of previous education and its match with the programme requirements, the documents provided at application and the scholarship form, with GPA and academic achievements (including the portfolio where requested) of utmost importance.
scholarships.program_type: University merit-based scholarship scheme for international Master of Science applicants, with Platinum, Gold, Bronze and Silver tiers plus partner-funded awards
scholarships.name: Politecnico di Milano — Merit Based International Scholarships

scholarships.title: University of Padua — Padua International Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.description: The University of Padua awards up to 76 Padua International Excellence Scholarships each year to the most deserving international candidate on each degree programme delivered entirely in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus full exemption from student fees, leaving only the regional right-to-education tax and the revenue stamp payable. There is no separate scholarship application: applying to an eligible English-taught degree programme by its admission deadline makes the candidate eligible automatically. Selection is made by the Teaching Committee of each degree programme on academic excellence and the quality of the candidate's prior academic record, with the youngest candidate preferred in a tie.
scholarships.deadline: Aligned with each programme's admission call (typically November 2025 – May 2026 for 2026/27 intake)
scholarships.deadline_display: Aligned with each programme's admission call (typically November 2025 – May 2026 for 2026/27 intake)
eligibility: Does not hold Italian citizenship, unless the candidate holds dual citizenship
Holds a non-Italian secondary school diploma (bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes) or a foreign degree diploma (master's degree programmes)
Is not resident in Italy at the time of application
Applies for admission to an English-taught degree programme at the University of Padua within the deadline set by that programme
Does not receive other scholarships or grants, which is a condition of receiving and keeping this award
Completes enrolment at the University of Padua
benefits: €8,000 per academic year (gross, paid in two €4,000 instalments)
Up to 3 years for Bachelor's/Single-Cycle, up to 2 years for Master's
requirements: Apply for admission to an eligible English-taught degree programme by that programme's deadline; there is no separate scholarship application
Accept both the admission offer and the scholarship offer, and pay the admission fee by the stated deadline
Meet the admission requirements, including obtaining the entry qualification, within the deadline in the admission offer
For non-EU candidates residing abroad, meet the requirements and conditions for an Italian student visa (D) for enrolment
Complete enrolment in the chosen degree programme, which is finalised after checks on the authenticity of the required documents
Hold an online bank account or prepaid card with an IBAN in an Italian or SEPA bank, in the student's own or joint name
Sign the Declaration of acceptance confirming the scholarship conditions and the absence of any incompatibility

Arrive in Padua by 15 December 2026 to receive the first instalment of the 2026/2027 award (30 November 2026 for awards funded by the Department of Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering; this earlier date does not apply to awards from the Department of Industrial Engineering or the Department of Land, Environment, Agriculture and Forestry)
scholarships.duration: 2 years for master's degree programmes; 3 years for bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes
scholarships.application_period: Aligned with each degree programme's admission call. For the 2026/2027 cycle the official call set first application periods of 2 November 2025 to 2 February 2026 for unlimited-access programmes and 7 January to 7 March 2026 for limited-access programmes, with scholarship results published from 11 March 2026 and 10 April 2026 respectively. The 2027/2028 call is due in November 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: The Teaching Committee of each degree programme shortlists eligible applicants and awards the scholarship to the most deserving candidates on the basis of academic excellence in their field of study and the quality and results of their prior academic career. In case of equal scores the youngest candidate is given priority. Scholarships are mainly reserved for candidates applying in the first application period and may be awarded to second-period candidates only on an exceptional basis. Results are published on the University website on the dates set out in the Admission Notice.
scholarships.program_type: University merit scholarship for international students enrolling in a completely English-taught degree programme: 2 years for master's degree programmes, 3 years for bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes
scholarships.name: University of Padua — Padua International Excellence Scholarship

scholarships.title: University of Trento — International Student Scholarships
scholarships.description: The University of Trento awards a limited number of merit scholarships to citizens of countries outside the European Union who live outside Italy and enrol in a degree programme, based on their admission score and programme of study. The scholarship is worth EUR 7,200 per year, or EUR 8,500 per year for female students enrolled in STEM programmes, and scholarship holders are also exempted from paying tuition fees for that year. It is paid in two instalments, the second conditional on earning at least half of the credits required by the course in the January and February exam sessions. The award lasts a maximum of two years on a master's programme and three years on an undergraduate programme.
eligibility: Citizen of a country outside the European Union
Living outside Italy at the time of application
Applying through the admission call for non-European candidates residing abroad for a University of Trento degree programme
Ranking high enough in the admission selection, since scholarships are limited in number and assigned on the admission score
requirements: Apply through the admission call for non-European candidates residing abroad for the specific degree programme; no separate scholarship application exists
Pay the EUR 30.00 application fee for the admission application
Earn at least 50% of the credits required by the course in the January and February exam sessions to receive the second instalment on time
Alternatively, obtain 42 ECTS credits (36 on Italian-taught courses) by 10 August to have the second instalment paid in October
Hold an Italian or SEPA bank account or other arrangement required for the University to credit the instalments
scholarships.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme; up to 3 years for an undergraduate programme
scholarships.application_period: Tied to each degree programme's annual admission call for non-European candidates residing abroad. For the 2026/2027 cycle published deadlines included 4 March 2026 at 12:00 CET on several English-taught master's programmes and 23 March 2026 on others, each with a EUR 30.00 application fee.
scholarships.selection_notes: The selection is competitive: the University states scholarships are limited in number and based on the admission score obtained, and candidates do not need to apply separately for the scholarship. Ranking lists with admitted candidates and scholarship assignation are published by each degree programme. In September the University checks the credits earned by 10 August and confirms or does not confirm the scholarship for the following academic year; candidates who fall short must return part of the scholarship and pay tuition fees for the following year according to the published credit table.
scholarships.program_type: University merit scholarship awarded through the degree programme admission ranking, with a tuition-fee exemption; renewable on credit milestones
scholarships.name: University of Trento — International Student Scholarships

scholarships.title: University of Milano-Bicocca — BISP (Bicocca International Scholarship Programme)
scholarships.description: The Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) is a merit award from the University of Milano-Bicocca for international students who hold a foreign qualification, are not resident in Italy and are admitted to one of the University's English-taught degree programmes. Around 100 scholarships are awarded each year, with five dedicated to each eligible English-taught course, mainly at Master's level. Each scholarship is worth EUR 10,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from tuition fees, and is renewable for a maximum of three years on Bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes and two years on Master's degree programmes. No separate application is needed: applying to an eligible programme makes the candidate automatically part of the selection, and applicants are not required to submit any further form.
scholarships.deadline: Admission must be confirmed by 15 March 2026
scholarships.deadline_display: Admission must be confirmed by 15 March 2026
eligibility: Holds a non-Italian entry qualification that allows admission to the Italian university system for the desired course
Does not possess Italian citizenship, except dual citizenship that includes Italian
Obtained the previous degree abroad
Is not resident in Italy
Is admitted to one of the degree programmes specified in the call; the admission offer counts as accepted once the deposit has been received
benefits: Renewable up to 3 years (Bachelor's/Single-Cycle) or 2 years (Master's)
requirements: Apply to an eligible English-taught programme; no separate scholarship application form is required
Be admitted and confirm the admission offer by the programme's deadline, with 15 March 2026 being the key date for free entrance courses in the 2026/2027 call
For limited-access programmes, complete all the admission steps required by the programme
Officially accept the scholarship offer by the deadline given
Confirm that the candidate is not a beneficiary of any other scholarships
Fulfil the enrolment requirements within the given deadline
For non-EU students, meet the requirements for an Italian student visa (D) for enrolment
Complete enrolment in the selected degree programme following checks on document authenticity and enrolment eligibility
Arrive in Milan by 31 October 2026 for the 2026/2027 award, otherwise the first instalment is not paid
scholarships.duration: Up to 3 years for Bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes; up to 2 years for Master's degree programmes
scholarships.application_period: Aligned with each degree programme's admission calls, referred to on the apply.unimib.it website. For 2026/2027 the key milestone was confirmation of admission by 15 March 2026 for free entrance courses, with a second session reflected in a further ranking decree on 15 July 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: Five scholarships are assigned to the best candidates on each eligible course, and the number may be increased at the discretion of the awarding body if additional funds become available. Selection results are published on apply.unimib.it by mid-April for free-access study programmes and following the publication of the admission ranking list for limited-access programmes. If a candidate withdraws, the Commission proceeds down the ranking and the next eligible candidate is notified through the Dream Apply messaging section. Priority is given to candidates who applied in the first Call for Admission.
scholarships.program_type: University merit scholarship for international students enrolling in English-taught degree programmes, awarded automatically through the admission ranking

It combines a cash stipend with services and supplements, including a free daily meal valued at EUR 829.00 for a.y. 2026-27, access to preferential-rate canteen services and a 200-hour work-study programme. Eligibility depends on three separate tests: enrolment for the absolute first year, an economic test set annually by the Lombardy Region (ISEE/ISEEU Parificato not above EUR 26,887.93 and ISPE/ISPEEU Parificato not above EUR 58,452.06 for a.y. 2026-27), and a merit test verified after the fact through credit thresholds. scholarships.title: Talents 4 UniTo — Two-Year Scholarships for International Students Enrolling in English-Taught Maste
scholarships.description: Talents 4 UniTo is the University of Turin's programme of 40 two-year scholarships for talented international students enrolling for the first time in a postgraduate degree without a restricted number of places taught in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 20,000 gross in total (EUR 10,000 per academic year) and holders are exempt from university tuition fees, except for the first instalment due for enrolment in each academic year. Candidates are international students who hold a qualification obtained outside the Italian system valid for admission to a postgraduate degree, do not hold Italian citizenship and are not resident in Italy. There is no separate application form: applicants are included automatically if they apply on apply.unito.it for up to two eligible programmes during the published window. Selection is carried out per programme by an Evaluation Teaching Committee on a 50-point scale with a 36-point eligibility threshold, and two scholarships are awarded per programme.
eligibility: Holds a qualification obtained at an institution outside the Italian system valid for admission to the chosen postgraduate degree, or obtains it by the final enrolment deadline for the academic year
Does not hold Italian citizenship; where Italian and another citizenship are held, the Italian citizenship prevails and the candidate is excluded

Is not resident in Italy; non-EU citizens holding a residence permit that allows enrolment at an Italian university under art. 39(5) of Legislative Decree 286/98 are treated as residents and are excluded
Meets the admission requirements of the chosen programme as published on apply.unito.it
Has submitted an application for a maximum of two postgraduate degrees without restricted access taught in English during the published window
Has English language proficiency of at least B2 level on the Common European Framework of Reference

Has never been enrolled in any degree programme, single-cycle master's degree or postgraduate degree at the University of Turin or any other Italian or foreign university, including simultaneous enrolment

The previous edition funded 38 scholarships, and the 2027-2028 call was not published at the verification date.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is carried out by the Evaluation Teaching Committee for each programme listed in the call, composed of academic staff who assess academic qualifications and personal preparation. Scholarships are awarded to the two highest-ranking candidates per programme on a maximum of 50 points, with a minimum eligibility score of 36 points. In a tie the younger candidate prevails, and scholarships not awarded by one programme cannot be reassigned to another.

scholarships.title: UNICORE 8.0 University Corridors for Refugees — University of Turin Scholarship (a.y. 2026-2027 / 2027-2028)
scholarships.description: UNICORE 8.0 (University Corridors for Refugees) is a project promoted by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees that creates educational corridors from selected countries in Africa and Asia to Italy, in partnership with MAECI, Caritas Italiana, Diaconia Valdese and a group of Italian universities. For the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 academic years the University of Turin awards three two-year cash-and-services scholarships for refugee students to access its open-access, English-taught Master's degree programmes. Each scholarship provides a cash benefit of EUR 7,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from all amounts due for university enrolment, except the first instalment of the student contribution. The award is paid in four instalments by bank transfer to an Italian bank account, with each payment conditional on enrolment and credit milestones.

Applications that are incomplete or not correctly filled in are not accepted. Winners are notified by the International Students Office, and if a winner withdraws the University proceeds down the ranking with the next eligible candidate.

scholarships.title: MOFA Taiwan Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Bachelor's, Master's, PhD, plus Pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program (LEP)
scholarships.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan), funds international students for degree programmes or a pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program at Mandarin-teaching institutions affiliated with MOE-accredited universities. Recipients receive a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programmes or NT$28,000 for the LEP, plus one-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan, and must cover all other expenses themselves. The award period is one year for the LEP, up to four years for undergraduate and doctoral study and two years for a master's, with a five-year total cap. Applications are accepted from 1 February to 31 March each year, and the programme is open to students of any country except mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, in principle prioritising Taiwan's diplomatic partners.

scholarships.deadline_display: February 1 – March 31, 2026 (apply through local ROC embassy/TECO)

Is not a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan).
Is not an overseas compatriot student.
Has never attended an educational institution in Taiwan at the same level of degree or LEP that he/she intends to apply for.
Is not an exchange student through any cooperation agreement between a foreign university/college and an educational institute in Taiwan while receiving the Scholarship.
Has not previously had a Scholarship revoked by an ROC government agency or other relevant institution.
In principle, holds citizenship of a country that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan; special consideration may be given to students from other countries.
The programme is not applicable to students from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau.

No previous Scholarship revocation by an ROC government agency or other relevant institution.
scholarships.duration: Pre-degree LEP: one year. Degree programmes: undergraduate maximum four years, master's maximum two years, doctoral maximum four years. Award periods must be continuous with no breaks and cannot exceed five years in total.
scholarships.application_period: Annual window from 1 February to 31 March, applying to the Taiwan Scholarship cycle for the following academic year. The February-March 2026 window has closed; the next is expected 1 February to 31 March 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: The Scholarship is in principle granted to students from countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan; special consideration may also be given to students from other countries. Selection follows the programme guidelines published by MOFA and administered for applicants through the Taiwan Scholarships portal.

scholarships.title: MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (HES)
scholarships.description: The Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) established the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship to encourage international students to study Mandarin Chinese in Taiwan. The award funds a 2-month summer course or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course, and pays a monthly stipend of NT$28,000. Applicants must be foreign nationals aged 18 or over with an excellent academic record and good moral character, must already have applied to a Chinese language centre, and must submit their documents to the ROC overseas office for their country of nationality. MOE publishes no single deadline date, noting only that applications are made 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'.

scholarships.title: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) – Academia Sinica
scholarships.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP), administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to fourteen English-taught Ph.D. programmes and pays a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable for one further year for students who perform well. Academia Sinica also subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, but students still pay the domestic tuition rate, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder. Applications are submitted online between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8) with no application fee, and admission results are usually announced in late June or early July for enrolment the following fall.
eligibility: International applicant seeking admission to one of the fourteen TIGP Ph.D. programmes.
Must satisfy the general and programme-specific admission requirements published on the TIGP site for the chosen programme.
Must not already hold the degree level to which they are applying, per TIGP's general admission requirements.
No application fee is required.
benefits: Programs in Chemical Biology, Molecular Science, Nano Science, Biodiversity, AI of Things, Earth System Science, etc.
requirements: Apply online through the TIGP application system between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8).
Meet the general admission requirements and the specific requirements of the chosen Ph.D. programme.
Select a thesis advisor before the end of the first year of study.
Uphold the academic integrity standards of Academia Sinica and the partner university.
Confirm tuition arrangements with the programme secretary, since the domestic tuition rate varies by partner university.
scholarships.duration: PhD programme of three years. The stipend is paid for the first year and, for students who perform well, extended for one more year; after the scholarship/stipend allowance period, further financial support depends on the individual thesis advisor.

Admission results are usually announced in late June or early July, and admitted applicants enrol in the following fall semester.
scholarships.selection_notes: Admission is decided per Ph.D. programme. TIGP states that admission results are usually announced in late June or early July, and each programme publishes its own admission criteria and evaluation. A research proposal and interview requirements are set at programme level.
scholarships.program_type: Research-based doctoral scholarship programme administered by a research institute (Academia Sinica) with partner universities
scholarships.name: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) – Academia Sinica

scholarships.title: INTENSE Program (International Industrial Talents Education Special Program)
scholarships.description: The International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program) is a Ministry of Education initiative, run with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies to recruit international students into industry-linked degree programmes in key fields such as STEM, finance and semiconductors. Admitted students receive full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket to Taiwan, initial administrative expense support and a monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 paid by the partner company, plus paid internships, in exchange for an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation. Applications are made to individual participating universities, which publish their own deadlines for each Spring and Fall intake, so there is no single programme-wide application date.
eligibility: Must meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
Must apply to a specific approved INTENSE programme at a participating university, in one of the key industry fields (commonly STEM, finance and semiconductors).
English-taught programmes: CEFR B1 English proficiency required at admission, and TOCFL Level A2 (Listening and Reading) by the end of the first semester of the second academic year.
Chinese-taught programmes: TOCFL Level B1 (Listening and Reading) required.
Some programmes restrict eligible nationalities, for example Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand; others accept students of all nationalities.
Must satisfy the participating university's own programme requirements, including academic performance within the top 50% of the class and a conduct score of not lower than 80 points.
benefits: Monthly living allowance from partner companies (ASUS, MediaTek, Realtek, etc.)
requirements: Meet the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.
Meet the participating university's programme-specific academic and language requirements.
Maintain grades in the top 50% of the class and a conduct score of not lower than 80 points, or equivalent to Grade A.
Accept the mandatory internship stage and the employment obligation in Taiwan.
For students already studying in Taiwan at junior or senior undergraduate level, academic performance within the top 50% of the class and a conduct grade of at least 80 or Grade A.
scholarships.duration: Typically a two-year degree programme of study plus internship, followed by employment in Taiwan.
scholarships.application_period: Two intakes a year. Spring intake first round runs from early October to late December and second round from early April to late June; the Fall intake mirrors those two rounds. Each participating university publishes its own exact dates, so no single application period applies.
scholarships.selection_notes: The university's proposal must pass joint review by the Ministry of Education and the relevant ministries before the programme can run, and participating universities must sign contracts with companies to provide student living allowances and internships. Admission is therefore per programme and per intake, with results typically announced in the middle of the year for a September start and in mid-January for a February start.
scholarships.program_type: Industry-academia collaboration degree programme (MOE specialised class) with a compulsory employment obligation in Taiwan after graduation
scholarships.name: INTENSE Program (International Industrial Talents Education Special Program)

scholarships.title: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship
scholarships.description: The NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship supports current international graduate students at National Taiwan University through a matching-fund structure: NTU waives the student's tuition, while the student's thesis or dissertation supervisor pays a monthly research-assistant salary, with published minimums of TWD 6,000 per month for two years for master's students and TWD 8,000 per month for three years for PhD students, before tax. Applicants must first secure a professor willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form, and must pass an annual review to keep the award. The published application period is 23 April to 15 May, through NTU's International Degree Current Student System, and roughly half of applicants are awarded.

Overseas Chinese students and Mainland Chinese students are excluded.
Must have a thesis or dissertation supervisor willing to sponsor the award and sign the university's word form.
Must pass the annual review to continue receiving the scholarship.

Secure a sponsoring thesis or dissertation supervisor who will sign the word form and pay the research-assistant salary.
Submit past years' transcripts or an Advisor Evaluation Form.
Submit a recommendation letter for the Outstanding International Graduate Student Scholarship and a curriculum vitae.
Pass the annual review to retain the award.
scholarships.duration: Minimum monthly support for two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to passing an annual review.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, with a published application period of 23 April to 15 May for existing international degree students at NTU, applying through the International Degree Current Student System.
scholarships.selection_notes: Decision on NTU scholarships is made by the professors of the department to which the applicant belongs. NTU's scholarship FAQ states that about half of applicants receive scholarships. Renewal requires passing review each year.
scholarships.program_type: University merit scholarship with a matching-fund structure (university tuition waiver plus a thesis supervisor's research-assistant salary)
scholarships.name: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship

scholarships.title: NTHU International Student Scholarship
scholarships.description: The NTHU International Student Scholarship, funded by the Office of Global Affairs at National Tsing Hua University, is applied for through the same online system as admission to an NTHU international degree programme. It provides a full tuition and credit-fee waiver plus a tiered monthly stipend: NTD 20,000 to 40,000 per month for doctoral students, NTD 10,000 per month for doctoral students in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences or the International Intercollegiate PhD Program with supervisors from that college, and NTD 5,000 per month for master and bachelor students. It is restricted to applicants who and whose parents have always held foreign nationality and never held Taiwan nationality, excludes overseas Chinese student status, and is not available for Medicine, Dentistry, Traditional Chinese Medicine, the College of Semiconductor or ICDF programmes.

scholarships.title: NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students Award
scholarships.description: The NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students awards a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 together with a tuition waiver for two years to new doctoral students at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University who have outstanding grades and hold no other scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government. It is not open to direct application: NYCU states that the award is made on the basis of recommendations from the college and a review by the scholarship committee. Recipients must submit semester transcripts and tuition payment receipts before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible, and the stipend is in principle deposited on the 10th of each month. The tuition waiver covers basic tuition only, with dormitory, insurance and campus facility fees remaining payable.

Existing recipients must submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts each semester before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible in the following semester, and renewals are handled in the application period announced by the OIA.

scholarships.title: MOE Elite Scholarship for University Lecturers from South & Southeast Asia
scholarships.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program was created by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) under its New Southbound Policy to encourage university lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue graduate degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral study. Awardees receive a total monthly award of NT$25,000 for up to two years of a master's programme or three years of a doctorate, reviewed annually; participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total and pay the remainder to the student as a monthly stipend, which at Taipei Tech works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years one to three and NT$12,000 in year four. Applicants must currently hold a lecturer or more senior post at a university in an eligible country with that position on hold, must supply an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, and apply through the participating university, which submits the case for MOE review. Around 100 places are awarded per academic year across a three-year cycle.
eligibility: Must be a university lecturer, assistant professor or professor currently employed at a public or private higher education institution in an eligible country.

Eligible Southeast and South Asian countries: Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.

African route: applicants from any African country who are either current university lecturers or professors with an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English, or have at least three years of university researcher experience in an African country with research publications or papers.
Must be a citizen of the country where they hold the teaching position.
The teaching position must be on hold because of the studies.
Must provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English; the African researcher route requires an employment certificate in English plus research publications.
Must not hold Taiwan (R.O.C.) nationality or overseas Chinese student status.

Must not be enrolled in, or hold a retained admission at, a university in Taiwan. This restriction does not apply to a student on course to graduate who is pursuing a next degree, provided they are still a lecturer from a South or Southeast Asian country.
Must not previously have studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level.
Must not be an exchange or dual-degree student under a partnership agreement with an overseas institution.
Must not have received stipends through this programme for more than three years.
Must not be a recipient of any other scholarship or financial assistance from a Taiwan government agency or a foreign government.
Must satisfy the participating university's own admission and English-taught programme requirements.
benefits: Disbursed as NT$25,000/month (used partly for tuition/credit fees, remainder as stipend)
requirements: Hold a current university lecturer, assistant professor or professor post at an institution in an eligible country.
Provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English.
Have the teaching position on hold because of the studies.
Apply to a participating university and, where required, choose a full English-taught programme.
Submit the MOE-Elite form and documents by the deadline stated in the university's post-admission email.
Complete enrolment procedures every semester to keep the two or three-year scholarship continuous.
Apply for renewal each year, subject to review.
scholarships.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme under the standard MOE terms, reviewed annually. Some participating universities extend this, and Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years.
scholarships.application_period: Tied to each participating university's admission cycle, with published Fall application windows running from around mid-December to mid-March, followed by a post-admission document submission stage with its own email-stated deadline. MOE announces recipient lists around late October for Fall and late April for the African Spring intake. The AY2026/27 Fall window closed in mid-March 2026; the next is expected to open around mid-December 2026 for 2027 Fall entry.
scholarships.selection_notes: The programme is administered under the MOE Elite Scholarship Program Action Plan and was created in accordance with the New Southbound Policy Work Plan announced by the Executive Yuan in December 2016, under the MOE New Southbound Policy Talent Development Program. Priority is given to doctoral programmes. The university evaluates the admission application by department, and the MOE then reviews and determines the scholarship award. Published quota: one hundred students per academic year over three academic years, for a total of three hundred students. MOE allocates the quota, so entry is limited to new PhD students in the relevant intakes and can involve a waitlist.
scholarships.program_type: Government graduate scholarship for university lecturers from South, Southeast Asia and Africa to study in Taiwan (Ministry of Education, New Southbound Policy talent development)
scholarships.image_alt_text: National Cheng Kung University Office of International Affairs
scholarships.name: MOE Elite Scholarship for University Lecturers from South & Southeast Asia

The fellowship is a grant of CHF 10,000 to CHF 15,000 per year with no teaching duties, awarded for one year and extended for the regular duration of the chosen Master's programme if the holder is academically successful at the end of the first semester. Selection is based on excellence, and applications are made online from the beginning of January with a 28 February deadline.

scholarships.description: The Alfred Werner Scholarship Program of the SCS Foundation, a partner organisation of the Swiss Chemical Society, supports highly talented international students who obtained their BSc outside Switzerland and wish to pursue an MSc in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences at a Swiss university or one of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology. The scholarship amounts to CHF 36,000, previously CHF 30,000, and is supported by the Swiss chemical and pharmaceutical industry and private donors. scholarships.title: CERN Doctoral Student Programme
scholarships.description: The CERN Doctoral Student Programme is a PhD-level employment contract in which doctoral students carry out cutting-edge research at CERN in collaboration with their university, in fields spanning physics, engineering, applied physics, electronics, electrical engineering, information technologies, chemical and process engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, data science and AI, and technology transfer. The programme pays a monthly net allowance of CHF 3,907 together with CERN health insurance, a possible family supplement, possible travel to Geneva on joining, and 30 days of paid leave plus two weeks of annual closure. Contracts run six months and are renewable up to three years, with the possibility of spreading the total over a maximum of four consecutive years. Eligibility is limited to nationals of CERN Member or Associate Member States, and applicants from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey are currently excluded because the Article II.5 ceiling has been reached.

scholarships.title: CERN Research Fellowship
scholarships.description: The CERN Research Fellowship Programme, part of CERN's broader Graduate Programme, is an opportunity for recent PhD graduates in physics and engineering to conduct advanced research in science, technology, engineering and mathematics at CERN. It pays a monthly net stipend of either CHF 7,004 or CHF 7,425 depending on the degree and years of post-graduation experience, together with CERN health insurance for the fellow, their partner and children, a contribution to the CERN Pension Fund, and depending on individual circumstances an installation grant, family, child and infant allowances and travel to Geneva on joining. Fellows receive 30 days of paid leave per year plus two weeks of CERN's annual closure, and on-the-job and formal training including language classes. Contracts run 6 to 24 months with the possibility of extension up to 36 months. Applicants must be nationals of a CERN Member or Associate Member State, must hold a PhD or obtain one within six months, must respect a research-experience cap of six years for Theoretical and Experimental Physics or three years for Applied Sciences and Engineering, and must never previously have held a CERN fellow or graduate contract.

Most run throughout 2026 on an available-until-allocated basis, while the BackPack Scholarship closes on 14 July. Scholarships are applied for through the Program section of the MBA application form and are awarded to candidates who have applied for and accepted an offer, with selection based on academic and professional excellence, GMAT/GRE scores, career progression, international exposure and Assessment Day performance. scholarships.title: WIPO Fellowship Program
scholarships.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program places professionals in specialized disciplines at the World Intellectual Property Organization in Geneva, Switzerland, for 12 to 36 months. Fellows are classified into four categories: translation fellows in the PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program, legal case manager fellows in the WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program, visiting and research fellows in the Research and Visiting Fellowship Program, and other specialized fellows. Applicants must hold at least a first-level university degree, with additional requirements such as professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies depending on the category. Fellows receive a monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and relevant experience, comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance largely paid by WIPO, relocation assistance covering travel at the start and end of the fellowship, assistance with visa formalities, 10 official holidays plus 2.5 days of annual leave per full month, and access to WIPO Academy training with up to six study leave days a year. Positions are advertised through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website and LinkedIn.

scholarships.title: Delft University of Technology (TU Delft) Justus & Louise van Effen Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships are financed by the legacy of Justus and Louise van Effen and administered by TU Delft together with Delft University Fund, with a minimum of 16 awards each year, two per faculty. Awarded students receive full tuition fees per year for a two-year regular TU Delft master's programme, based on the statutory or institutional rate for their nationality, plus a contribution towards living expenses. Applicants must be excellent international students among the top 10% of their graduating class and must submit a complete MSc application, the scholarship application form, a reference letter and an English language certificate by 1 December 2026 (23:59 CET), with results announced by the end of March 2027.

Not a TU Delft bachelor's student, including international students
Bachelor's degree not obtained at a Dutch university
Not already started MSc studies at TU Delft (for new incoming students only)
requirements: Complete the MSc application and tick the scholarship option
Submit the Scholarship Application Form 2027-2029
Submit one reference letter
Submit the English language certificate with the MSc application before the scholarship deadline
scholarships.application_period: One round per year tied to the TU Delft international MSc application; scholarship application form 2027-2029, results emailed by the end of March 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: The university states the scholarships are "extremely limited and highly competitive, with only the strongest candidates selected", and that applications far outnumber the funds available.
scholarships.program_type: University excellence scholarship financed by the Justus & Louise van Effen Fund

scholarships.title: Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS)
scholarships.description: The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship is a study scholarship for excellent students joining a full-time Leiden University master's programme starting in September, with the exception of the non-advanced LLM and MSc programmes of Leiden Law School. Applicants must normally hold a non-EEA/non-EFTA passport and not be eligible for Dutch student finance. The scholarship is awarded for the duration of the programme at one of five tuition-fee levels between EUR 10,000 and EUR 19,000, and Leiden states it is not a full scholarship, so a significant personal contribution is still required and non-EEA recipients must prove sufficient funds for their residence permit. The application is made inside the master's admission application with a motivation letter of maximum 500 words, and the deadline is 1 December 2026.

Excellent academic results in the previous study programme, indicated as being amongst the top 10% of graduates

scholarships.name: Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS)

scholarships.title: University of Groningen Holland Scholarship & Talent Grant
scholarships.description: The University of Groningen's NL Scholarship is a one-time grant for international students from outside the EEA who wish to pursue a master's degree in the Netherlands, co-funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and the university. It amounts to EUR 5,000, is awarded for one academic year only and can be received only once in a lifetime, and it is intended to help cover living expenses during the first year of study rather than to cover the full cost of studying. Applicants need an admission offer for one of the listed master's programmes, a bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands and excellent undergraduate performance, and they must submit a motivation letter, a transcript of records and the admission letter before the deadline. The published deadline for the 2026-2027 academic year was 1 February 2026, with results notified by 15 March.
eligibility: Do not hold the nationality of an EEA country and not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for any other reason
Enrolled at the University of Groningen as a full-time student for the academic year and master's programme for which the scholarship is awarded
Bachelor's degree obtained or to be obtained outside the Netherlands, with no diplomas from the Netherlands and no previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes are excluded)
Demonstrated excellent academic performance during the bachelor's studies
Hold an admission offer letter from the University of Groningen for one of the programmes on the published applicable-programmes list
Be eligible to meet the requirements for obtaining a Dutch student visa
Not have obtained the NL Scholarship before
benefits: Talent Grant: tuition fee waiver for outstanding students
requirements: Receive an admission offer from the University of Groningen for a listed programme first
Complete the scholarship application form on the official page
Upload the motivation letter, transcript of records and admission letter
Submit before the published deadline; incomplete applications are not considered
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle tied to the master's admission round; applications open after the applicant receives an admission offer, with a 1 February deadline for the 2026-2027 academic year and results notified by 15 March.
scholarships.selection_notes: Recipients are selected on academic excellence, ambition and relevant experience, assessed by the faculty selection committee of the programme applied for; the University aims to notify all applicants by 15 March.
scholarships.program_type: Government and university co-funded one-time grant for incoming non-EEA master's students
scholarships.name: University of Groningen Holland Scholarship & Talent Grant

scholarships.title: Radboud University Scholarship Programme
scholarships.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a very selective scholarship for talented, highly motivated non-EEA students with outstanding study results applying to a complete English-taught Radboud University master's programme. A Radboud Scholarship reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 for 2027/2028, against an example normal fee of about EUR 19,000, and covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs, while living and studying costs remain the student's responsibility. A maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027/2028 across six faculties, the application is made through the OSIRIS master's application with two reference letters and a CV, the OSIRIS submission deadline is 31 January 2027 and the file must be complete by 14 February 2027, and the decision is communicated before mid-April 2027.
eligibility: Hold a non-EU/non-EEA passport
Not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons

Have (or be about to obtain) a bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands, with no Dutch degrees and no previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded unless part of that bachelor's)
Meet the English language proficiency requirement of the chosen master's programme
Be fully admitted to the English-taught master's programme starting 1 September 2027, as stated in the formal admission letter
Be able to comply with the conditions for obtaining a visa for the Netherlands
Be enrolled at Radboud University as a full-time student for the academic year and programme concerned
requirements: Indicate in the OSIRIS master's application that you wish to apply for a Radboud Scholarship
Upload two reference letters and a curriculum vitae as part of the scholarship request
Submit in OSIRIS by 31 January 2027 23:59 CET
Ensure the application is complete by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET
scholarships.application_period: One round per academic year for the September 2027 intake: submit in OSIRIS by 31 January 2027 23:59 CET, complete by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET, decision before mid-April 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: The university states the programme is "a very selective scholarship programme" and that selection is by the selection committee of the faculty applied to, based on academic excellence, ambition and references; some study programmes also hold interviews.

scholarships.title: Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship programme awards 18 full scholarships each academic year, including a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend, to highly talented students from outside the EU who have been admitted to a Maastricht University master's programme. It combines the High Potential Scholarship, funded by the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund, with the ministry-funded NL Scholarship. For the 2027-2028 intake, scholarship applications run from 1 October 2026 to 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET), the participating master's application must be complete through Studielink before 10 December 2026, and applicants must be non-EU/EEA (also excluding Switzerland and Surinam), aged 35 or under on 1 September 2027, with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 and no previous degree-seeking study in the Netherlands. Recipients receive a living-expense stipend of EUR 20,150 over 13 months or EUR 38,750 over 25 months, tuition fees, visa costs and EUR 700 of health and liability insurance paid at cost, a mandatory UM room until 16 July 2028 and a two-week Pre-Academic Training programme. Only about 2% of applicants are awarded.
eligibility: Hold a nationality from outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland or Surinam and meet the requirements for a Dutch entry visa and residence permit
Not have dual nationality from an EU/EEA country or Switzerland
Have applied for admission to a participating full-time master's programme for 2027-2028 and submitted the application file in full, meeting all admission requirements, before 10 December 2026
Meet the specific admission requirements of the chosen UM master's programme
Never have participated in a degree-seeking higher education programme in the Netherlands (completed exchange programmes are welcome)

Submit only one application, for one UM scholarship only
