scholarships.duration: If the scholarship covers only tuition fees, make sure you can finance your living expenses (rent, food and insurances) for the complete duration of your studies.
scholarships.application_period: One round per academic year for the September 2027 intake: scholarship applications open 1 October 2026, the master's application must be complete by 10 December 2026, scholarship applications close 1 February 2027 23:59 CET, statuses are given in April 2027 and final results by May 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: The UM International Services Desk checks completeness after 1 February, forwards complete files to each faculty in February 2027, each faculty ranks its top five, the shortlist is confirmed by the end of March, shortlisted candidates are invited to an online interview, and statuses (selected, waitlisted or rejected) are communicated in April 2027, final by May 2027. Maastricht states that only about 2% of applicants receive the scholarship.
scholarships.program_type: University full scholarship (university fund + national NL Scholarship)
scholarships.name: Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship

scholarships.title: University of Twente Scholarship (UTS)
scholarships.description: The University of Twente Scholarship is a scholarship for excellent students from non-EU/EEA countries applying for an English-taught master's programme at the University of Twente. Its value ranges from EUR 3,000 to EUR 22,000 for one year and is intended as compensation for study-related costs, with no costs such as tuition fees paid on the student's behalf; for two-year programmes a second-year award of an equal amount is possible if the student obtains an average grade of 7 out of 10 and at least 50 percent of the European Credits at the end of the third quartile of the first year. Applicants must first obtain an academic admission letter for a qualifying 2027/2028 master's programme, hold a UT student number, meet English requirements of IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 90 with 6.0 in speaking, not be eligible for a Dutch study loan, and belong to the top 5 to 10 percent of their graduating class. The application form opens on 15 October 2026 and closes on 1 April 2027 at 16:00 CET, with results in the first week of May 2027.

Be (provisionally) admitted to a qualifying UT master's programme starting in the academic year 2027/2028 (September)
Have a UT student number
Not have graduated from a UT undergraduate or graduate programme

scholarships.title: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (VU) Fellowship Programme
scholarships.description: The VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) is a merit-based tuition fee waiver from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam for non-EU/EEA applicants who pay higher tuition fees. It can be granted for a one- or two-year full-time English-taught Master's programme starting in September 2027, and a second year is only extended if 100% of the ECTS of the first year are achieved. The official page states the VUFP 'covers the tuition fees only' and 'does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances'. Applications for the 2027/2028 cycle open on 1 November 2026 and close on 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET.

Prove academic excellence with a GPA equivalent to a Dutch 8

Joint programmes where VU Amsterdam does not administer the admission process are excluded
The degree for which admission is sought has not been obtained in the Netherlands
Not currently enrolled in a Bachelor or Master programme in the Netherlands
No preparatory programme required before the start of the Master's

Paste the GPA proof/programme transcript and grading scale explanation at the end of the form
Upload the single PDF in the Scholarship section of the personal VU dashboard
Apply for only one Master's programme for the VUFP
Submit the application only once - resubmission is not allowed
scholarships.duration: One- or two-year full-time English-taught Master's programme starting September 2027

scholarships.title: Lund University Global Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Lund University Global Scholarship is a selective, merit-based scholarship that Lund University awards each year to high-achieving international students from outside the EU/EEA (and Switzerland) who pay tuition fees. Grants may cover part or all of the tuition fees, with the percentage set by the programme or faculty budget rather than the student's academic standing. The official page states 'Scholarships cover tuition fees only - living costs are not included', and recipients must independently meet the Swedish Migration Agency's living-cost funding requirement. Lund University awards approximately SEK 26 million in scholarship grants per year across the programme.

It is funded by the Swedish Council for Higher Education and is open to citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. Selection is merit-based and financial need is not considered; Uppsala states that only about 2% of applicants are granted a scholarship. The most recent application period was 16 January to 2 February 2026 for autumn 2026 studies, and the next round opens in early 2027.

The 2027 round opens on 1 December 2026 and closes on 15 January 2027, with results announced on 1 April 2027. In 2026, 9% of scholarship applicants who were admitted to a programme were nominated for the scholarship (65 out of 718).

scholarships.title: Linköping University Scholarship for Master's Students
scholarships.description: The LiU International Scholarship is a limited number of tuition-fee reductions awarded by Linköping University to fee-paying international master's students with significant academic potential; the tuition fee of an awardee is normally reduced by 50%. Applicants must have applied in the first admission round, ranked a LiU master's programme first, been admitted to that first choice in the first Notification of Selection Results, and met a minimum academic standard of GPA 3.5 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent. The application window opens on the day the Notification of Selection Results is published and closes a few days later - 26 to 30 March 2026 in the last published round - and no additional documents are required. Awards can cover 30 credits per semester, must be maintained by passing at least 75% of courses in the first academic year, and are rescinded if a Swedish Institute scholarship is awarded instead.

scholarships.title: Umeå University Scholarship for International Students
scholarships.description: The Umeå University Scholarship for International Students is awarded each autumn semester alongside the autumn admission to academically talented applicants who are required to pay tuition fees. Scholarships take the form of tuition waivers, and selected candidates receive a full or partial waiver of the tuition fee for their programme; no living-cost component is published. Applicants must be citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, have applied for a full bachelor's or master's programme, paid the application fee, and have a Umeå University programme as priority 1 on University Admissions by 15 January. Invitations to register interest are emailed in early February and the interest deadline falls in early March - 4 March 2026 at 23:59 CET in the last published cycle - with results announced by email in mid-April. Selection is made by faculty committees on academic merit.

scholarships.selection_notes: After the interest registration deadline, a committee within each respective faculty selects candidates. The selections are based on the applicant's academic merit, as well as any other relevant information shared in the registration form.

scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees — Sweden-based
scholarships.degree: Master's (2 years, joint degree, 2+ EU countries including Sweden)
scholarships.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes are master's degrees jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries, plus academic and non-academic associated partners. The European Commission's Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, maintained by EACEA and updated annually, lists the master's programmes currently supported by the EU; the stored row corresponds to the catalogue's Sweden country facet. Master's-level students from all over the world may apply, and Erasmus Mundus scholarships are available for outstanding students at participating programmes. Applicants apply directly to the consortium running their chosen programme, not to the European Commission.

scholarships.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS)
scholarships.application_period: Applications for courses starting the following academic year are submitted between October and January; the exact date is set by each consortium.

scholarships.title: One World Scholarship (Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg)
scholarships.description: The One World Scholarship of the Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg is a partial scholarship of EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) for students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who study in Salzburg. Applicants must already be enrolled in Austria or admitted to a regular degree programme, hold a student residence permit or visa, and be admitted to a regular Master's or PhD programme in Salzburg. Selection is a multi-stage process - online form until 12 July, verification of formal criteria, full application until 15 July, online interview, then acceptance or rejection - and the Institute states that applying does not guarantee a scholarship place because positions are very limited. Successful applicants are expected to show financial need, good study progress, interest in development-related issues and a willingness to attend monthly meetings and actively contribute to the programme. Regarding equally qualified individuals, priority is given to female students.

scholarships.title: Doctoral Scholarship from the University of Innsbruck
scholarships.description: The University of Innsbruck awards a doctoral scholarship as start-up, interim, bridge or final financing for doctoral candidates, with a monthly allowance of EUR 1,120 for a maximum of 24 months. Funding is granted in six-month blocks confirmed by an interim progress report from the dissertation supervisor, and the 24-month period can be interrupted twice, each interruption not exceeding six months. Applicants must be enrolled as regular students and registered for continuation with a registered dissertation, and must evidence excellent academic success - an excellent grade point average plus normal duration of study - or scientific achievements; a maximum of two resubmissions is possible. The University states that at least 50 per cent of available funding is to be awarded to women in order to promote young female scientists, and that applicants of equal scientific quality are prioritised if they work in the University's main research areas or on project proposals. Payments are made exclusively by SEPA transfer.

scholarships.title: FWF ESPRIT (Early-Stage Program: Research - Innovation - Training)
scholarships.description: ESPRIT (Early-Stage Program: Research - Innovation - Training) is an Austrian Science Fund career programme that lets highly qualified postdoc-level researchers lead an independent research project at an Austrian research institution. The FWF states a funding period of 36 months, paying the principal investigator's salary at the current senior postdoc rate plus project-specific costs of EUR 45,000 as a flat rate, or up to EUR 75,000 with justification. Submissions are accepted on a rolling basis through the elane online application portal, and decisions are taken at five Scientific Board approval meetings per year.

The programme is decided by the FWF Scientific Board on the recommendation of an international jury following peer review and a hearing, with about 18 awards per call and half of them awarded to women. Proposals are submitted through the elane portal during a published annual application window, which was closed on the verification date.

scholarships.title: Doctoral Recruitment Call 2026 - Social Sciences, Humanities & Cultural Studies (SSH Call 2026), University of Vienna
scholarships.description: The University of Vienna's SSH Call 2026 is a central recruitment call offering at least 40 fully funded four-year doctoral positions in the social sciences, humanities and cultural studies across nine participating doctoral schools, including the Vienna Doctoral School in Cognition, Behavior, and Neuroscience (CoBeNe). scholarships.title: DAAD Research Grants - Doctoral Candidates and Young Academics
scholarships.description: The DAAD Research Grants in Germany fund a research project at a state or state-recognised university or non-university research institute in Germany, carried out with a German scientific supervisor. Doctoral candidates may be funded for 2 to 12 months and early postdocs for 2 to 6 months; the grant cannot be extended and cannot be split within the funding period. The current DAAD announcement sets a monthly scholarship payment of EUR 1,400 plus insurance cover, a travel allowance, and for stays over six months a research allowance of EUR 460, a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly family allowance. Applications are submitted online through the DAAD Portal and are open annually, with deadlines updated in the second quarter of each year; on 2026-10-04 the DAAD stated that applications for the 2027 funding period were closed.

Applications are accepted each year from 1 September to 30 October at 23:59 Central European Time, and courses run between June and September.

scholarships.title: MEXT Scholarship for Undergraduate Students
scholarships.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for students from abroad who want to study as undergraduate students at Japanese national universities, selected through the recommendation of a Japanese embassy or consulate general. Applicants first pass a First Screening (documents, written academic examinations and interview) at the diplomatic mission in their country, are recommended to MEXT, and then pass MEXT's Second Screening. The scholarship pays a monthly allowance of JPY 117,000, waives entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and provides an economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on return, back to the grantee's home country. The scholarship period is five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory Japanese language education, or seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and six-year pharmacy courses.

scholarships.title: MEXT Young Leaders Program (YLP) Scholarship
scholarships.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students is the seventh type of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship. It funds a one-year master's course at a Japanese graduate school for university or college graduates with practical work experience and for young public administrators who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries. The scholarship pays JPY 242,000 per month, the tuition is exempted, and round-trip airfare to and from Japan is provided. Unlike the other six MEXT scholarship types, YLP is neither embassy-recommended nor university-recommended: recruitment is conducted by the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, the initial selection is by document screening, interview and essay writing, and the final selection is made by the YLP Committee set in MEXT.

scholarships.title: JASSO Reservation Program for Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship by Pre-arrival Admission
scholarships.description: JASSO's reservation programme for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students, for students who have already received pre-arrival admission to a Japanese institution and face financial difficulties. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 for 12 months if the student enrols in April, or for 6 months if the student enrols in September or October. Applications are not made to JASSO directly; the applicant must apply through the school they plan to enrol in. There are three reservation categories: graduate level, EJU exam, and English courses.

Faces financial difficulties and has an excellent academic and character record

scholarships.title: MOFCOM Scholarship-CSC Program
scholarships.description: The MOFCOM Scholarship is an aid programme hosted by the Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China that offers postgraduate study in China to applicants from developing countries. It runs in two tracks: the MOFCOM-40 direct-admission track of 40 MOFCOM-led projects, and the MOFCOM-CSC joint track operated with the China Scholarship Council. Through the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone, applicants register on the CSC portal under institution code 00010, select three target universities and majors, and email the full document set to the embassy. The official programme PDF states free on-campus accommodation and annual stipends of RMB 36,000 for master's and RMB 42,000 for PhD students. Admission is decided by the receiving university.

scholarships.title: Chinese Government Scholarship - Tsinghua University Program (Type B)
scholarships.description: The Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS) is funded by the Chinese government and administered by the China Scholarship Council, which is entrusted by the Ministry of Education with admission, enrolment and administration of recipients. Tsinghua University hosts the Category Type B route, in which the university nominates candidates under the CGS-Chinese University Program, and the page also explains that Type A programmes are handled by other authorities such as the bilateral, EU and AUN programmes. This record covers the Type B route for graduate study at Tsinghua. Full CGS covers tuition, university accommodation or an accommodation subsidy, a stipend and comprehensive medical insurance, for one to three years of master's study or four to five years of doctoral study.

scholarships.title: UCAS Chinese Government Scholarship (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)
scholarships.description: Entrusted by the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China, the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences recruits outstanding young graduate students from around the world for master's and doctoral study and provides full scholarships. The award exempts tuition (RMB 40,000 per year for PhD, RMB 30,000 for master's) and the RMB 600 application fee, pays a monthly stipend of RMB 5,000 for PhD and RMB 3,500 for master's students, provides free accommodation on the Beijing campus or an off-campus subsidy, and includes medical insurance of RMB 800 per person. Sponsorship runs for 36 months, with up to 12 months of permitted extension for doctoral students. Applications must be filed in both the CSC system and the UCAS admission system before the published deadline.

scholarships.title: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship (GOI-IES)
scholarships.description: The Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship supports high-calibre international students who wish to study at NFQ levels 9 or 10 (master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD) in Ireland. The programme is funded by the Government of Ireland in partnership with Irish higher education institutions and managed by the Higher Education Authority, and 60 scholarships are awarded each year for one year of full-time study. Each scholarship comprises a stipend of EUR 10,000 plus a full fee waiver from the host institution for the scholarship year. Applicants must come from outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK, must already hold an offer from an eligible Irish institution, and must submit one application with proof of admission and two references through the HEA portal.

Must first apply for admission to a master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD programme at an eligible Irish higher education institution under that institution's own admission procedures

Must hold a conditional or final offer of admission to an eligible Irish higher education institution at the time of applying, with proof of admission submitted in the relevant section of the GOI-IES application form
Students who have previously held a GOI-IES scholarship are not eligible to apply
Russian and Belarusian nationals are not eligible to apply
A maximum of one application per candidate may be submitted in the 2026 cycle
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver by host institution
requirements: Read the call documentation carefully to ascertain eligibility

Submit the application through the GOI-IES online application portal

scholarships.duration: One year of full-time study at NFQ level 9 or 10
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 cycle ran to a 5pm (Irish time) deadline on 12 March 2026 with the call outcome in early June 2026. Sixty scholarships are awarded each year, so the programme is annual and the 2027 date had not been published when checked.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants are expected to demonstrate a record of outstanding academic achievement, excellent communication skills, participation in extracurricular activities such as humanitarian work, politics, arts or sport, and a strong rationale for pursuing study in Ireland aligned with their longer-term goals. Institutions shortlist against their own strategic objectives before an independent panel assesses. Applications cannot be submitted once the deadline has passed and no alterations can be made after submission.

scholarships.title: UCD Global Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.description: UCD Global Excellence Scholarships offer a limited number of 100% and 50% tuition fee scholarships to outstanding international students who are classed as non-EU for tuition fee purposes and are applying to undergraduate or graduate taught programmes that appear on UCD's eligible-programmes list. Students must first secure an offer or conditional offer on an eligible course. Application deadlines are regional - 1 February 2026 for North American undergraduates, 28 February 2026 for undergraduate and graduate taught applicants from the Middle East, Africa and Pakistan and graduate taught applicants from South Asia, and 31 March 2026 for all other regions. Results are published via SISWeb about seven weeks after each regional deadline. The award is a tuition fee reduction only, is not automatically renewable, and is reassessed for continuing students between late September and October.

Awards are not automatically renewed for continuing students; each is reassessed in line with the original award terms, with outcomes notified between late September and October
requirements: Submit the programme application as early as possible - UCD reports a significant surge in applications during peak scholarship competition windows and processing delays may occur
Have received an offer or conditional offer for an eligible programme before the scholarship application
Check the Eligible Programmes 2026 document because some programmes are excluded
Read and accept the Terms & Conditions 2026/27
Follow the Application Instructions 2026
scholarships.duration: Not stated; the scholarships apply to the programme start in September.

scholarships.title: Trinity College Dublin Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: Trinity's Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarships are awarded to exceptional international students who have received a course offer for a full-time undergraduate degree at Trinity College Dublin. Scholarships range in value between EUR 2,000 and EUR 5,000 depending on the region and are applied as a reduction to the year one tuition fees of a full-time undergraduate programme. Applicants must have non-EU fee status and hold an offer to commence year one in 2026/2027; medicine, dentistry, acting, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are exempt, and students from China are not eligible and should apply for the Claddagh Undergraduate Scholarship instead. Applications are made online, assessed and awarded on a rolling basis, and awards take regional and programme diversity into account.

scholarships.title: Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships
scholarships.description: The Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships are offered by the New Zealand Government to eligible citizens of developing countries to study at a New Zealand or Pacific education institution. The tertiary strand is described by the administering agency as full scholarships for eligible international students to study full-time, and scholars may study at one of eight universities or three institutes of technology in New Zealand, or at one of two Pacific universities. The programme also runs vocational, thematic cohort and English language training for officials strands. Applications are submitted through the Manaaki applicant portal and require an academic transcript including the grading scale, with the awarding body warning that application systems may close early for countries with high application volumes.

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection follows the official steps: check eligible countries, check eligibility criteria, study subjects, research available courses, apply, then the selection process. The award is made on the recommendation of a selection committee and granted by the Vice-Chancellor.

scholarships.title: University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship
scholarships.description: The University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship is a competitive scheme run in four awarding rounds each year for high-achieving candidates applying for admission to an approved doctoral programme at Waipapa Taumata Rau. No separate scholarship application is needed — the candidate confirms in the doctoral programme application that they wish to be considered, and must not enrol before the outcome is advised. scholarships.title: University of Otago Global Scholarship
scholarships.description: The University of Otago Global Scholarships provide NZD $15,000 towards tuition fees to new international Bachelor degree students who hold a passport from one of twelve nominated countries — Bangladesh, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Macau, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam. There is no separate scholarship application: candidates are automatically assessed during the admission process and must tick the agreement to be considered for international scholarships in their eVision application for study. The scholarship is paid only as a credit towards tuition fees with a one-year tenure, is not deferrable, and becomes invalid if study does not commence by the enrolment date in the Offer of Place. Applicants must study on campus, and students sponsored by their home government or the New Zealand government are not eligible.

scholarships.title: VUW Postgraduate International Scholarship (Victoria University of Wellington)

scholarships.title: VUW Undergraduate International Scholarship (Victoria University of Wellington)
scholarships.description: The VUW Undergraduate International Scholarship is a partial fee-based scholarship of NZ$15,000 towards tuition fees for one year of study, for new international students entering their first year of a Bachelor's degree programme at Te Herenga Waka — Victoria University of Wellington and studying full-time on campus. No separate scholarship application is required: eligibility is assessed when the student applies for their programme, and the outcome is communicated in the Offer of Place. scholarships.title: LUT University Scholarships
scholarships.description: LUT University reduces tuition for fee-paying students of its two-year master's programmes in two automatic steps. In the first academic year every tuition-liable student who accepts the study place and pays the remaining EUR 10,000 of the first-year fee within 21 days of the official admission email receives an early bird discount of EUR 5,000. In the second academic year every tuition-liable student who has completed at least 60 ECTS credits in accordance with their personal study plan, with those credits recorded on the Transcript of Records by 31 July, and who pays the second-year fee on time receives a LUT scholarship of EUR 5,000. Neither award requires a separate application and neither covers living costs.

scholarships.title: Danish Government Scholarship for Highly Qualified Non-EU/EEA Students
scholarships.description: Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year to fund highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland. Applicants must be citizens of a non-EU/EEA/non-Swiss country, enrolled in a full degree programme and hold a time-limited residence permit for education, and they are excluded if they seek admission to an artistic higher education institution, have a legal claim to Danish citizens' rights, or are eligible for SU. The scholarship consists of two parts and may be a full or partial tuition fee waiver, a grant towards living costs, or both. The individual university administers the award and selects the students.

scholarships.title: Jagiellonian University Rector's Scholarship for International Students

Alongside it sit the Nova SBE Social Mobility Scholarship (20%, 50% or 100% of tuition, for candidates with proven financial need), the Nova SBE Continuity Scholarship (50% or 100%, for Nova SBE bachelor's graduates within a widened income threshold), and a series of partner-funded awards including Accenture (100%), Antonio Serrenho (100%), Banco Primus (100%), Deloitte (100%), Andre Sousa Bessa (100%), Women in Finance (20% or 50%), plus CEMS-specific awards. The Faculty of Social Sciences does not administer the scholarship: applications must be submitted through an embassy in the applicant's country, and the faculty becomes involved only after the Ministry of Education's initial selection.

scholarships.title: Václav Havel Bursary - Charles University
scholarships.description: The Václav Havel Bursary is Charles University's own financial support for international students whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes anywhere in the world. Students from countries where humanitarian organisations report violated human rights and freedoms and where discriminatory measures restrict access to education may apply, provided they have already been admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at a Charles University faculty through the standard admissions procedure. Students submit the application to the Student Affairs Office of their faculty, which forwards it digitally through the Dean to the Chair of the Václav Havel Bursary Board. As part of the preparation for studies in the Czech language, applicants may also request a contribution towards living expenses.

scholarships.title: Visegrad Scholarship Program 2027
scholarships.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports full-time Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for one to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. It is funded by the International Visegrad Fund, founded by the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia. The award is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, and it does not cover tuition. Applicants must already hold a bachelor's or master's degree, and their country of citizenship or residence must differ from the host institution's country.

scholarships.title: CTU Scholarship for Foreign Students - Czech Technical University in Prague
scholarships.description: CTU awards a scholarship to foreign students who wish to take a Master study programme at the Czech Technical University in Prague and display qualities that entitle them to the award, and to foreign doctoral students capable of doing scientific work who study on a doctoral programme in English at CTU in Prague. The Master's award is a contribution towards the costs of a stay in the Czech Republic of up to CZK 10,000 per month for one to two semesters; the doctoral award covers the basic doctoral-study scholarship plus living costs of up to CZK 16,000 per month for six to twelve months. Both are financed equally from the rectorate's scholarship fund and the relevant faculty's fund, and are awarded under Act No. 111/1998 Sb. on Universities, section 91(3)(b). The award is a living-cost contribution and does not cover tuition fees.

scholarships.title: RESDOC Doctoral Researcher Positions - Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project (MSCA COFUND)
scholarships.description: RESDOC (Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project) is an international doctoral training project at the University of Helsinki, co-funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions COFUND scheme under Horizon Europe and the University itself. It recruits 30 doctoral researchers for four-year, 100% employment contracts running 2027-2030, at a gross salary of approximately EUR 2,900 per month including a mobility allowance, plus an annual travel allowance for conferences and secondments. Research must fit one of four interdisciplinary themes: Infectious Diseases and Antimicrobial Resistance in Changing Environment; Biodiversity and Nature's Resilience; Secure and Sustainable Food and Water Systems; and Just Socio-Ecological Transition. The 2026 call closed on 31 August 2026 with 2,159 applications, and evaluation by external evaluators was under way in September 2026.

It covers the full tuition fee for the target time of the degree programme - three years for a bachelor's degree and two years for a master's degree. scholarships.description: The Embassy of France in South Africa invites citizens of South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi to apply for Master's or PhD study at French higher education institutions in the 2027/28 academic year under the France Excellence scheme. Because of the opposing hemispheres' academic calendars, laureates follow online French-language courses through the Alliances Françaises network in South Africa from February to July 2027 before departing for France in September 2027.

scholarships.title: ANRF Ramanujan Fellowship

Fellows must not already hold any permanent, tenure-track or contractual position in an Indian institution or university, and must be working abroad at the time of nomination. The fellowship pays Rs 1,35,000 per month consolidated including HRA, plus a research grant of Rs 7.00 lakh per annum and Rs 60,000 per annum in overhead charges to the host institute.

scholarships.title: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term (FY2027, 2nd Recruitment)
scholarships.description: The JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan invite mid-career and senior overseas researchers to Japan for lectures, discussions and exchange activities hosted by a Japanese researcher. The short-term option runs 14 to 60 days and covers a round-trip economy air ticket, a maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day, overseas travel insurance and a host-applied research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000. The candidate does not apply directly: a host researcher in Japan submits the application through the head of their institution.
eligibility: Candidate eligibility (both conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection, and during the fellowship period): (1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. (2) Be a full-time researcher or person with full-time researcher status at a university or research institution in a foreign country and have a position equivalent to a professor, associate professor or assistant professor in Japan (including positions such as professor emeritus). Researchers of other status may apply if it has been six years or longer since they obtained their doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution.

Host researcher (applicant) eligibility: be affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the Procedure for the Handling of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) issued by MEXT, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and wish to host an overseas researcher.

Host researcher eligibility: be a full-time researcher. However, researchers who are not employed full time may be eligible if the host institution judges them able to execute their responsibility to carrying out the program uninterruptedly throughout the Fellow's tenure including providing them a suitable research environment (e.g. laboratory, space, facilities and personnel) in the same way that a full-time researcher would be able to do.
Selection policy requires that the applicant (host researcher) and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan.
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution.
The host researcher must choose the review section in which the application will be screened from the FY2027 Review Section Table, referring to the FY2027 Review Section Set.

The host institution's application must be sent to the president of JSPS by the application deadline for the programme, verified as approved by the head of the institution and confirmed that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved.
Before sending the application, the institution must check the 'List of Applications' on the JSPS Electronic Application System to verify that the registered information is correct.
A Research Proposal Document (S-2) must be completed jointly by the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate.
A Fellow's Curriculum Vitae (S-3) must be completed by the candidate.
scholarships.duration: 14 to 60 days
scholarships.application_period: FY2027 2nd recruitment: host-institution submissions to JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027; selection results published in early August 2027; periods for arrival in Japan 1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028. The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before each JSPS deadline.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.

Complete the Bachelor's degree and upload the diploma before 1 December 2026

Pay the revised first-year invoice, approximately EUR 16,500, before 1 July 2027 after accepting the scholarship

scholarships.title: Embassy Science Fellowship (ESF-NL) 2027
scholarships.description: This Call for proposals is open to all PhD graduates at any of the following research organisations and to 'lectoren' and senior researchers of universities of applied sciences:
scholarships.deadline: 10 September 2026 before 14:00:00 CEST - Deadline for proposals. Proposals submitted after the deadline will not be taken into consideration by NWO.
scholarships.deadline_display: 10 September 2026 before 14:00:00 CEST - Deadline for proposals. Proposals submitted after the deadline will not be taken into consideration by NWO.
eligibility: Be a PhD graduate at a listed research organisation: a Dutch university or university of applied sciences, a university medical centre, a KNAW or NWO institute, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics, Naturalis Biodiversity Center, ARCNL, the Princess Máxima Center, IHE Delft Institute for Water Education, or a TO2 institution
Be a 'lecten' or senior researcher at a university of applied sciences
Have an employment contract running at least until the end of the fellowship period
Researchers who have not yet obtained their PhD but whose PhD date is fixed may apply, provided the degree is obtained at the start of the fellowship
Apply for no more than one of the 12 selected positions
Be available during the fellowship period of 1 March 2027 to 29 February 2028
benefits: Grant of up to EUR 30,000 for the fellowship
Funding for international travel in economy class
Funding for research expenses, including domestic travel, representation and meetings
Replacement grant to cover the applicant's work at home
The host mission helps with accommodation and a place to work
Practical experience in a diplomatic context and a contribution to Dutch foreign policy
requirements: Submit the complete application in the Isaac application and reporting system
Create an Isaac account at least one workday in advance if you do not have one
Use the current budget form: on 12-08-2026 the budget form was replaced with a new version
State in the motivation letter which fellowship you are interested in, why you are suitable, what value you bring, and your availability between 1 March 2027 and 29 February 2028
State your approach to involving relevant local partners and stakeholders in the research
Do not mention h-indexes, journal impact factors or any other indicator of general journal or publisher reputation
Submit before the deadline, since late proposals will not be considered
scholarships.duration: 1 to 3 months of secondment to a Dutch diplomatic mission, within the fellowship period 1 March 2027 to 29 February 2028
scholarships.application_period: 2027 cycle: informative webinar 2 July 2026, proposal deadline 10 September 2026 14:00 CEST, decision by November 2026, fellowship period 1 March 2027 to 29 February 2028
scholarships.selection_notes: Proposals are assessed against three weighted criteria: quality and motivation of the applicant (40%), match between the applicant and the assignment as formulated by the mission (40%), and feasibility (20%). Because of the expertise on the assessment committee and the small size of the grant, NWO applies Article 2.2.4 second subsection of the NWO Grant Rules 2024 and assesses proposals without involving referees. The assessment consists of an assessment committee meeting in October 2026 and decision-making by the NWO Executive Board in November 2026.
scholarships.program_type: Government-funded research secondment fellowship placing researchers at Dutch diplomatic missions abroad
scholarships.name: Embassy Science Fellowship (ESF-NL) 2027

scholarships.title: KB Fellowship at NIAS
scholarships.description: The Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study offers temporary fellowships at an intellectual haven to a diverse year group of international scientists, writers, journalists and artists.
eligibility: Be a scholar with at least three years of research experience after obtaining your PhD, measured on the closing date of the call; institutional affiliation is not required
Be a creative practitioner with at least three years of independent practice since graduating, or equivalent experience; affiliation is not required
Be proposing a project that relates to the KB research agenda or extends its scope
Be able to be at NIAS four days a week for the whole semester
Have an excellent command of spoken and written English, as the working language at NIAS is English
requirements: Submit the application through the online application form
Provide a project proposal of no more than 1,500 words excluding the bibliography
Provide an academic or artistic CV of no more than four pages
Provide a statement of no more than 300 words
Be available at NIAS four days a week from the start to the end of the semester
Be willing to publish resulting publications under the Creative Commons CC BY 4.0 licence
scholarships.duration: Five months, from September to January
scholarships.application_period: Annual; the 2027-2028 call opens 15 January 2027 and closes 15 March 2027 at 12.00 noon CET, for a September-to-January fellowship
scholarships.selection_notes: NIAS first checks all applications for eligibility. A ranking committee appointed by the KB then ranks eligible candidates, giving preference to proposals that bring new questions or unexpected dimensions to the KB research agenda. The KB returns its ranking to NIAS, where the Fellowship Advisory Committee assesses it with a view to a cohort balanced in discipline, location, career stage and gender, and advises the NIAS Director, who makes the final decision.
scholarships.program_type: Residual research fellowship at a national advanced-study institute, funded jointly by NIAS and the National Library of the Netherlands
scholarships.name: KB Fellowship at NIAS

scholarships.title: Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship
scholarships.description: Fellowship at NIAS for researchers in the field of applied monetary economics, macro-economics or public finance
eligibility: Have a minimum of three years of post-PhD academic experience
Be based in the Netherlands or abroad
Work in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics, macroeconomic policy, public finance or public finance policy
Be a prominent, leading mid- to late-career researcher, or a promising early-career talent, in the Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation's priority fields
Have a good command of English, the working language at NIAS
Be willing and able to be present at NIAS four working days per week for the duration of the semester
requirements: Submit the application through the online application form
Keep the project proposal to no more than 1,500 words including footnotes, excluding references and abstract
Provide an up-to-date CV
Reflect in the proposal on how the research would benefit from and contribute to the multidisciplinary NIAS research community
Be present at NIAS four working days per week for the duration of the semester
scholarships.duration: 5 to 10 months, as either a five-month or a ten-month semester
scholarships.application_period: Annual; the published 2027-2028 call ran from 15 January to 13 April 2026, one five-month and one ten-month fellowship awarded per academic year
scholarships.selection_notes: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation gives particular priority to researchers with an outstanding record in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics or public finance. Applicants are encouraged to reflect on the collaborative and multidisciplinary environment at NIAS and to consider how their research might both benefit from and contribute to the NIAS research community and beyond.
scholarships.program_type: Residual research fellowship in economics at a national advanced-study institute, funded by the Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation
scholarships.name: Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship

scholarships.title: Eric Bleumink Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Eric Bleumink Fellowship is a University of Groningen grant for nationals of a listed group of countries who hold provisional or unconditional admission to a one or two year master's programme starting in September. The grant covers tuition fee, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance. It is nomination-based: the University of Groningen's Admission Office decides which admitted applicants are nominated, so there is no direct scholarship application. The University of Groningen states that a considerable number of students apply each year while it can issue only a limited number of grants.
eligibility: Have received provisional or unconditional admission for a master programme before February; only then are applicants considered for a grant
Have excellent academic performance, preferably to be confirmed by letters of recommendation
Have excellent grades during their bachelor/undergraduate studies
Have excellent English language proficiency, in accordance with the admission requirements of the program of choice
Be available for the whole period of the programme and be able to take part in the entire programme
Be in good health, so that health insurance in the Netherlands can be arranged
Hold the nationality of a country appearing in Appendix 1
Have no other means of financing the study in question
scholarships.duration: 1 or 2 year master's degree programme, starting in September only
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle tied to master's admission for a September start; master's applications to be completed before 1 December and admission offers received before February
scholarships.selection_notes: The University of Groningen's Admission Office, in consultation with the Admission Boards of its faculties, determines which applicants are nominated. A considerable number of students apply each year while the University can issue only a limited number of grants.
scholarships.program_type: Master's scholarship grant awarded by the university, nomination-based
scholarships.name: Eric Bleumink Fellowship

scholarships.title: KITLV Visiting Fellowship
scholarships.description: The KITLV Visiting Fellowship is a three month funded research stay at the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV) in Leiden for researchers who hold a PhD in the social sciences and/or humanities and are not tax residents of the Netherlands. Fellows work on a publication or research project of their own choice in Southeast Asian or Caribbean Studies and do not need a university or research institute affiliation. The offer covers a return economy air or train fare, reimbursement of accommodation costs in Leiden up to EUR 2,000 per month against proof of payment, and a case-by-case monthly compensation for higher living costs. It is explicitly not a salaried position and fellows are expected to have a steady income during the stay.
eligibility: Have a PhD in the Social Sciences and/or Humanities
Carry out research in the field(s) of Southeast Asian and/or Caribbean Studies
Are interested to carry out their desired research in the Netherlands
Are prepared to be based at KITLV during the entire period of the fellowship
Are not a (tax) resident of The Netherlands
Have a steady income for the period of the Visiting Fellowship
No affiliation at a university or research institute is required
requirements: Candidates are invited to send in a proposal of the work they wish to carry out while at KITLV.
scholarships.duration: 3 months
scholarships.application_period: Open Call, selection twice a year. Eight three-month fellowships are available each year across four periods: March-May, June-August, September-November and December-February. The next call is published in September 2026 and closes 14 October 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is based on the submitted application documents only and no interviews are held. Applications are assessed by a rotating committee composed of KITLV staff. For the 2026 call KITLV aimed to inform all applicants by the end of April. Note: KITLV states it will not review any proposals before submission and/or the deadline.
scholarships.program_type: Funded visiting research fellowship (three month research stay)
scholarships.name: KITLV Visiting Fellowship

scholarships.title: Tilburg University Waiver
scholarships.description: The Tilburg University Waiver halves the institutional tuition fee for up to 21 non-EEA international applicants each year, as part of the university's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion commitment. It applies to all regular one-year Master's programmes starting in September 2027, with the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence as an explicit exception; Research Master's and Pre-Master's students are not eligible. Applicants must have completed their most recent degree in a designated country and must not already hold any other tuition-fee waiver. If more eligible applicants apply than there are waivers, recipients are chosen by random lottery, and outcomes are notified by 1 June 2027.
eligibility: Hold a non-EEA nationality
Have completed, or be due to complete before the start of the Master's program, your most recent degree in one of the designated eligible countries
It must be your first Master's program at Tilburg University
Submit a complete application for a regular one-year Master's program starting in September 2027 by April 1, 2027
Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application form by April 1, 2027
Not hold any other tuition-fee waiver; the waiver cannot be combined with any other scholarship covering all or part of tuition
Not apply to a Research Master's program
Not be enrolled in, or have been enrolled in, a Pre-Master's program at Tilburg University
scholarships.duration: One year of tuition for a regular Master's programme; the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence is also eligible
scholarships.application_period: Annual for the September intake. The current cycle is the 2027-2028 academic year (21 waivers), applications open now and close 1 April 2027, with outcomes by 1 June 2027. Waivers are not available for the February intake.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection takes place by random lottery if more eligible applicants apply than waivers available. Only applicants who are conditionally or unconditionally admitted to a Master's programme are included in the draw, so the programme application must be submitted in good time. A waiver becomes effective only after unconditional admission has been confirmed. If fewer than 21 waivers are accepted, the remaining awards are assigned by lottery to non-EEA applicants who submitted the form before 1 April 2027 and hold conditional or unconditional admission by 1 June 2027.
scholarships.program_type: Partial tuition-fee waiver awarded by the university (DEI scheme), allocated by lottery among eligible admitted applicants
scholarships.name: Tilburg University Waiver

scholarships.title: Radboud Scholarship Programme
scholarships.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a highly selective Radboud University scheme for talented, highly motivated non-EU/non-EEA students with outstanding study results, covering English-taught Master's programmes. A scholarship reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 (the university notes the amount is to be confirmed) instead of an illustrative EUR 19,000, and additionally covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs. Costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered. A maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027/2028, allocated across six faculties, and selection is based on academic excellence, ambition and the quality of two reference letters.
eligibility: Hold a non-EU/non-EEA passport
Are not eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons

Have (will obtain) a Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands, have no degrees achieved in the Netherlands and did not receive any previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded, provided they are part of the Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands)
Meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice
Have been fully admitted to the English-taught Master's programme starting 1 September 2027 as stated in the formal letter of admission
Are able to comply with the conditions for obtaining a visa for the Netherlands
Are enrolled at Radboud University as a full-time student for the academic year and Master's programme for which the scholarship will be awarded
requirements: hold a non-EU/non-EEA passport.
meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice.
have been fully admitted to the English-taught Master's programme starting 1 September 2027 as stated in the formal letter of admission.
scholarships.duration: Nominal duration of the Master's programme
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle for the September 2027 intake. OSIRIS submission by 31 January 2027 23:59 CET, complete application by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET, decision before mid-April 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is by the selection committee of the faculty applied to and is based on academic excellence (outstanding study results, relevancy of the previous degree, ranking of the university where the previous degree was obtained), ambition (quality and relevance of the motivation letter, promise based on previous achievements, life experience and extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering) and references (quality of two reference letters, preferably two academic references). Faculties may apply additional criteria and some study programmes hold interviews. Admission to the Master's programme is a separate process and does not imply selection for the scholarship.
scholarships.program_type: Partial tuition-fee scholarship awarded by the university, merit-based
scholarships.name: Radboud Scholarship Programme

scholarships.title: Erasmus University Rotterdam Scholarships
scholarships.duration: 1-2 years depending on programme
scholarships.name: Erasmus University Rotterdam Scholarships

scholarships.title: University of Amsterdam Scholarships
scholarships.description: The University of Amsterdam runs several scholarship programmes for talented and motivated international students, published from one official Fees and funding hub. The flagship is the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship for outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA planning a Master's programme at the UvA. Each faculty also runs its own scholarships for international Master's students, covering Economics and Business, Humanities, Law, Science and Social and Behavioural Sciences, and a separate set of Bachelor's scholarships exists. The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship equals the tuition fee but the UvA states it cannot be used as a partial tuition waiver, so the recipient still pays the full tuition, payable in monthly instalments. Amounts are set annually and are published by each faculty.
eligibility: For the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship: hold a non-EU/EEA nationality and plan to do a Master's programme at the University of Amsterdam
Be an outstanding student with excellent study results; the UvA states the programme is highly selective and that only applicants with excellent study results and motivation might be eligible
Meet the admission requirements of the chosen UvA degree programme
Satisfy the additional criteria set by the specific faculty scheme, which differ per faculty
scholarships.duration: 1-3 years depending on programme
scholarships.application_period: Annual. The main Amsterdam Merit Scholarship round opens at the beginning of October with a 15 January deadline and results at the end of April; individual faculties publish their own rounds, amounts and deadlines, and amounts are published in late autumn.
scholarships.selection_notes: The UvA describes the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship as highly selective and states that only applicants with excellent study results and motivation might be eligible to receive it. Selection, award volumes and assessment criteria are set and published by each faculty, and the Faculty of Science states it selects in March and informs applicants in April.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship programmes for international students (Amsterdam Merit Scholarship plus faculty-specific schemes)
scholarships.name: University of Amsterdam Scholarships

scholarships.title: Tulī Takes Flight Scholarships
scholarships.description: Tulī Takes Flight scholarships are funded by the New Zealand Ministry of Education and administered by the Pacific Education Foundation to reduce financial barriers to tertiary study and vocational training for Pacific people. They form part of the government's gesture of goodwill and reconciliation to Aotearoa Pacific communities following its 2021 apology for the Dawn Raids. Awards can be made for either vocational or academic study and can run for one, two or three years. For the 2027 round the Ministry states applications are closed and outcomes will be notified by 18 March 2027; a new annual round is expected to open in the same late-summer window each year.
scholarships.deadline: Applications for the 2027 round are closed. The Ministry's official page states "Applications for the 2027 round are now closed" and "You will be notified of the outcome of your application by 18 March 2027". The round closes annually on 30 September at 11.59pm; no date for the next still-applicable round is published on the page as at 2026-10-04.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications for the 2027 round are closed. The Ministry's official page states "Applications for the 2027 round are now closed" and "You will be notified of the outcome of your application by 18 March 2027". The round closes annually on 30 September at 11.59pm; no date for the next still-applicable round is published on the page as at 2026-10-04.
eligibility: Have enrolled or be in the process of enrolling into full-time training or study with a tertiary provider in New Zealand; part-time study is not eligible
Be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident
Have lived in New Zealand for the last three years
Be of indigenous Pacific cultural heritage
Have completed NCEA 3 (or equivalent) and be 16 years or over by the time the course starts; or, if already out of secondary school, be 18 years or over

For a new to study or training award: not have done more than half a year of equivalent full-time tertiary education, meaning 0.5 EFTS or 60 credits at Level 3 or above on the NZQA framework, including equivalent tertiary education in any country
For a continuing study award: have successfully completed at least 1 year of study, or be expecting to enter a second or subsequent year of training or study
benefits: Tuition fees covered for full-time study
Course materials and equipment costs covered
Help with living costs including accommodation, transport and childcare
scholarships.duration: 1, 2 or 3 years per award
scholarships.application_period: Annual round for study in the following year. The 2027 round closed at 11.59pm on Wednesday 30 September 2026, with outcomes notified by 18 March 2027. The next round is expected to follow the same pattern but no date is published yet.
scholarships.selection_notes: Decisions about awarding the scholarships are made by the Pacific Education Foundation Board and are final. The Board informs all applicants by email of the outcome and provides general feedback, but is unable to give individual feedback on applications. A quarter of scholarships are targeted to priority pathways.
scholarships.program_type: Government-funded scholarship for Pacific students, administered by the Pacific Education Foundation
scholarships.name: Tulī Takes Flight Scholarships

scholarships.title: New Zealand Space Scholarship
scholarships.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students a fully supported three-month internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, working alongside scientists and engineers on space missions and research. Applications for the 2027 scholarship opened on 1 October 2026 and the internship runs from July to September 2027. The scholarship covers return economy flights to the United States, accommodation, a daily living allowance and reasonable travel-related expenses including insurance support where applicable. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, and hold at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.
eligibility: Be a New Zealand citizen (NASA requirement)
Be aged 18 years or older
Be enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities
Hold a minimum GPA equivalent of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, with New Zealand grades converted to the US GPA scale
Be proficient in written and spoken English (NASA requirement)
Be available to undertake the internship in person from July to September 2027 (dates subject to change)
Be willing to undergo any required health and security checks for travel to the United States and entry into US federal facilities
Be eligible for a J1 or F1 visa and understand the applicable visa conditions
Be able to obtain appropriate travel and medical insurance
Not currently hold, and never have held, citizenship in a country listed on NASA's Designated Countries List
scholarships.duration: 3-month internship, July to September 2027 (dates subject to change)
scholarships.application_period: The 2027 round opened on 1 October 2026 and is open now. The internship itself runs July to September 2027. No closing date is published on the official page.
scholarships.selection_notes: The scholarship is highly competitive. Candidates are assessed on academic excellence, relevance of experience to JPL projects, personal qualities and self-management, and commitment to contributing to JPL and New Zealand's space sector. Final shortlisted candidates are submitted to JPL for final selection, so MBIE's assessment is not the final word.
scholarships.program_type: Government-funded postgraduate research internship placement abroad (not a degree programme)
scholarships.image_alt_text: New Zealand Ministry of Education (Te Tāhuhu o te Mātauranga)
scholarships.name: New Zealand Space Scholarship

scholarships.title: Aotearoa New Zealand Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowships — New Zealand Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowship
scholarships.description: The Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowship is the early-career scheme within the Aotearoa New Zealand Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowships, administered by Royal Society Te Apārangi on behalf of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment. It funds employed researchers within 0-4 years of research experience after PhD conferral to build the foundations of an independent research career. Around 20 fellowships are awarded each year, each worth NZ$820,000 over four years, made up of salary contribution, institutional overheads and research expenses. The scheme replaced the previous Rutherford Discovery, Rutherford Foundation and James Cook Research Fellowships.
scholarships.deadline: For the 2026 round the on-line portal opened Friday 1 May 2026 and closed at 2.00pm NZST on Thursday 9 July 2026; the Society has not published the opening or closing dates for the next round.
scholarships.deadline_display: For the 2026 round the on-line portal opened Friday 1 May 2026 and closed at 2.00pm NZST on Thursday 9 July 2026; the Society has not published the opening or closing dates for the next round.
eligibility: Within 0-4 years of research experience after PhD conferral
Based at a New Zealand host research organisation registered in the on-line application system
May make only one Tāwhia te Mana Fellowship application per funding round
A former successful applicant may not apply for a second Fellowship in the same scheme
A previous holder of a Rutherford Discovery Fellowship or the James Cook Research Fellowship may not apply for an equivalent Tāwhia te Mana Fellowship
Not eligible if the applicant has previously received substantial research grant funding in a leadership capacity, such as principal investigator on a Marsden Fast Start or Endeavour grant
benefits: NZ$820,000 total value over four years

Endorsed and nominated by the National Commission for UNESCO of their country
Meets the field-specific qualifications in Annex III for the chosen project
Some projects are restricted to candidates from particular regions - check Annex III and Annex IV
benefits: Free tuition for six months plus university facilities
Monthly allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc) or PLN 2,200 (MSc)
One-time special allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc) or PLN 2,200 (MSc) on arrival
International travel to and from Poland covered by UNESCO
Health insurance taken out and paid for by UNESCO

scholarships.title: Erasmus+ Programme
scholarships.description: Erasmus+ is the European Union programme supporting projects, partnerships, events and mobility in education, training, youth and sport. Its higher education strand is mainly a student exchange programme that also covers placements in companies abroad and academic staff mobility. Students can spend part of their studies in another country without additional tuition, registration or examination costs and receive a scholarship covering living costs, with the period and courses recognised by their home institution. In Poland the programme is implemented by the Foundation for the Development of the Education System, appointed as the Polish National Agency.
scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published on study.gov.pl or on the Polish National Agency's site. Erasmus+ calls are announced nationally by the Foundation for the Development of the Education System and by each sending or receiving university, so the deadline varies by institution and call.
scholarships.deadline_display: No central deadline is published on study.gov.pl or on the Polish National Agency's site. Erasmus+ calls are announced nationally by the Foundation for the Development of the Education System and by each sending or receiving university, so the deadline varies by institution and call.
eligibility: Enrolled student or employed staff member at a participating higher education institution
Sending and receiving institutions must hold an inter-institutional Erasmus+ agreement
Mobility must be within the Erasmus+ Programme Countries or an eligible Partner Country
The home institution must recognise the study period and the courses completed abroad
benefits: No additional tuition, registration or examination costs at the receiving institution
Graduate mobility for practical training or work placement
requirements: Applications are made through the sending university, not directly to the National Agency
The Learning Agreement must be completed for the period before mobility starts
The home institution must accept the period abroad and credit the courses completed
scholarships.duration: Not specified on the official pages read; mobility periods are agreed bilaterally between the sending and receiving institutions
scholarships.application_period: Continuous programme with institution-level calls announced each academic year; no single national window is published
scholarships.selection_notes: Not published on the official pages read: Erasmus+ selection is run at institutional level, so criteria and weighting vary by university. The official page confirms only that mobility must be agreed between the institutions and recognised by the home institution.
scholarships.program_type: EU-funded academic mobility programme
scholarships.image_alt_text: Study in Poland (study.gov.pl) portal logo: red outlined map-pin/book mark containing the words "READY, STUDY Go! POLAND"

scholarships.description: Jeffrey Hanafie. Student from Indonesia studying robotics in Warsaw, scholar of Łukasiewicz Programme.
