scholarships.title: CEEPUS Exchange Programme
scholarships.description: CEEPUS is a multilateral exchange programme with Central and Eastern Europe, organised as a transnational university network of subject-specific networks, each containing at least three higher education institutions from at least two different CEEPUS contractual countries. Exchanges last 3 to 10 months. Within a network, incoming students are exempted from paying tuition fees and receive a comprehensive grant from the host country sized according to local living costs. Eligibility requires CEEPUS-country nationality and participation through a member institution.
eligibility: National of a CEEPUS country
Enrolled at a higher education institution that participates in a CEEPUS network
Applying within a network of at least three institutions from at least two different CEEPUS contractual countries
requirements: Home institution must participate in a CEEPUS network
Apply through the network, not through a central scholarship portal
Check the current network list on ceepus.info
scholarships.duration: 3 to 10 months of exchange within a CEEPUS network
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycles. The network application round for 2027/28 closed on 30 November 2026 (signed letters by 15 December 2026); student scholarship calls follow the network rounds and are announced per network.
scholarships.selection_notes: Not published on the pages read; CEEPUS selection runs at network level.
scholarships.program_type: Multilateral university exchange programme
scholarships.name: CEEPUS Exchange Programme

scholarships.title: SAF Merit Scholarship
scholarships.description: The SAF Merit Scholarship is a top-tier military scholarship offered by MINDEF/SAF to Singapore citizens and permanent residents intending to take up citizenship. It pays full tuition fees and other approved academic charges, a monthly salary for the duration of studies, maintenance and other allowances, return airfare and a one-time sponsorship for summer exchange programmes, and can sponsor up to six years of studies inclusive of a Master's degree. Recipients must qualify for and excel in Officer Cadet School and serve a six-year bond in MINDEF/SAF after graduation.
eligibility: Singapore citizen or permanent resident intending to take up Singapore citizenship
Good GCE 'A' Level or International Baccalaureate results, Polytechnic Diploma (with Merit) or equivalent
Good co-curricular activities (CCA) records
Strong leadership qualities
Qualify for and excel in Officer Cadet School
Possess a strong interest in a military career
All MINDEF/SAF scholarships are open for application to both genders
requirements: Applicants are expected to apply to universities themselves, as admission is dependent on individual merit
Arrange to sit necessary pre-admission tests such as SAT where required
Obtain approval to study at the chosen local or overseas university
Male recipients disrupt for studies only after being commissioned as an officer
Law graduates will not be called to the Bar while serving in MINDEF/SAF
scholarships.duration: Sponsorship for up to 6 years of studies, inclusive of a Master's if applicable; FAQ states a stipulated study period of four years
scholarships.application_period: Male applicants: 1 September to 30 April of the following year. Female applicants: 1 April to 31 August.
scholarships.selection_notes: The selection board looks for leadership potential, sound character, commitment to serve Singapore and Singaporeans, and a keen interest in a challenging and fulfilling profession with MINDEF/SAF. For females there are up to three rounds of interviews, with the final round assessing military performance in Officer Cadet School before the scholarship is confirmed.
scholarships.program_type: Military undergraduate scholarship for SAF officer cadets
scholarships.name: SAF Merit Scholarship

scholarships.title: MHA Civilian Scholarship
scholarships.description: The MHA Civilian Scholarship is offered by the Ministry of Home Affairs to Singapore citizens and permanent residents for a civilian appointment in the Home Team, with Generalist and Specialist tracks in Commercial Affairs, Intelligence, Internal Security and Psychology. It covers tuition fees and other approved charges, a monthly overseas or local maintenance allowance including accommodation, a pre-studies allowance, and return economy class airfare for selected tiers. The scholarship may be awarded at the Singapore Government Scholarship, Local Merit Scholarship or Home Team Local Study Award tier, and carries a bond of four years for local studies.
eligibility: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who is intending to take up Singapore Citizenship
Strong leadership qualities and potential
Strong interest in safeguarding the safety and security of Singapore
Good academic and Co-Curricular Activities (CCA) records
GCE A-Levels, International Baccalaureate, Polytechnic, NUS High School or other high school diploma/certificate
Current undergraduate students who are not in the final year of studies may apply for the mid-term scholarship
requirements: Indicate a preferred career track (Generalist or one of the Specialist tracks) at the point of interview
If converting from Civilian to Uniformed scheme or changing specialisation after award, strong justifications must be provided and MHA will consider the appeal case by case
Study at a local or overseas university in most disciplines except medicine, dentistry and architecture
Law degree holders will not be called to the Bar while serving in the Home Team
scholarships.duration: Full-time undergraduate degree; bond of 4 years for local studies, 5 years for studies in non-English speaking countries and 6 years for studies in English speaking countries
scholarships.application_period: Applications for the 2027 intake are open until 15 March 2027
scholarships.selection_notes: There is no difference in promotion prospects between overseas and local scholars; promotions are based on potential and performance in service. Applicants must indicate their preferred specialisation track at interview.
scholarships.program_type: Civilian public service undergraduate scholarship, Generalist and Specialist tracks
scholarships.name: MHA Civilian Scholarship

scholarships.title: The Singapore Police Force Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Singapore Police Force Scholarship is a uniformed scholarship offered jointly by the Public Service Commission and the Singapore Police Force, described on the official page as 'one of the most prestigious scholarships awarded by the Public Service Commission'. It is awarded to candidates with outstanding leadership qualities, impeccable integrity and a strong interest in policing. It pays tuition fees and other approved charges, a monthly maintenance allowance including accommodation, a pre-studies allowance, return economy class airfare for overseas study, National Service disruption support and a full salary including bonuses for the duration of studies, against a bond of four to six years.
eligibility: Be a Singapore Citizen
Strong leadership qualities and potential
Keen interest in serving in the Singapore Police Force
Outstanding academic and Co-Curricular Activity (CCA) records
GCE A-Levels, International Baccalaureate, Polytechnic, NUS High School or other high school diploma/certificate
Excel in Officer Cadet School
requirements: Female applicants must submit earlier to have enough time to prepare for enlistment into Basic Military Training
Study at a local or overseas university in most disciplines except medicine, dentistry and architecture
Law degree holders will not be called to the Bar while serving in SPF
Be assigned to a uniformed career track in the Singapore Police Force
scholarships.duration: Full-time undergraduate degree; bond of 4 years for local studies, 5 years for studies in non-English speaking countries and 6 years for studies in English speaking countries

scholarships.selection_notes: Awarded to candidates who have shown outstanding leadership qualities, possess impeccable integrity and have a strong interest in policing work to safeguard the nation. In the first 6 years of career, scholars are rotated through regular postings to acquire investigation acumen, policy conceptualisation skills and command and leadership abilities.
scholarships.program_type: Uniformed public service undergraduate scholarship for the Singapore Police Force
scholarships.name: The Singapore Police Force Scholarship

scholarships.title: PSC Scholarships
scholarships.description: The PSC Scholarships are the Singapore Government's premier merit-based undergraduate scholarships, awarded by the Public Service Commission for entry to the Singapore Public Service. Applicants may apply before beginning their degree or as mid-term applicants up to the penultimate year, and must be Singapore Citizens who demonstrate strong leadership qualities and potential with good academic and non-academic records. Value of award covers tuition fees and other approved charges, return airfare for overseas degrees, maintenance and other allowances, full salary including bonuses on the Uniformed Service track, and sponsorship of PSC development programmes and approved exchange or summer programmes.
eligibility: Be a Singapore Citizen
Demonstrate strong leadership qualities and potential
Present themselves as well-rounded individuals with good academic and non-academic records
Hold a GCE A-level, International Baccalaureate, NUS High School Diploma, Polytechnic Diploma with merit or other high school diploma or equivalent
For mid-term applicants: at least one semester of university results and application made before the final year of undergraduate study
For professional schemes with a tied agency: be undertaking an undergraduate degree relevant to that tied agency
requirements: The application must include an essay and a video interview alongside supporting documents
May apply before receiving final examination results, in which case a provisional offer may be made subject to confirmation
Study duration must stay within the published maximum, which varies by country of study
For mid-term applicants, tuition and compulsory fees incurred before the award are back paid but allowances only start from the point of award
scholarships.duration: Up to 3 years undergraduate degree in the UK (plus 1 to 2 additional years for a Master's), 4 years in the US (plus 1 to 2 years for a Master's), 1 year plus Master's years in Singapore, 2 years plus 2 years for a Master's in other countries
scholarships.application_period: Applications open and close on a single annual cycle; the 2027 cycle closes 15 March 2027
scholarships.selection_notes: Scholarship holders are described by PSC as a diverse group of outstanding young talents who are all-rounded and committed to serving Singapore, excelling in both academic and non-academic pursuits, possessing sound character and exemplifying the ethos of the Public Service. Shortlisted candidates are informed of further stages.
scholarships.program_type: Government undergraduate scholarship for the Singapore Public Service, three career tracks
scholarships.name: PSC Scholarships

scholarships.title: PSC Master's Scholarships
scholarships.description: The PSC Master's Scholarships are postgraduate awards for those who wish to pursue a Master's degree and a career in Public Administration and Sustainability in the Singapore Public Service. Applicants choose between the PSC Master's Scholarship and the PSC Master's Scholarship (Sustainability). The award covers tuition fees and other approved charges, return airfare for overseas degrees, maintenance and other allowances, and a series of sponsored development programmes including student exchange and summer opportunities. Holders serve a three-year bond and study for a maximum of two years in any country.
eligibility: Be a Singapore Citizen
Demonstrate strong leadership qualities and potential
Be well-rounded with good academic and non-academic records
Hold a GCE A-level, International Baccalaureate, NUS High School Diploma, Polytechnic Diploma or other high school diploma or equivalent, plus university results
Be in the final year of undergraduate studies, or a fresh graduate with no more than 3 years of working experience in the private or non-government sector only
Be prepared to start the Master's programme in the academic year immediately following the offer

For the Sustainability variant, intend to read a Master's in a field related to sustainability and circularity
Choose courses relevant to the Public Service and obtain PSC approval
MBA programmes are not allowed
Complete the online application with supporting documents, an essay and a video interview

scholarships.application_period: 2027 cycle: applications open and closing 15 March 2027
scholarships.selection_notes: On graduation, holders are emplaced on the Public Service Leadership Programme and developed for multi-sectoral or sectoral leadership positions. Sustainability variant holders take a first posting in a sustainability and circularity role.
scholarships.program_type: Government postgraduate scholarship for the Singapore Public Service, Public Administration track
scholarships.name: PSC Master's Scholarships

scholarships.title: MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term)

Applicants may be offered either an Education Merit Scholarship or Teaching Scholarship administered by the Public Service Commission, or a Teaching Award administered by MOE, and are considered for the full range. Scholars receive undergraduate tuition fees and other approved charges, a maintenance allowance, developmental programmes and approved student exchange, summer programmes and co-curricular activities, against a bond of four to six years depending on where they study.

scholarships.title: SMU Global Impact Scholarship Award

The published benefits, applying from Academic Year 2028-29, are a waiver of subsidised tuition fees for regular terms for up to 4 years, a S$5,000 annual living allowance, a S$14,000 GLOW grant for overseas exposure and community service, a S$1,800 computer allowance, a S$9,000 Enhanced Flexibility Grant and up to S$40,000 for an optional concurrent or sequential SMU Master's programme. Be applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU

scholarships.title: Temasek Undergraduate Overseas Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Overseas Scholarship is awarded to exceptional polytechnic graduates who show academic excellence, outstanding extracurricular involvement and a strong passion for STEM, to study a STEM undergraduate degree at an overseas university, with Medicine and Dentistry excluded. Temasek lists tuition and other compulsory fees for the whole course, a monthly living allowance, one-time relocation and pre-studies allowances, reimbursed application fees for up to five universities and visa fees, plus exchange programmes, internships and mentoring. Eligibility is capped by a Gross Monthly Household Income of S$15,000 or less at the point of admission, and graduates must serve a 4-year bond in a STEM-related role in Singapore or with a Singapore-headquartered company.

Declare Gross Monthly Household Income as part of the application

Complete a four-stage assessment process if shortlisted: an online psychometric and personality assessment, a remote on-demand video interview, a one-day in-person group assessment, and a final 60-minute structured interview

A provisional scholarship offer may be extended to a suitable applicant, subject to confirmation on release of the final cumulative GPA, examination results and acceptance into an overseas university. scholarships.title: AAUW International Fellowships
scholarships.description: AAUW's International Fellowships fund international women pursuing graduate study in STEM disciplines in the United States, with the intention of applying their expertise and leadership in service of their home countries. The programme has supported international women in full-time postgraduate study in the United States since 1917. scholarships.title: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)
scholarships.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). They pay a fixed grant of $8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on the duration of overseas study, and the programme states plainly that the award "is not all-inclusive" and is designed to cover only the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. In exchange, recipients commit to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation.
eligibility: U.S. citizens at the time of the national application deadline
A high school graduate, or have earned a GED
At least 18 years of age or older by the time the application is submitted
Planning an overseas program in an overseas destination outside of Western Europe, Canada, Australia, or New Zealand
Planning to study in an overseas destination of which they are not a citizen

Matriculated for the duration of their Boren Awards-funded program in an undergraduate or graduate degree program located within the United States and accredited by a body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education

Boren Scholarships applicants must be matriculated in an associate's or bachelor's degree program at the time of application and must remain matriculated in an undergraduate degree program; they may not graduate until the scholarship is complete

Boren Fellowships applicants may be matriculated in or applying to a graduate degree program, but Boren Fellows must be matriculated in a graduate degree program by the start date of the fellowship and may not graduate until the fellowship is complete

Eligible graduate degree programs include master's (MA, MS, MBA, LLM and others), juris doctor (JD), or doctoral (PhD, MD and others) programs; non-degree certificate programs are not eligible by themselves
requirements: Two letters of recommendation for Boren Scholarships (a third letter is optional); three letters of recommendation for Boren Fellowships, with at least one from a research advisor at the U.S. institution if a research component is proposed
Recommenders may be academic or professional contacts who know the applicant well; they may not be family or friends
Essay 1 - National Security, maximum 800 words, single-spaced
Essay 2 - Motivation and Public Service Careers, maximum 800 words for Boren Scholarships and 1000 words for Boren Fellowships, single-spaced
Study Plan Summary: maximum 250 words for each segment of the proposed overseas program, plus descriptions of alternate overseas destination programs
Weekly contact hours of formal language acquisition - the Boren Awards requires overseas programs contain at least 15-20 weekly language hours

An alternate study abroad program is required for applicants choosing an overseas destination marked with an asterisk (blue on the map) or for the languages Arabic, Mandarin or Russian; it is not required for Mandarin in Taiwan, Arabic in Morocco, or Language Flagship capstone applicants
Employment History: up to three jobs, each described in 50 to 100 words
Activities: up to three extracurricular activities, each described in 50 to 100 words
Language Self-Assessment in the online application, plus up to four additional languages studied or spoken
Up to three non-U.S. countries where you have lived, traveled or studied; up to five relevant honours and awards; optional list of up to five other scholarships applied for
Applicants must agree to the policies in the Submission Information section in order to actually submit
Boren Scholars whose airfare is funded by Boren must comply with the Fly America Act and send a photocopy of the passenger receipt page(s) to their airline to show compliance
All Boren-funded programs must include language study within a classroom as a core element for the duration of the grant
scholarships.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study; 25-52 weeks preferred; minimum 12 weeks for most applicants (8 weeks minimum for undergraduate STEM summer programmes).
scholarships.application_period: The 2027-2028 Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship application cycle is open as of 2026-10-01. National deadlines are January 20, 2027 (Fellowships) and January 27, 2027 (Scholarships), 5pm Eastern time. Selected applicants are notified in mid-to-late April. Campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that applicants are asked to respect.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by IIE-organized regional merit review panels made up of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The panels make recommendations on each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know must be stated in the essays and other application materials. Selection preference is given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.

scholarships.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (NSF GRFP)
scholarships.description: The NSF GRFP funds full-time graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM fields at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student. There is no post-graduate study service requirement, and fellows may transfer to a different institution after completion of the first fellowship year. Estimated 1,500 awards for the 2027 solicitation (NSF 26-526), pending availability of funds.
eligibility: At the time of submission, must be a U.S. citizen, national, or a permanent resident ("green-card" holder).
Must intend to enroll or be enrolled full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.
Must have declined any previously offered NSF Graduate Research Fellowship by the deadline (if applicable).

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program according to the institution's academic calendar; non-degree coursework must be clearly identified in the transcript and does not count toward this limit.
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
An eligible applicant can submit only one application per annual competition.

Fellowships may only be used for an eligible graduate degree program at a nonprofit academic institution accredited in, and having a campus located in, the U.S., its territories, possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
requirements: Prepare and submit the application in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov.
Create a Research.gov account to access the module.
Provide accurate personal information: full legal name, mailing address, permanent address, date of birth, high school location, and demographic information.
Select a level (Level 1 undergraduate, or Level 2 graduate) in the application.
Provide the list of institutions, enrollment status, enrollment dates and degree conferred (if applicable) for all degree-granting undergraduate and graduate institutions attended.
Provide significant academic honors, fellowships, scholarships, publications and presentations.
Select the Major Field of Study most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan; the Major Field of Study determines the application deadline and the reviewers.

Request reference letters in the GRFP Application Module and rank them in order of preference; three reference writer names and contact information are required, and two reference letters must be received by NSF.
Provide a Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement of a maximum of three pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Provide a Graduate Research Plan Statement of a maximum of two pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Reference letters are due before the NSF GRFP application deadlines, by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on the reference letter date in the Notice of Funding Opportunity.
All materials are submitted through the GRFP Application Module; emailed and/or physically mailed applications will not be accepted.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance with the format requirements; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted by the module.
scholarships.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
scholarships.application_period: The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August; applications for the 2027 competition close between October 19 and October 23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study, with reference letters due October 16, 2026. The module opened in time for the 2026 application cycle; the 2027 application deadlines were published August 25, 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.

scholarships.title: SA-TIED Request for Research Proposals: Public revenue mobilization; Poverty, inequality, and labour markets
scholarships.description: UNU-WIDER and the South African National Treasury invite proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa - Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme for research using South African tax administrative data. Accepted proposals are paid a research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000 on delivery of a working paper of 10,000 words or fewer, and the resulting papers are published in the SA-TIED research paper series. This is research funding rather than a degree scholarship: the deliverable is a policy paper, and the honorarium is expected to cover all expenses of the research.
scholarships.deadline: Closing date: 15 October 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2). Submit questions by 8 October 2026.
scholarships.deadline_display: Closing date: 15 October 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2). Submit questions by 8 October 2026.
eligibility: Proposals from individuals, groups of individuals, and non-profit organizations are welcome
Calls for South Africa-based and international researchers to submit proposals
Research must be conducted primarily, but not exclusively, using South African tax administrative data
Papers must be written in English and limited to 10,000 words or fewer, inclusive of text, tables, figures, footnotes and references
Papers may use either theoretical or empirical approaches
Researchers requiring access to National Treasury tax administrative datasets will be subject to agreed restrictions to preserve confidentiality
benefits: Publication of the resulting paper under UNU-WIDER copyright as an SA-TIED research paper
Possible publication in the WIDER Working Paper Series
Opportunity to participate in at least one knowledge-sharing event
Engagement with the SA-TIED communications team to develop a knowledge mobilization output such as a video, social media product, infographic, brief or blog
Inclusion in a research team building capacity in South African institutions, with UNU-WIDER seeking participation from Historically Disadvantaged Institutions
requirements: Proposals must be submitted electronically using the online form on the RfRP announcement page
Three forms are provided: one for individuals, one for groups of individuals, and one for non-profit organizations
Details such as address, gender, nationality and date of birth of all researchers involved must be entered on the form
The cover page, the proposal, and short CVs of five pages or less per researcher must be uploaded
The provided proposal template must be used for the proposal
No budget submission is required
scholarships.duration: Milestone-driven: first draft of papers due 8 June 2027 and final draft due 8 September 2027, with a work-in-progress workshop in June or July 2027
scholarships.application_period: Launched 17 September 2026; proposals close 15 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC+2. Questions on the proposal process were due by 8 October 2026, with queries and responses published on the RfRP announcement page and updated on a rolling basis.
scholarships.selection_notes: Each proposal is reviewed for scientific merit and feasibility and selected on three criteria: relevance to the research project, strength of empirical and policy contributions, and qualifications and experience of the research team. Preference is given to applications from early-career and female scholars and researchers from South Africa. Only the final decision on whether the proposal is accepted is communicated; applicants must not expect feedback on their proposals. Funding decisions are targeted for 9 November 2026.

scholarships.title: Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program
scholarships.degree: Not a degree programme - professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators
scholarships.description: The AEF Programme places accomplished K-12 STEM educators for eleven months in federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices, working on national education programmes and policy. Each fellow receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200, a travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency, an education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved professional development expenses, relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for fellows relocating from outside the Washington, DC area, and a health insurance stipend of up to $550 per month on an individual plan or $1,300 per month on a family plan. The DOE sponsors up to five congressional office placements. The programme is a single eleven-month appointment; it is not a degree award and involves no tuition.
scholarships.deadline: Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026. Online application opened August 3, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.
scholarships.deadline_display: Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026. Online application opened August 3, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.
eligibility: Be a U.S. citizen at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).

Have a minimum of five complete years of full-time classroom teaching experience prior to submitting the application; student teaching does not count toward this minimum full-time teaching requirement.

Have been teaching full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school for at least five of the last seven years in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) discipline; current employment may be as an educator or district official.
Be currently employed full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school or school district in the U.S.
Be able to provide a letter of recommendation from a school district official as one of their three required letters of recommendation.
Be able to obtain a leave of absence from teaching in order to participate in the program for the full eleven months.
benefits: Develops a professional development plan to guide individual professional development objectives outside host office responsibilities, with ongoing mentoring provided by the AEF Programme.
Access to a national network of education leaders and programmes.
Placement in a federal agency or U.S. Congressional office, with the DOE sponsoring up to five placements in congressional offices.
Up to ten personal days off per year and up to ten sick days off without reduction in the Fellow's stipend.
Fellows are connected with outgoing Fellows to help identify available housing in the Washington, DC area.
requirements: All applications must be completed online through the online application system.
Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements.
All applications, including recommendations, are due by the specified application deadline; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for evaluation and placement.
Materials uploaded into the application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Completion of all required fields, including contact information; education background (formal education and continuing education); teaching and professional experience; professional awards and recognition; citizenship status; interest in federal agency and/or Congressional office placement; and five essay questions.
Submission of three letters of recommendation online, including one recommendation letter from a school district official.
School district officials do not include department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals or vice-principals.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring their recommenders have the information needed to access the online Recommender form; requests can only be sent electronically through the online application system.
Provide proof of U.S. citizenship upon accepting a Fellowship offer.
Secure a leave of absence from teaching during the fellowship year.
Complete the eleven-month full-time appointment (mid-August through mid-July) in Washington, DC.
Meet the terms and conditions in the offer letter of appointment, including requirements for ethical conduct, and financial disclosure and conflict of interest.
Participate in the official professional development meetings, conferences and field trips organised for Fellows by the AEF Programme.
Have health care coverage during the fellowship appointment; Fellows are eligible to participate in the ORISE health insurance plan if they do not have other health insurance coverage.
Establish an individual Professional Development Plan for the year, which must be completed by early October.
Submit the requested written reports, presentations and surveys related to the Fellowship experience before the published deadlines.
Represent themselves as educators in a responsible and professional manner.
Only use the AEF Programme name or the Fellow's affiliation with the AEF Programme in an authorised manner.
In managing their responsibilities throughout the fellowship, give priority to the duties assigned to them by their host office.
scholarships.duration: Eleven months, mid-August through mid-July; the fellowship begins on the third Monday in August with the initial programme Orientation
scholarships.application_period: Online application opens August 3, 2026 and closes 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026 for the 2027-2028 programme. Semi-finalist notifications with travel arrangements are made by February 24, 2027; interviews in Washington, DC February 27 - March 1, 2027; finalist notifications March 9, 2027; congressional fellows placement interviews mid-June 2027; fellows arrive in Washington, DC mid-August 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review conducted by the AEF Programme to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation. Merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination by evaluators who must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies, applying pre-established criteria in four areas: the applicant's teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Programme. Sponsoring federal agencies then review the highly reviewed applications on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, the applicant's interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the interests of the host office, and quality of recommendations, and select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days of individual interviews and information sessions. Following interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements. Recruitment and selection is done without regard to race, gender, age, colour, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.

scholarships.title: Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) Program
scholarships.description: SCGSR provides supplemental awards to thesis-based doctoral students to conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist, in a DOE Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total for inbound and outbound transportation if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from their home graduate institution. The award does not pay tuition or fees, does not cover supplies and materials, and does not cover travel during the project; the student must remain enrolled full-time at their home institution and keep paying their own tuition. Successful applicants are considered guest scientists at the host laboratory, not employees.
scholarships.deadline: Applications are due November 4, 2026, at 5:00PM ET. This is 2026 Solicitation 2. The online application system closes at 5:00 PM Eastern Time and no additional materials will be accepted after it. 2027 Solicitation 1 dates are published but all tentative: application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027.
scholarships.deadline_display: Applications are due November 4, 2026, at 5:00PM ET. This is 2026 Solicitation 2. The online application system closes at 5:00 PM Eastern Time and no additional materials will be accepted after it. 2027 Solicitation 1 dates are published but all tentative: application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027.
eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age at the time of applying.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective.
At the time of application, applicants must have obtained the Ph.D. candidacy at their home institution, and must have established a defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.
The applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor must provide a Letter of Support.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
The Ph.D. degree program pursued must require a research thesis/dissertation, with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research.

Applicants must demonstrate that their graduate thesis research is in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.
The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating research scientist at a DOE laboratory and jointly developing the research proposal.
Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists may be from any of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities.
The duration of the proposed research to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
For applications in BES priority research areas, eligibility depends also on proximity between the applicant's university and the host DOE national laboratory.
Applicants must remain enrolled as a full-time graduate student in a qualified graduate program during the duration of the proposed SCGSR research project period at the host DOE laboratory/facility.
benefits: Access to DOE national laboratory expertise, user facilities, instrumentation and leadership-class computing systems.
Professional network expansion and access to scientific user facilities not available at most universities.
The possible opportunity for a short international research visit of 6 weeks maximum to an institution such as CERN or RIKEN, applied for after the award is received.
Weekly virtual office hours and application assistance workshops offered by the SCGSR Program.
A running list of collaborating laboratory scientists who are ready to work with SCGSR awardees.
requirements: All applications must be completed through the online application system; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for review.
Materials uploaded into the online application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Complete all required fields: Contact Information; Academic Information including Current Graduate Program Information; Citizenship or Permanent Residency Status; Professional Information such as Scientific Publications and Awards; Graduate Thesis Advisor and Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist Contact Information.

Submit the SCGSR research proposal, co-developed by the applicant and the collaborating DOE laboratory research scientist in consultation with the primary graduate thesis advisor, as a PDF through the online application.
Upload a PDF copy of current official graduate transcripts.
Provide official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as an official, signed letter from the Registrar's office or from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the applicant's academic department.
Submit two Letters of Support, one from the primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, both completed through the online application system.
Indicate in the online application system which Office of Science priority research area the proposed project aligns with.
List citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, in the appropriate section of the online application; do not submit supplemental materials.

The research proposal must address the stated aims in at least one of the SCGSR Priority Research Areas and must identify how the proposed research will take advantage of the DOE laboratory/facility's research capabilities and assets.

The proposed research must be an integral part of the applicant's overall doctoral thesis project and must be approved by the primary graduate thesis advisor, whose approval is made through the thesis advisor's Letter of Support.
Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline and become familiar with the application information requested.
scholarships.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility, within a project period bounded by published earliest and latest start dates
scholarships.application_period: 2026 Solicitation 2: online application opened August 12, 2026 and closes 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026. Offer notifications April 1 - 16, 2027. Proposed project periods may start as early as June 7, 2027 and must start no later than October 4, 2027. 2027 Solicitation 1 (tentative): application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027, offers September 2027, project periods starting November 2027 and ending no later than March 2028.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review. All eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by subject matter experts in the field of the proposed research, using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Two merit review criteria apply: (1) Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, asking whether the research is well-conceived with a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges, whether the method and approach are appropriate, whether the graduate student is sufficiently well prepared, and whether DOE laboratory resources are adequate, including whether necessary access to a scientific user facility has been secured by the collaborating scientist; and (2) Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, asking whether the proposed research can make a significant contribution to the applicant's thesis project and whether it will enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio. The application materials received, including the research proposal, provide the sole basis for evaluation. Participation in other DOE programmes is collected for internal purposes only and does not affect selection.

eligibility: To be eligible for a Chevening SIDS Scholarship, you must meet the standard eligibility criteria for Chevening, and be a citizen from one of the participating countries shown on the map on the official page.
Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.

If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country. This does not have to be the country of citizenship, but all applicants must show a clear intention to support their country of award.
Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after your scholarship ends.
Have at least two years' work experience, acquired after completing your undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours.

Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme. You must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you have not yet received your certificate; you will need the certificate by the time of your interview.
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses, and receive an unconditional offer from at least one by the deadline listed on the application timeline.

Applicants are required to study on courses that help to address a national development priority or capacity shortage. This includes courses relating to: human rights, democracy and the rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; supportive societies that help people lead peaceful and productive lives.
benefits: Full tuition fees for a one-year UK master's degree at the university of the scholar's choice
A monthly stipend, stated in the Final Award Letter, which Chevening says is intended to cover all living costs including accommodation
Return flights between the nearest airport in the home country and the nearest airport to the UK university, booked by Chevening's designated travel agency, where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Student visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge ('you don't need to pay the visa fee or the Immigration Health Surcharge')
Arrival allowance where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Departure allowance for scholars on a full award
requirements: Applications must be submitted through the Chevening online application system reached from your own country/territory page.
Opt in to be considered for the Chevening SIDS Scholarship within the standard Chevening Scholarship application.
Choose three different eligible UK master's degree courses in order of preference; duplicate courses at the same university cannot be considered.
Courses must be full-time, taught master's courses (not research-focused MRes programmes), based in the UK, starting in the autumn term (usually September/October) and lasting nine to twelve months.
Courses cannot be part-time, distance learning, a PhD or DPhil, or include more than one month of study outside the UK.
Provide the names and contact details of two referees in the application.
If shortlisted, upload two reference letters and your undergraduate degree certificate to the online application system no later than seven working days before your interview.
If successful at interview, submit at least one unconditional UK university offer by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
Apply for your own student visa; Chevening cannot apply on your behalf.
scholarships.duration: One-year master's degree in the UK
scholarships.application_period: Opened at 11:00 UTC on 4 August 2026 and closes at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026, for the 2027-28 Chevening Scholarship cycle. Studies begin in the UK in September/October 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are sifted against the eligibility criteria from October 2026, then independent reading committees assess all eligible applications from mid-October 2026 to January 2027. British embassies and high commissions produce shortlists and interview candidates in March to April 2027; results are announced from mid-June 2027. Applicants are assessed on leadership and influencing skills, the ability to build professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes, the reasons for the course and university choice (linked to UK priorities such as promoting growth and prosperity, building climate resilience, strengthening security and stability, and supporting development for more inclusive and effective societies), and a realistic short, mid and long-term career plan. Chevening states: 'The use of AI software to generate answers in Chevening applications is strictly prohibited.' The official page does not publish a separate SIDS selection weighting, so the SIDS element appears to be applied alongside the standard Chevening assessment.

eligibility: In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must be a citizen of and resident in one of the following countries at the point of application: Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, or Switzerland.
If you live in a European overseas territory, you may apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which you are a citizen.
Hold a postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field).
Have at least five years' relevant professional experience.

Be a mid-career professional with responsibilities for national or international security, and employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation.
Be working in a role with the potential to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness within their organisation and/or country.

General Chevening Fellowship criteria: be a citizen of a fellowship-eligible country or territory; demonstrate the potential to rise to a position of leadership and influence; demonstrate the personal, intellectual, and interpersonal attributes reflecting this potential; return to your country of citizenship (country of award) for at least one year after your fellowship ends; and meet all programme-specific fellowship eligibility requirements.

'If you do not already have the level of work experience required for your chosen fellowship programme, you will be unable to submit your application.'
You do not need to meet the work experience requirement in one period of employment; applicants can submit up to fifteen different employment periods.
benefits: Living expenses for the duration of the fellowship, including pre-arranged accommodation (the page states 'close to Oxford')
A monthly personal living allowance (stipend), confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Arrival allowance, paid on arrival in the UK
Departure allowance, where applicable to the fellowship type
A travel top-up allowance to attend events in London, for those in receipt of non-London stipends
A contribution of up to £75 for TB testing where this is required for the visa application
Reimbursement of the UK visa application fee for the fellow only
Reimbursement of the Immigration Health Surcharge, or a contribution towards travel insurance of up to £200

A research allowance as a contribution towards the cost of producing a thesis/dissertation where required for the course, or for conducting research associated with the programme, confirmed in the Final Award Letter
requirements: Meet the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria and all programme-specific requirements.
Apply through the Chevening online application system reached from the relevant European country/territory page.
Demonstrate five years' (7,200 hours) of relevant professional experience, calculated automatically from the weeks and hours you enter.

Ensure the employing organisation will release you for the six-week programme: 'it is your responsibility to ensure that they will release you if you are selected for a Chevening Fellowship. The British embassy/high commission or the Chevening Secretariat cannot intervene in this.'
Secure and comply with the UK entry clearance (visa) requirements applicable to the fellowship, including medical clearance.
On return of the acceptance form, agree to abide by the Chevening Fellowship terms and conditions for the duration of the award.

For this programme the assessment is against the general Chevening Fellowship criteria plus the published programme-specific requirements, and against the needs of a cohort drawn from the listed European countries. Chevening Fellowships are 'an important element of Britain's public diplomacy effort', and fellows are active in their field or subject. Chevening does not publish a separate scoring framework or interview format for this programme; applications for Chevening Scholarships follow the published sifting, reading committee, embassy shortlist and interview stages, while Chevening states that 'Application timelines for Chevening Fellowships vary.'

eligibility: At the time of application the applicant must be in the first year or the second year of a PhD program.
The field of study must be broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and address issues relevant to Canada's future.
The PhD research must align with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment.

The applicant must be one of the following: a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university; a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada; or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university.
Applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and a high level of intellectual ability, assessed across the whole application including transcripts and letters of recommendation.
Three letters of reference are required: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, and one from a referee outside academia.
There is no age limit to apply.
There is no requirement to be fluent in both official languages; applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English.
benefits: Annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Annual allowance of up to $20,000 for three years to support research, networking activities, and travel related to the doctoral work
Membership in the Foundation's community of Scholars, Fellows and Mentors
Lifelong membership in the Foundation's alumni network of more than 500 individuals
Mentorship and experiential learning: meetings, masterclasses, seminars and field experiences
requirements: Complete the eligibility screening form first; only applicants whose eligibility is confirmed gain access to the full application form
Applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed
Provide exactly three letters of reference — thesis supervisor, another academic referee, and a non-academic referee — no more and no fewer
Reference letters must be attached within the application file; they cannot be sent directly to the Foundation
The application form must be filled out in one language only, either English or French
Attend the mandatory information sessions offered in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026
Declare all additional sources of income each year, including other scholarships
scholarships.duration: Three-year program
scholarships.application_period: Applications open September 1, 2026 and close November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET. Two-step process: eligibility verification form must be submitted by October 2, 2026; references received by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET; mandatory information sessions in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on academic excellence, the clear alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes, the rigour of the research proposal, and the ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society. Only applications meeting the programme's eligibility criteria are assessed. Applicants who pass review are notified by email; all other applicants are informed at the end of the application review period. Applicants shortlisted in the selection process are invited to group meetings and individual interviews, conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference. scholarships.title: Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships
scholarships.deadline: No single calendar deadline is published. The Alberta Innovates programme page gives the due date as "Continuous" and states "This program is accepting applications on a seasonal basis. Intake Open Date is specific to each individual university; please contact your university of choice for deadline information." At the University of Calgary, "The Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 of each year" and "Deadlines vary by program"; the Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline is February 1.
scholarships.deadline_display: No single calendar deadline is published. The Alberta Innovates programme page gives the due date as "Continuous" and states "This program is accepting applications on a seasonal basis. Intake Open Date is specific to each individual university; please contact your university of choice for deadline information." At the University of Calgary, "The Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 of each year" and "Deadlines vary by program"; the Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline is February 1.
eligibility: Be a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident of Canada, or an international student.

Be enrolled as a full-time graduate student conducting full-time research at one of the participating institutions: Athabasca University, Concordia University of Edmonton, the University of Alberta, the University of Calgary or the University of Lethbridge.
Be conducting research in a key emerging technology area of information and communications technologies (ICT) or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies (AMM).

Be able to clearly articulate how your research aligns with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and how your research can produce potential environmental, health, economic, social and other impacts for Alberta.
At the University of Calgary: be applying to, or enrolled in, a thesis-based graduate degree programme.
At the University of Calgary: have submitted your admissions application and received your University of Calgary student number (UCID).
Meet the eligibility requirements in the terms of reference of the award at the time the award is paid, even if you did not meet them at the time you applied.
benefits: Scholarship funding enabling full-time graduate students to devote their full time to their academic studies
Published range of $12,000 to $31,000 per year, with terms of one to four years
At the University of Calgary: $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years

AGES top-up value of $18,000, available only to students who have applied for and been awarded both an Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarships award and an Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships award
Major Award top-up value of $12,000, available only to students who have applied for and been awarded both a major award and an Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships award
requirements: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for full descriptions and application details.
Submit your application to your institution; the applicant does not apply directly to Alberta Innovates.
At the University of Calgary: submit your admissions application and obtain your UCID before applying for the award.

At the University of Calgary: go to your Student Centre and click the link Apply for Graduate Funding in the Financial Aid section of your home screen, then select the Graduate Award Competition Application.
Only one application is required regardless of the number of awards you are applying for.
You may create one application per competition each year; if an application is incorrectly cancelled you must contact your graduate program to request reactivation.
Request and track your references before finalizing your application so they arrive before or by the application deadline.
New students can use their references from their admission application toward their scholarship application.

Reference letters used for admission may be used toward the scholarship competition as long as they were written within the eleven months prior to the Faculty of Graduate Studies' February 1 deadline.
Transcripts will be uploaded to the application by your program; scholarship requirements may differ from admission requirements.
Awards are based on merit; read and understand the terms of reference.
scholarships.duration: Terms vary from one to four years, depending on the recipient's time in the program. At the University of Calgary the published terms are $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years.
scholarships.application_period: Continuous at the funder level, with a seasonal intake at each institution. Alberta Innovates publishes the due date as "Continuous". At the University of Calgary the Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 each year, program deadlines vary and must be confirmed with Graduate Program Staff, and results for the Alberta Innovates competition are announced September to December. Awards are paid in the following academic year, with the majority starting in September.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is institution-specific. Each of the participating Alberta institutions has its own scholarship application and evaluation processes for students in full-time programmes, and Alberta Innovates directs students to their faculty of graduate studies for that information. At the University of Calgary the competition is merit-based and the applicant must be able to clearly articulate alignment with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and the potential impacts of the work for Alberta. For the Killam and Open Doctoral categories a first-class average is required, which at the University of Calgary is a grade point average of 3.5 or higher in the last two years of study, though that published indicator is stated for those categories rather than for the Alberta Innovates category. Successful students may normally hold one GAC scholarship per year across the Open Doctoral and Special Awards categories and will be awarded the highest-value scholarship for which they are eligible.

eligibility: I am less than 45 years old
I have proof of German language skills of at least B2 or a comparable level
I show above-average performance at school or in my studies
I am actively involved in voluntary work (politics, church, social association, sports, music, etc.)
I am politically interested
I support democracy, rule of law, and human rights

benefits: Monthly study scholarship of at most 992 €/month calculated according to BMBF guidelines, the level depending on the income and assets of the person responsible for support (page 'Finanzielle Förderung')

Study-cost flat rate of 300 €/month paid in addition to and independently of parents' income, intended for study-related expenditure that does not serve subsistence – for example learning and working materials (including books, hardware and software), language courses, relevant specialist conferences, congress visits and excursions
requirements: Applications can be submitted only through the HSS application portal; incomplete applications cannot be submitted
Scholarship holders receive an electronic confirmation that the application has been submitted; no separate confirmation email is sent
Applicants from countries where the HSS maintains a country office must contact that office first; where no office exists, the application is submitted directly via the online application portal
Selection presupposes a preliminary screening in the Institute for Talent Promotion and, for shortlisted candidates, an invitation to a selection meeting
The applicant is informed by email about the outcome and any next steps approximately four weeks after the application deadline
scholarships.duration: Study scholarship: normally up to the maximum funding period under BAföG, reviewed at the end of each funding year; doctoral scholarship: initially three years, extendable by six months on justified application and in exceptional cases up to a maximum of four years

scholarships.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung funds doctoral candidates from abroad who are admitted to a German university, paying 1,500 euros a month plus a supplement for statutory health insurance, together with an extensive political education programme. Applicants must have very good German skills (B2 accepted, also without a certificate, and required even when the dissertation is written in English), socio-political engagement, identification with the values of social democracy, an above-average and fast degree result, and a research project that makes a significant contribution to research. The scholarship does not have to be repaid.
eligibility: You come from abroad
You are admitted to doctoral study at a German higher education institution
You have very good German language skills
You are socio-politically engaged
You identify with the values of social democracy
You completed your degree with an above-average result and promptly
Your research project makes a significant contribution to research
With the exception of doctorates in medicine, doctoral projects in all subjects are funded
requirements: Applications must be submitted in German, because German language skills are a requirement for the scholarship
You must already be studying in Germany at the time of your application and be admitted to doctoral study
Proof of German language skills is absolutely necessary and must be provided; B2 is accepted also without a certificate
You have three weeks to submit your documents and up to six weeks for the expert opinions after the request
From the application to the decision it can take three to seven months

The foundation does not fund, outside an existing FES scholarship: short-term stays abroad, project proposals, short-term courses of study (fewer than three semesters, e.g. two-semester Master's programmes), research visits, trainee programmes, Studienkolleg, medical studies before the Physikum, doctorates and further medical training, pure final phases of a degree or doctorate, postdoc projects, physiotherapist training, purely foreign degree programmes outside the EU, part-time or extra-occupational study, language courses, internships and summer schools, and second degrees
scholarships.duration: As a rule three and a half years; in justified exceptional cases it can be granted for longer, but at the latest until the final examination
scholarships.application_period: Continuous/rolling: applications are accepted while the doctoral thesis can still be completed within the funding period, in principle from about two years before submission of the dissertation. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and the final decision is communicated at the latest one week after the relevant meeting.
scholarships.selection_notes: The FES checks the online application for formal and content criteria. In selecting, it particularly considers applications from people who are the first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, as well as from women and from students at universities of applied sciences and in MINT subjects. Suitable applicants are passed to a trust lecturer for a specialist interview that produces an opinion; shortlisted applicants then have a second interview with a member of the selection committee, whose opinion goes to the committee's meeting. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and decides on admission; the applicant is informed at the latest one week after the meeting. All applicants are informed by email at each stage. 'Above average' refers to the average grade in the subject at the university location or in the training occupation.

scholarships.title: France 2030 - PEPR GFM "Grands Fonds Marins" - Appel à projets - 2026
eligibility: The submission file must be deposited complete on the ANR submission site before the published closing date and time, and the administrative and financial document signed and stamped by each partner institution must be deposited at the date and time indicated in the AAP.
The project scientific document must imperatively follow the template published on the call website and be deposited in unprotected PDF format.
The project must have a duration of between 36 and 54 months.
The amount of aid requested must be between 0.8 M€ and 3 M€.
The coordinating institution must be a French higher education and research institution.

The beneficiaries of the aid are research organisations and higher education and research institutions; private institutions contributing to public-service missions in higher education and research under article L.732-1 of the Code de l'Education may be financed after ANR analysis, MESRE opinion and SGPI validation.
Companies and foreign institutions may be associated as partners but cannot receive funding for that participation.
The project must fit into one or several of the five PEPR GFM challenges (Défi 1 to Défi 5).
The project must require a wide interdisciplinary and/or transdisciplinary approach as defined in section 2.2 of the AAP.
requirements: Obtain an account (login and password) on the ANR submission site in advance; the AAP recommends registering as early as possible.
Deposit the complete submission file electronically from the project manager's account before the published closing date and time.
Only the electronic version of the submission documents present on the submission site at the call closing time is taken into account for evaluation.

Define, in the scientific document, a structured maturation phase at the start of the project, with duration, budget and responsible persons, producing an operational roadmap, an ethical issues analysis, an internal ethics charter and a Data Management Plan.
Designate a person responsible for data (référent données) who drafts and updates the PGD.
Identify, from the time of submission, a person responsible for ethical issues (référent des enjeux éthiques).
Identify among the people involved in the project one person responsible for monitoring equity and inclusion (équité et inclusion).
Describe strategies for maintaining the interdisciplinary and/or transdisciplinary dialogue throughout the project and designate the person responsible for monitoring them.

Explicitly justify in the project budget the participation of project leaders in 2 in-person meetings every 18 months in metropolitan France and 3-4 travels for workpackage leaders or staff in training (doctorate or post-doctorate) every 2 years.

Projects acquiring new data or samples at sea on unprogrammed French oceanographic fleet (IR* Flotte) means must justify why non-realisation would not undermine the project and must follow the upstream operational feasibility study procedure of the IR* Flotte (FOF naval operations pole); the minutes of the ad hoc commission (CNFH or CNFC) must be supplied.
Data management must rely on the Research e-Infrastructures tools and services (Data-Terra, Huma-num, Progedo), following FAIR and, where relevant, CARE principles.
scholarships.duration: Projects must run between 36 and 54 months.
scholarships.application_period: Ouverture : 21/07/2026 à 09:00 CEST. Clôture : 17/11/2026 à 11:00 CET. Single-phase call (l'appel à projets se déroule en une seule phase): full proposals are submitted and evaluated by an international committee set up by the ANR.
scholarships.selection_notes: Only proposals satisfying the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are assessed by an independent international-dimension committee convened by the ANR, which may call on external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after sending questions in advance. The committee produces (1) a list of projects it recommends for funding on the published criteria and (2) a list it proposes not to fund because quality is insufficient on at least one criterion, with a written justification for each project, and may give an opinion on the amount requested. Uninvolved PEPR GFM programme directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after opinion of the CPMo and the SGPI, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (a) scientific ambition and excellence (research question going beyond the documented state of the art, discipline combination justified by the question, dialogue of conceptual frameworks, ethical questions treated as integral to ambition); (b) quality of the consortium, resources mobilised and governance (recognised complementary expertise, adequacy of staff with objectives including a precise role and career benefit for each contractual worker, structured maturation phase, mechanisms for shared appropriation of questions, inventory/acquisition/management strategy for data and samples, recurrent ethical monitoring mechanisms, explicit choices to minimise the environmental footprint, coherent sizing with an argued 0.8-3 M€ budget); (c) fit with the PEPR GFM challenges and impact (clear fit with at least one challenge and the programme's strategic priorities, described scientific/economic/environmental/societal impacts, described sharing of data and results, open-access data strategy with FAIR and CARE and Opidor PGD links, dissemination to academic and non-academic audiences).
