scholarships.title: France 2030 - PEPR PROPSY - "Psychiatrie de précision" - Appel à projets - 2026
eligibility: The submission file must be deposited complete on the ANR submission site before the closing date and time, and the administrative and financial document signed by each partner institution and scanned must be deposited at the date and time indicated in the call document.
The project scientific document must imperatively follow the template available on the call website and be deposited in unprotected PDF format.
Project duration must be 24-48 months for the pre-clinical axis and 36-48 months for the clinical and mixed axes.
Aid requested must be 500 000 €-800 000 € for the pre-clinical axis, 800 000 €-1 500 000 € for the clinical axis, and 800 000 €-2 000 000 € for the mixed axis.
The coordinating institution must be a French higher education and research institution, a research organisation, or a foundation of scientific cooperation.
For the clinical and mixed axes, projects are necessarily collaborative with a minimum of two different French research structures (structure identified by an RNSR number).

Beneficiaries are research organisations, higher education and research institutions, and recognised foundations of scientific cooperation described as "organismes de recherche et de diffusion des connaissances".

Private institutions contributing to public-service missions in higher education and research under article L.732-1 of the Code de l'Education may be financed after ANR analysis, MESRE opinion and SGPI validation.
Companies and foreign institutions may be associated as partners but cannot receive funding for that participation.
Pre-clinical studies may be single-team; collaborations are encouraged. Clinical and mixed projects must be collaborative.
Teams of the PROPSY "Projets Ciblés" are eligible as partners, but their coordinators are not authorised to coordinate a project in this call.
requirements: Open an account (login and password) on the ANR submission site in advance; the AAP recommends registering as early as possible.
Deposit the complete submission file electronically from the project manager's account before the published closing date and time.
Only the electronic version of the submission documents present on the submission site at the call closing time is taken into account for evaluation.
Contribute to strengthening and enhancing the capacity of French research actors, their attractiveness, their European and international influence, and their impact on the economy and society.
Produce high-quality research strengthening the acquisition of disciplinary and/or interdisciplinary scientific knowledge to address current and future precision-psychiatry issues.
Valorise the research and innovation produced, accompanying clinical implementation and/or industrialisation.
Integrate the sharing of data, results and knowledge in an open science logic.

Respect the PROPSY thematic scope: projects mainly on addictions are not eligible, except where those conditions are addressed within precision psychiatry as secondary phenomena or comorbidities of one of the four PEPR PROPSY disorders.

Integrate a humanities and social sciences dimension where relevant, for example analysis of care pathways, clinical, social or ethical acceptability of innovations, and/or the involvement of patients, affected persons or associations in the design, implementation and valorization of projects.
Signal any overlap with an already funded or submitted project and supply, where applicable, the justifications showing the absence of duplication.
Where relevant, rely on public or private co-funding, national or international: these are not mandatory but are encouraged.

For clinical studies, the data sets mobilised (cohorts, national or international databases, SNDS or existing health data warehouse data) must be identified and documented from the submission to guarantee project feasibility within the granted duration.

For clinical studies, included patients must present at least one disorder of interest to PEPR PROPSY (bipolar disorders, resistant depressions, psychotic disorders, autism spectrum disorders) and/or the project may cover several disorders simultaneously.

For the pre-clinical axis, explicitly declare the co-deposit of the project or obtain agreement from the French and foreign partner institutions; the actual co-deposit wording is not published in the AAP for this axis, so confirm it with the ANR contact.
scholarships.duration: 24 to 48 months for the pre-clinical axis; 36 to 48 months for the clinical and mixed axes.
scholarships.application_period: Ouverture : 24/06/2026 à 09:00 CEST. Fermeture : 10/11/2026 à 11:00 CET (extended from 15/10/2026). The call page shows status "Ouvert – 2026". A webinar was held on 26/08/2026 with presentation and FAQ published.
scholarships.selection_notes: Only proposals meeting the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are evaluated by an independent international-dimension committee, which may use external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after transmitting questions in advance. The committee delivers to the PEPR PROPSY scientific directors a report with a list of projects recommended for funding, a list of projects it proposes not to fund for insufficient quality on at least one criterion, a written justification for every project, and possibly an opinion on the amounts requested. The PEPR PROPSY scientific directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after SGPI opinion, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (1) excellence and scientific ambition in precision psychiatry - clarity of objectives and hypotheses, innovativeness, ambition, originality, methodological or conceptual rupture against the state of the art, methodological relevance, preliminary data, project feasibility; (2) quality of the consortium, project management, resources mobilised and governance - competence, expertise and involvement of the project leader including capacity to coordinate ambitious multidisciplinary projects or consortia, academic track record, international recognition, quality and complementarity of the scientific consortium, adequacy between human and financial means and the objectives, relevance of the schedule and management of scientific risks with alternative solutions and credible milestones, relevance and efficiency of governance including patient associations and links with industrial partners or other programmes; (3) impact and outcomes - capacity to address precision-psychiatry development issues, active strategy to measure economic and/or societal impact, contribution to solutions for pathophysiological, diagnostic or therapeutic issues, dissemination and valorization strategy in itinere and ex post, adherence to FAIR and Open Science principles and promotion of scientific culture. Committee members and external experts commit to ANR deontology and integrity rules, strict confidentiality, declaration of conflicts of interest, and a ban on AI tools in the evaluation.

scholarships.title: Appel à projets M-ERA.NET 2026/27 - Science et ingénierie des matériaux pour l'innovation en Europe
eligibility: The pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one (and only one) scientific collaboration theme defined in the call.
Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).

Minimum consortium composition of 3 Partners requesting funding from a funding agency listed in Annex 3 of the call text and eligible for that funding, from at least three different countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026. Partners not requesting funding may participate if this minimum is met.
The coordinator must request funding from one of the agencies participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026 and be eligible there.
The involvement of a single Partner must not exceed 60% of the total involvement (measured in person-months) of the proposal.
The involvement of Partners from a single country must not exceed 70% of the total involvement (measured in person-months).

If one or more Partners are not eligible (or not invited to step 2) and their total effort is equal to or greater than 15% of the total project effort (in person-months), the entire pre-proposal or detailed proposal is discarded from the selection process.
To be invited to submit a detailed proposal in step 2, the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different countries participating in the Call 2026.

A pre-proposal containing one or more Partners requesting ANR aid must clearly indicate the topic studied and the TRL levels of the tasks of each French partner in the consortium, and must be deposited on the ANR submission site in step 2, in addition to the deposit on the call site, providing all the information requested on the site.

A pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one of the ANR-eligible topics: 1. Materials for energy storage and distribution systems; 2. Materials for energy conversion; 4. Innovative functional materials with designed architectures; 6. Next-generation materials for electronics. The relevance of the proposal to the chosen topic must be clearly justified from step 1; proposals not matching these topics are rendered ineligible for ANR funding.

The final TRL of the project must not exceed 5 for an ANR-funded partner, on pain of ineligibility, and the work carried out by partners requesting ANR aid must necessarily be positioned either in the "fundamental research" segment or in the first "applied research" segment.

Partners, legal or natural persons, subject to European Union sanctions are excluded from the call; the ANR declares ineligible any partner requesting its aid who is associated within the submitted project with partners covered by a sanction measure. As of publication this concerns in particular partners from Russia and Belarus, and partners from territories of Ukraine escaping the control of the Ukrainian government. The list is non-exhaustive and may change with new EU sanctions.

A project proposal may not be similar in whole or in part to another proposal submitted to any ANR call under evaluation (all calls and all evaluation stages) or funded by the ANR. Similarity is established when the projects describe identical main objectives or result from a simple adaptation.
A researcher may request ANR aid (whether as partner, coordinator or co-coordinator) for only one proposal in the 2026/27 M-ERA.NET call.
Each project Partner must meet its own funding agency's national or regional criteria, including its TRL requirements, and must be selected by that agency to receive funding.
requirements: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, written in English, must be deposited by the project coordinator on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site.
Use of the templates available on the M-ERA.NET site is mandatory; any unauthorised modification, in particular exceeding the page limit, may render the proposal ineligible.
The pre-proposal must be the duly completed pre-proposal form, in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions.

The detailed proposal must be the duly completed detailed-proposal form in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions, and must include Annex 1 describing the Partner profiles together with the CVs of all consortium participants, also in English.

Partners requesting ANR aid invited to step 2 must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with information identical to the central deposit; the exact link and deadline are communicated later by email.
National and regional eligibility, selection and funding rules apply at both steps, and for some countries/regions restrictions on topics, TRL levels and the type of eligible partners apply.
The scientific and technological objectives stated in the pre-proposal cannot be modified at step 2.

It is not possible to add Partners from new countries to the consortium in step 2; only new Partners from countries already involved in the pre-proposal via a funding request to one of their funding agencies may be added.

Any change must be communicated to and accepted by the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date, with the consortium coordinator ensuring acceptance.

The scientific lead (Responsable scientifique) formally commits that their hierarchy (administrative and financial services and persons legally entitled to represent the managing institution, or their representatives) has approved the submission and that the information has been communicated to them.

French project leaders (requesting funding or not) ensure compliance with the national research professions deontology charter and the ANR deontology and scientific-integrity charter within the research activities carried out under their responsibility.

Where genetic resources are used, all participants (requesting funding or not) must respect the Nagoya Protocol obligations, and beneficiaries under the access-and-benefit-sharing regulation must provide the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the date of the final payment.
Where relevant, take into account the sex and/or gender dimension in the research and give equitable visibility to the work produced.

Before any ANR project deposit, applicants should approach their institution's defence and security officer or PPST services to verify their project's eligibility conditions; projects with foreign public or private partners are subject to SHFDS/MESR opinion, and a negative opinion prevents selection.
scholarships.duration: Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).
scholarships.application_period: Ouverture : 31/03/2026 à 09:00 CEST. Limite de dépôt des pré-dossiers : 12/05/2026 à 12:00 CEST (step 1, closed). Limite de dépôt des projets : 18/11/2026 à 12:00 CET (step 2, open on 2026-10-01). An information webinar was held on 18 March 2026, 12:00-14:00 CET, with presentations and the recording available on the M-ERA.NET call site.
scholarships.selection_notes: Evaluation and selection are centralised at M-ERA.NET level and take place in two steps: step 1 central evaluation of pre-proposals by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat, with invitations to step 2 issued in ranking order and taking account of the participating agencies' budget capacity; step 2 central evaluation of detailed proposals by independent international experts convened by the same secretariat. Proposals are ranked on the evaluation results and selection follows the ranking. The list of projects recommended for funding is drawn up by the group of participating funders taking account of their respective budget capacities, and the final funding decision is then taken individually by the funders concerned. Results are sent by the call secretariat to the project coordinators. Evaluation modalities and criteria are those of the call text (Guide for proposers) available on the ANR call page and the M-ERA.NET call site; the ANR adds its own horizontal objectives, which are that projects show significant French participation (in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the work), generate significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and are ambitious with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration. During discussions to separate projects of similar scientific quality within the funder group, projects involving a wider and/or more diverse consortium may be favoured.

eligibility: Researchers at the career stage 'PhD Candidate (with Masters)'

Applicants must meet cumulative eligibility conditions: demonstrate a link to Luxembourg, be enrolled in a PhD programme by the project start date, not already hold a PhD, and not benefit from an old-age pension
Each applicant may submit one proposal per call
Bottom-up: proposals from all fields of research and technological development are eligible
requirements: Demonstrate a clear link to Luxembourg
Be enrolled in a PhD programme by the project start date
Not already hold a PhD
Not be in receipt of an old-age pension
Submit only one proposal per call
Applications must be submitted in English via the FNR Grant Management System

scholarships.application_period: The very first call was launched mid-September 2026 with a deadline on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET, so the scheme is open on 2026-10-01. From 2027 there will be two calls per year: the first call launched mid-February closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET, funding decisions are communicated in July and funded projects must start no later than 1 February of the following year; the second call launched mid-September closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET, decisions are communicated in March of the following year and funded projects must start no later than 1 October.
scholarships.selection_notes: Eligible proposals are assessed on the scientific quality and potential of the project, the applicant's profile and potential, the quality of the Host Institution, supervision and training environment, and the expected impact of the project. AFdoc follows a bottom-up approach: proposals from all fields of research and technological development are eligible, and projects do not need to align with Luxembourg's National Research Priorities provided they fall within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner. The 2026 call is a pilot for a self-assessment on potential research security aspects.
scholarships.program_type: Government research funding
scholarships.name: AFdoc - Aides à la formation doctorale (FNR PhD funding scheme)

scholarships.title: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)
scholarships.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme gives young people who hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation. The grant is made up of a one-off travel allowance and a monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, both set in advance; the monthly amount depends on the host city. Nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant, and the programme targets people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights. The 2026 budget is exhausted; a budget is available again for 2027, with applications reopenable from January 2027.
scholarships.deadline: No more grants for 2026: 'You can no longer apply for a grant for internships continuing into 2026. There is no more budget available for 2026. A budget will be available again in 2027. You can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027.' Within a funded budget year: 'You can submit your grant application up to six months in advance until one day before the start of your internship.'
scholarships.deadline_display: No more grants for 2026: 'You can no longer apply for a grant for internships continuing into 2026. There is no more budget available for 2026. A budget will be available again in 2027. You can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027.' Within a funded budget year: 'You can submit your grant application up to six months in advance until one day before the start of your internship.'
eligibility: You are younger than 35 on the start date of your internship.
You have obtained a secondary or higher education diploma in Flanders. So your nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant.
You have secured an internship with a multilateral organisation from the published qualifying list.
The internship lasts at least two and up to six months.
The internship must take place at the headquarters or a field office of the organisation, within the areas of jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders.
benefits: The grant is not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, so it is not an obstacle to the Flemish Growth Package/child benefit you may still be entitled to for 12 months after finishing your studies
Payment in two instalments: 85% of the total grant after approval, and the remaining 15% after the internship once you submit the internship report and the supervisor's evaluation report
The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders
requirements: Be under 35 on the internship start date
Hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained at a Flemish educational institution
Have secured the internship; you may apply up to six months before it starts or after it has started
Your internship supervisor must complete the attestation regarding the internship offer and submit it to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be
If you apply after the internship has started, the remaining period counted from the first day after you submit must be at least two months
After the internship, submit the personal evaluation form and have your supervisor complete and submit the evaluation form, at the latest two months after the end of the internship
Take part in an intake interview before the internship and a follow-up conversation afterwards
You must not receive a salary from the hosting organisation if you want to keep the Flemish Growth Package/child benefit
Inform the programme if you end the internship early; you may have to repay part of the grant
scholarships.duration: The grant covers an internship of at least two and up to six months. The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for 2026 are closed. The 2027 budget reopens for applications in January 2027 for internships taking place in 2027, and new internship vacancies will be published on the programme's internships page from late 2026 onwards. Inside a funded budget year the published rule is that you may apply at any time of the year until one day before your internship starts, up to six months in advance, but a grant is only granted while budget remains.
scholarships.selection_notes: No competitive jury or published ranking is described for this programme. The published route is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: in principle you can apply at any time of the year, but you only get a grant if budget is still available, and if a budget is no longer available for the current year that is announced clearly on the programme website; an application submitted after the budget is gone is not processed and is not kept until a new budget is available. The average administrative turnaround time is three weeks. The grant is reduced by any remuneration or financial allowance you receive for the same internship from another Belgian or foreign government or from the multilateral organisation itself.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.name: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)

scholarships.title: Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff — Scholars
scholarships.description: A monthly stipend for foreign students who already hold an admission confirmation from an Estonian higher education institution for the 2026/2027 academic year. The rate is EUR 350 per month for first-cycle (BA) and master's studies and EUR 660 per month for doctoral studies. The Board pays the scholarship to the host university, which then disburses it. The scheme is funded under bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements and is run through the Estonian Scholarship Programme.
eligibility: The scholarship can be applied for by foreign students who wish to study at a higher education institution in Estonia during the 2026/2027 academic year at formal studies or as an exchange student

Applications will be accepted only from students from countries whose citizenship is in the listed countries: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czech Republic, Cyprus, Egypt, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Israel, Italy, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Mexico, Moldova, People's Republic of China, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Korea, Slovenia, Spain, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, United States of America
The scholarship supports master's and PhD studies in all fields
In the first stage of higher education (BA), the scholarship can only be applied for in fields that are related to Estonian language and culture
The application should include a confirmation letter concerning the student's admission to an Estonian higher education institution with reference to 2026/27 academic year
Degree studies scholarship applicant from 2nd year upwards has to be enrolled in full time studies
requirements: Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia (the strand applied for here)
The scholarship decision does not guarantee admission to the desired higher education institution — the applicant must separately meet the institution's own admission requirements
The final scholarship decision will be made after confirmation of admission
If the applicant does not start or continue studying in Estonia, they shall lose the right to the scholarship
Applications that are incomplete, drafted offhand, include false information, omit relevant information or have been submitted after the deadline will not be considered for assessment
scholarships.duration: One academic year (2026/2027); scholarships are paid for undergraduate students for 12 months of the academic year, except for the final nominal year when the scholarship is paid for 10 months
scholarships.application_period: Applications accepted 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026 (23:59 Estonian time); results announced personally by email
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications shall be evaluated and the proposal for awarding the scholarship shall be made by the scholarship committee, based on the provisions of the directive and the committee's rules of procedure. Applications shall be evaluated based on the applicant's motivation (based on the letter of motivation) and the overall quality of the application — these two criteria carry equal weight. The scholarship recipients shall be approved by a directive of the Director General of the Board. The page warns the programme is highly competitive: historically only about 10% of applicants receive the scholarship, and in the 2026 application round 15 scholarships will be awarded.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.name: Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff — Scholars

scholarships.title: Nordic Scholarship Programme (Nordic Africa Institute)
scholarships.description: A one-month funded research stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala for Africa-focused researchers and students already based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland. The scholarship covers return travel at the least expensive fare, free centrally located accommodation in Uppsala, a desk and computer in a shared office at the Institute, and a subsistence allowance of SEK 450 per day. It is a short-term research stay award, not a degree programme.
eligibility: You must be pursuing Africa-oriented studies/research within the fields of social sciences or humanities
You can be a master student, PhD candidate, postdoctoral or mid-career researcher

You may apply regardless of citizenship, but you must be affiliated to and based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland (both when you apply and when you take up the scholarship)
The scholarship is awarded for a one-month stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala
benefits: Access to the Nordic Africa Institute's library collections on contemporary Africa (books, periodicals, newspapers, and government publications)
Support to connect to existing work at the Institute through NAI research hosts
Access to a workspace in a shared office at the Institute for the one-month stay
requirements: Applications are submitted online
The application and appendices must be in English
Incomplete applications will not be considered
The application must be uploaded with all four listed documents
scholarships.duration: One-month stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala
scholarships.application_period: Open now for scholarships in 2027, closing 11 October 2026; applicants informed of the outcome by the end of November 2026 at the latest
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are primarily evaluated based on the outline of the research project. The Institute states that it reads proposals carefully and that it is important to learn about the applicant's research in their own words and framing, and that using AI to develop the text may place an applicant at a disadvantage in the assessment process. Scholarships are awarded once per year.
scholarships.program_type: Research funding
scholarships.name: Nordic Scholarship Programme (Nordic Africa Institute)

scholarships.title: UC Doctoral Scholarship (UCDS)
scholarships.description: The UC Doctoral Scholarship is a centrally funded Te Whare WÄnanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury award that supports study towards a first research doctoral degree in any discipline at UC. Its published value is financial assistance of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points. The same round can add recognition-only or top-up Prestige awards, but applicants who hold one of the Core scholarships are also automatically considered for Prestige awards with no separate application, and the Prestige value is added on top of the Core value (for example a $32,650 p.a. stipend becomes $37,650 p.a. with a $5,000 top-up). It is not a New Zealand Government scholarship; it is a university award and subject to funding availability and annual review.
eligibility: You intend to study at UC towards your first research doctoral degree.
Your GPA over the last two years of relevant academic study is equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0.
The award is available in any discipline at UC.
International students can apply for any UC scholarship unless the regulations specifically restrict the scholarship to NZ citizens or holders of NZ residence class visas.
Most scholarships require that you have admission to the University, so you must also meet the criteria for admission to your research doctoral programme.

You must have also submitted your separate application for admission into your research doctoral degree programme at UC before the closing date for scholarship applications (point 2.2 of the Regulations); this is done in your myUC account.
You need to have created a myUC account prior to applying for a scholarship.
requirements: Applications for the following doctoral scholarships are now open and will close 15 October: UC Doctoral Scholarship (UCDS), UCDS for Students with Disabilities, UC Pacific Doctoral Scholarship and UC Matariki Doctoral Scholarship.
This application round is for students who intend to start their doctoral studies before the 1 July 2027.

With the exception of the UC Doctoral Scholarship for Students with Disabilities and the UC Connect Doctoral Scholarships, students can apply for all other Core UC Doctoral Scholarships on the single 'UC Doctoral Scholarship' application form.
You must also have submitted your separate application for admission into your research doctoral degree programme at UC before the closing date for scholarship applications.
These scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year.

Most UC scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports; some require an interview with the selection panel, and the Scholarships Office will notify you if one is required.
UC states that late applications are not accepted and that the closing date is not flexible.
scholarships.duration: Up to a total of 360 points of thesis-only doctoral enrolment (three years of full-time study)
scholarships.application_period: Two rounds a year. October round: opens 20 August 2026, closes 15 October 2026, for doctoral study starting before 1 July 2027. May round: opens 20 March, closes 15 May, for students starting in the second half of 2027. UC states applications generally open approximately eight weeks before the closing date.
scholarships.selection_notes: UC states that most scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports, that some require an interview with the selection panel, and that selection committees vary according to the scholarship. It states the selection process typically takes six to eight weeks but may take longer, and the outcome is notified in writing once selection is final. The scholarship's own selection criteria sit in the Regulations document, which is not published on the pages read here. Prestige awards are awarded from the applicants who applied for a Core scholarship in a given academic year, with no separate application, and are awarded at the end of each academic year.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.name: UC Doctoral Scholarship (UCDS)

scholarships.title: Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS)
scholarships.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship is a Charles Darwin University award for international students with a record of academic excellence. CDU publishes that it covers 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course, and that it is neither transferable for cash nor refundable and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. Applicants must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification, must be paying international student fees, and must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency. Results are announced during Orientation Week.
eligibility: Applicant must apply to commence study in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027, in the intake they are first offered.
Applicant must meet the University's academic and English language entry requirements for their chosen course.
Applicant must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification.
Applicant must be an international student paying international student fees.
Applicant must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency.
Applicants must be able to pay their portion of the tuition fees on or before the payment due date, which CDU states is the first day of teaching of each semester.
The scholarship applies to an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree.
requirements: Step 1: apply to study at CDU.
Step 2: submit your application for the VCIHAS.
The application form requires an application intake, an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC) and an email address that matches the one provided in the Studylink application.
The form requires an average overall score in your highest completed qualification, expressed as a percentage.

The applicant statement is mandatory and answers why you should be selected, how you will become an outstanding ambassador of CDU, your extracurricular activities with a focus on community engagement, work experience, creative arts and sport, and how you will use your CDU qualification to make a difference in your community.

A declaration must be ticked confirming the information is true and correct, that you have read and understood the conditions of application, that the decision of the University selection panel is final, that you cannot hold more than one tuition fee scholarship from CDU at a time, that you do not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsorship agency, and that you accept you may be asked to provide a student story or testimonial as a scholarship recipient.
The form must be signed and dated.

Ongoing eligibility: continue to be an international student liable for international student fees, pay your portion of tuition fees on or before the first day of teaching of each semester, maintain satisfactory academic progress each semester with a minimum GPA of 5.3 and no fail grade in any unit, and maintain a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless you have approval to reduce your study load or take a leave of absence for the semester.
scholarships.duration: The minimum time in which the course can be completed, or until the maximum scholarship value is exhausted, the course is completed, or the recipient no longer meets the ongoing eligibility of the scholarship.
scholarships.application_period: Applications are open at the time of checking on 1 October 2026. CDU publishes closing dates of 31 January 2027 for Semester 1 2027 and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2 2027, but does not publish a separate opening date for the scholarship.
scholarships.selection_notes: CDU publishes the selection criteria as the overall score in your highest completed qualification plus a supporting statement. The application form adds that the decision of the University selection panel is final, and the declaration confirms the process is competitive. CDU publishes no interview requirement, no weighting for the two criteria, no offer round structure and no appeal process for VCIHAS; other CDU International College scholarships on the same page do publish an interview requirement, so confirm whether an interview applies to VCIHAS.

scholarships.name: Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS)

scholarships.title: ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award
scholarships.description: The ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award is an Australian National University award whose stated objective is to attract a diverse range of academically capable overseas students to enrol in undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs at ANU, funded by the University. ANU publishes the value as 20% off first-year tuition fees, with the tuition scholarship applied towards tuition at the start of each semester for the one year of the award. It is restricted to residents of China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, and excludes the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE). Recipients are responsible for the costs of books, study materials, accommodation and all other costs of study.
scholarships.deadline: Application period: Open for applications. ANU publishes no closing date for this award; consideration is automatic with the admissions application.
scholarships.deadline_display: Application period: Open for applications. ANU publishes no closing date for this award; consideration is automatic with the admissions application.
eligibility: You are an international student.
You are a new commencing student, or a continuing student who has received an offer of admission to a higher AQF level of studies.

You hold residential status in one of the following Countries or Regions: China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, Republic of Korea, or The Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

You meet the minimum academic entry requirements: undergraduate applicants a Selection Rank of 85 (or equivalent as determined by the University) or above, or postgraduate applicants a minimum GPA of 5.5 (or equivalent).
You are not the recipient of an external sponsorship that covers all or part of your tuition fees at the University.

You acknowledge that the award can be offered only once at each level of study, except where you progress from an undergraduate degree (AQF Level 7) to a one-year Honours program (AQF Level 8), or accept a packaged offer such as a Graduate Certificate leading to a Master's degree.
Your program is an eligible program, excluding the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE).
Study level: Undergraduate/Bachelor, Honours, Postgraduate/Masters and Graduate certificate. Selection basis: academic merit.
benefits: No separate scholarship application: all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the University are considered automatically.
You accept the academic offer and the scholarship offer separately; more information is provided with the scholarship offer letter.

ANU publishes a separate ANU International Achievement Award for applicants resident outside this award's country list, with published values of 20% for Undergraduate, 20% for Postgraduate, 25% for South East Asia and 50% for Pacific.
requirements: There is no need to apply for the scholarship; all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the university will be automatically considered.
Press the 'Apply now' button to start the Admissions application process.
You will need to accept both your academic offer and your scholarship offer separately; more information is provided with your scholarship offer letter.
The recipient is responsible for making payment of all tuition fees by the prescribed date as set out by the University each session.
The value of the Award is stated in the letter of offer.
Only applicants who meet all the eligibility criteria will be considered.
ANU publishes a Conditions of Award document numbered 63/2026, linked from the scholarship page.
scholarships.duration: Payment made for 1 year (payments are made for a fixed number of years; for this award that is one year)
scholarships.application_period: Continuous. ANU's scholarship page shows the application period as 'Open for applications' with no closing date, because no separate scholarship application is required: all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the University are considered automatically.
scholarships.selection_notes: ANU states that selection is based on academic merit, that only applicants who meet all the eligibility criteria will be considered, that qualifications submitted for admission will be converted to the common scale which determines whether an applicant is eligible, and that eligible applicants with multiple qualifications will be ranked according to the qualification used as the basis of admission. The value of the Award is stated in the letter of offer. ANU publishes no interview, no referee requirement, no offer rounds and no appeal process for this award.

scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.description: The MEXT Scholarship research-student route funds postgraduate research study at a Japanese graduate school: it exempts tuition, pays a monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000, and provides round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Recipients are selected by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country after sitting that mission's Japanese and English qualifying examinations, and are then placed at a graduate school. This record covers the Embassy Recommendation route for the 2027 cohort; the separate University Recommendation route is administered by individual Japanese universities.
scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
scholarships.deadline_display: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
eligibility: Research students: You must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's program or a doctoral program (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.
Embassy Recommendation: scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country).

The type and field of application may vary from country to country. Please check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in your country to see if there are any openings in the type and field you wish to apply for.
All required documents and interviews will be conducted by the Japanese embassy or other diplomatic mission abroad in your country.
benefits: Preliminary training of Japanese etc. of 6 months for those who need this training, where offered by the institution
Placement into a Japanese graduate school at no application cost
requirements: Application must be made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's own country (Embassy Recommendation route).
Applicants must take the embassy/consulate's qualifying examinations, which for research students are Japanese and English.
The applicant must submit a 'Configuration Preference for University of Placement' (配置希望大学申請書) as part of the application forms.
Application fee is not charged; MEXT warns that organisations or individuals charging application fees or deposits have no relation with the Japanese Government.
scholarships.duration: Embassy Recommendation: irregular course within 2 years; regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)
scholarships.application_period: Applications for the 2027 cycle are handled at embassy/consulate level. MEXT lists the 2027 Embassy Recommendation Research Student recruitment under "募集中のプログラム" (programmes currently being recruited). No central opening or closing date is published; embassies set and publish their own deadlines and sit their own qualifying examinations.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants are recruited and initially screened by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country, which sits its own qualifying examinations (Japanese and English for research students), conducts the interview and collects all required documents; MEXT then selects the scholarship students and allocates them to host graduate schools, subject to the host university's acceptance.

scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published. eligibility: Young Leaders Program (YLP) students: You must be under 40 years of age (in principle), and university or college graduates who have practical work experience, young public administrators, etc. who are expected to play active role in Asia and other countries.

Study in Japan: 'Young Leaders Program (YLP) students' - Embassy recommendation: No; University recommendation: No. Recommendations come from official overseas recommending organizations (footnote 2).

scholarships.duration: Within 1 year and 6 months including Japanese language education (MEXT table); GRIPS states a 1-year programme, October enrolment to September graduation

scholarships.title: GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) Program - Undergraduate Degree Programs
scholarships.description: The Korean government-invited scholarship degree programme that funds a year of Korean language training followed by an associate degree (2-3 years) or bachelor's degree (4-6 years) at a designated GKS university in Korea. The published benefits list is airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances. Selection runs through two routes: an Embassy Track that applies through the Korean embassy/consulate, and a University Track in which the student applies directly to a GKS-designated university (UIC specialisation and Associate Degree).
scholarships.deadline: Announcement by NIIED in September. Application submission: Embassy Track in September; University Track September - November. Screening and selection October - December. Final results announced by NIIED in December. The page publishes month-level timing only; no day-level deadline is published on this page.
scholarships.deadline_display: Announcement by NIIED in September. Application submission: Embassy Track in September; University Track September - November. Screening and selection October - December. Final results announced by NIIED in December. The page publishes month-level timing only; no day-level deadline is published on this page.
eligibility: Nationality: Applicants and both of their parents must hold non-Korean citizenship
Age: Applicants must be under 25 years of age as of the applicable year
Education: Associate Degree Program - High school graduate or expected to graduate; Bachelor's Degree Program - High school or associate degree graduate or expected to graduate

Academic Performance: Applicants must meet the academic performance requirements, such as a cumulative score of 80% or higher, ranking within the top 20% of their class, or meeting the required CGPA threshold
Embassy Track General and Overseas Korean applicants may apply to up to three universities, including at least one Type B university
Embassy Track R-GKS applicants may apply to up to two Type B universities
The UIC Program under University Track provides customized curriculum and field experience through industry-university cooperation focused on the fields of natural science and engineering
Specialization (UIC) is available only for associate and bachelor's degree programs
requirements: Korean language training (1 year) + degree programs
Detailed information on universities and academic departments can be found in the 'University Information File' available for download from the GKS announcements
For detailed information, please refer to the application guidelines and announcements posted in the GKS notices

scholarships.application_period: Embassy Track: applications accepted in September. University Track: applications accepted September to November. On 2026-10-01 the University Track falls inside the published September-November window; the Embassy Track submission month published is September.
