scholarships.title: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
scholarships.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
scholarships.deadline: Depending on chosen study programme; please check the DAAD list of application deadlines or the website of the chosen study programme. Applications are sent directly to the course, not to the DAAD.
scholarships.deadline_display: Depending on chosen study programme; please check the DAAD list of application deadlines or the website of the chosen study programme. Applications are sent directly to the course, not to the DAAD.
eligibility: Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from the countries on the DAAD EPOS list of eligible countries
Bachelor degree (usually a four-year course) in an appropriate subject
Academic degree completed with far above average results (upper third)
At least two years of related professional experience after the first degree (bachelor) at the time of application
Academic degrees should normally not be more than six years old
Applicants who have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered

Working context is normally a public authority or a state or private company in a developing country, in planning and executing directives and projects with development-policy emphasis in technological, economic or social areas
Proof of development-related motivation and an expectation of taking on social responsibility and initiating and supporting processes of change after the scholarship
benefits: Monthly rent subsidy under certain circumstances
Monthly allowance for accompanying members of family under certain circumstances
Six-month preparatory German language course in Germany for scholarships for German-taught courses
requirements: Applications have only to be sent to the respective course directly; applications sent to the DAAD will not be forwarded to the course or university
You can apply for up to three courses; if applying for more than one course, list the courses in order of priority in the DAAD application forms and do not change the priorities
The complete applications have to be submitted in English or German to be considered
Incomplete applications cannot be considered
One uniform letter of motivation must be submitted to all postgraduate degree programmes of your choice, explaining the choice of courses and prioritisation
If the motivation letter does not explain the specific courses and priority order, the application cannot be considered or an already awarded scholarship may be withdrawn
Applicants from the People's Republic of China are asked to submit an APS Certificate with their application documents

For courses in German: a minimum German language level of B1 at the time of application, evidenced by a current certificate, and successful passing of DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before the start of the study course
For courses in English: proof of adequate language skills according to the regulations of the respective course
Keep a copy of every document, because the documents must be uploaded as PDF files to the DAAD portal if you are suggested for a DAAD scholarship
scholarships.duration: 12 to 42 months (dependent on study programme)
scholarships.application_period: Cycle-based: applicants apply directly to a listed EPOS postgraduate course for the published intake year (the current DAAD programme list is headed 'List of Application Deadlines for Intake 2027/2028'); the course's own committee then nominates candidates, who are invited to upload to the DAAD portal for the final selection.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is by independent, voluntary selection committees. Candidates must fulfil the academic requirements and be expected to complete the study programme successfully (above-average first academic exam, top performance in the third, language skills), hold a relevant Bachelor degree, have at least two years' professional experience, and prove a development-related motivation. Special circumstances such as a disability may be taken into account.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.name: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)

scholarships.title: MOPGA 2027: Visiting Fellowship Program for Early Career Researchers
scholarships.description: MOPGA is a French Government visiting fellowship that pays a monthly allowance to early-career foreign researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory on climate and environmental themes. Each fellowship covers a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health, civil liability and repatriation coverage. Host laboratories receive no funding under the programme; the money is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses, and international travel costs are not covered.
eligibility: Hold a doctoral degree awarded less than five years before the application deadline, i.e. have defended your PhD thesis between December 2021 and December 2026 inclusive
Be exclusively of foreign nationality (all nationalities are eligible except French nationality)
Apply for the purpose of undertaking international mobility to France
Not be residing and professionally active in France at the time of application
Not have previously received a MOPGA fellowship
benefits: Status of French Government Scholarship holder (BGF)
Fellowship paid directly by Campus France
Research stay agreement signed between the French host institution and the researcher
requirements: Applications must be submitted online through the Campus France SMApply platform; applications sent by email will not be considered
A research stay agreement must be signed between the host institution in France and the researcher
Host laboratories undertake to provide an appropriate scientific environment for the research stay, but do not receive any funding under the programme

This French Government fellowship cannot be combined with a French employment contract, such as a research contract or postdoctoral contract, or with any other individual funding awarded by a French government entity
Research project must fall within one of the five MOPGA research areas
scholarships.duration: 12 months
scholarships.application_period: Applications open 15 September 2026 and close 15 December 2026. Results are notified May-June 2027, and successful applicants arrive in France between September and December 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection takes place in two stages: scientific experts appointed by the French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space in the relevant fields assess the applications received, then a scientific committee makes the final selection. Innovative approaches involving advanced technologies within the eligible research areas are given particular consideration during the selection process.

scholarships.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher at a university or other eligible research institution. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows can also be applied for through the host institution to cover cooperative research-related expenses. Because this is a research appointment rather than a degree programme, there is no tuition to pay and the award is not presented as tuition funding.

As of April 1 of the fiscal year, have obtained a doctoral degree within six years of the date the fellowship goes into effect (on or after April 2, six years prior to the fiscal year), or who are expected to receive a Ph.D. by the start date of the fellowship period
Whether or not the candidate is employed in a full-time position is not considered
Researchers who obtained their PhD within six years minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks of leave counted as one month)

Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship Program for Research in Japan (Standard, and Pathway to University positions in Japan) are not eligible
Japanese citizens and foreigners with permanent residence status in Japan are not eligible
A selected fellow must submit an original copy of the doctoral degree certificate or diploma before the fellowship starting date
Host researcher must be a full-time researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution, eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and each host researcher can submit up to three applications
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
Submit the application form using the JSPS Electronic Application System by the deadline designated by the host institution

At least 18 years of age on entry

scholarships.title: MBZUAI Graduate Funding for M.Sc. and Ph.D. Students
scholarships.description: MBZUAI's graduate funding is not a single named scholarship but a University-and-faculty funding model under which funded M.Sc. and Ph.D. students receive free tuition fees, a monthly stipend, one return airfare each year to their home country, health insurance for the approved funding period, and a University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID where eligible. Ph.D. Year 1 funding is centrally funded by the University while the student is matched with a faculty advisor, and funding moves to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is secured through a faculty advisor-sponsored research or teaching assistantship, or an approved government scholarship for UAE nationals, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence is a fee-based programme and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding.

From an accredited university or college recognized by the UAE Ministry of Education (MoE)
Minimum CGPA of 3.0 or 3.5 (on a scale of 4.0) depending on the program
Senior-level students can apply initially with a copy of their transcript and, upon admission, must submit the official complete degree certificate and transcript
A degree attestation for degrees from the UAE, or a Certificate of Recognition for degrees acquired outside the UAE, should be furnished within the first semester at MBZUAI
requirements: Submit only one application per admission cycle; multiple submissions will not be processed
Submit a curriculum vitae
Submit a statement of purpose
Submit a research statement
Provide referee recommendations
Complete the screening exam
Take the technical interview if invited

scholarships.title: Wellcome Early-Career Award
scholarships.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and lead their own independent research programme. The award provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period, determined by the administering organisation, plus up to £400,000 for research expenses. Certain costs sit outside the £400,000 limit, including overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support, and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Staff salaries are funded up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, and no studentships are provided on this award.
eligibility: You should be able to demonstrate the ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, achieved through completion of a PhD or equivalent higher research degree (you must have passed your thesis defence by the date you submit your application), or through at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD.

Any periods of research undertaken during an undergraduate or Master's degree are not counted as equivalent research experience, and you must not have started a PhD or equivalent higher research degree if relying on the experience route.

You may have some postdoctoral experience in your proposed field of study, but no more than three years at the date of submission unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career.

You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project proposed in the award, and should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research related activities; if you are in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% of your time on clinical duties.

If you are a health professional and want to continue with clinical activities, you must be registered with, and be licensed by, the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.

Your administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China; the organisation must be not-for-profit and can be a higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation.

Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or an honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award, and must guarantee the space and resources you will need from the start date to the end date of the award.
You should also identify a mentor for the period of your award with a track record in training and mentorship; your sponsor can also be your mentor. Sponsors and mentors are not paid for their input.
Coapplicants are not accepted.
You may only have one application under consideration as a lead applicant at any one time for the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes.

Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing; it can be in any discipline including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health.
requirements: Submit your application through Wellcome Funding, and only once all required sections and documents are complete
Obtain a sponsor statement from an individual at your administering organisation who holds an established post for the duration of the award
Identify a mentor with a track record in training and mentorship
If requesting overheads, provide a letter from your Finance Director stating how overhead costs were calculated, including confirmation of any externally validated rate and when it was last reviewed
You must check that your type of research project is within what Wellcome funds in Discovery Research before applying
scholarships.duration: Usually 5 years, but may be less for some disciplines, and may only be longer if held on a part-time basis
scholarships.application_period: Rolling, applications accepted year-round. Location eligibility changes on 29 October 2026: from that date applications are only accepted from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia. Applications submitted on or before 28 October 2026 are assessed under the current location eligibility requirements.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. The same project may be submitted for consideration a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, and resubmissions must include significant changes demonstrating clear development of the original proposal. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.

On or after the date the JJ/WBGSP scholarship application process opens, not be employed (as a staff or any type of employment) by the Government of Japan or its related agencies, including JICA, local governments and the Central Bank

Have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past six years from the date of the Application Deadline

At the time of the application submission, be either admitted unconditionally (except for financing) or currently enrolled full-time in a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
requirements: Register interest with the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat by emailing scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org from February 15, 2027
Details on eligibility criteria for each call for applications are provided in that call's Application Guidelines, and those detailed criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions

Be admitted unconditionally (except for financing) to, or currently enrolled full-time in, a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries
Inform and document to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat any other sources of scholarship funds if notified of being a semi-finalist or awarded a scholarship
scholarships.duration: Up to two years; all JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
scholarships.application_period: A single application window for the 2027 cycle for Japanese nationals, from February 15 to April 16, 2027. From the opening date, prospective candidates are invited to register interest with the Secretariat by email. Results are communicated by mid-July 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10 on four factors: Quality of Academic Experience and Recommendation (20% weight), Quality of Professional Recommendations (20% weight), Quality of Professional Experience (20%), and Commitment to International Development Career (40% weight). The Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors plus maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists are presented to the JJ/WBG Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
scholarships.program_type: Development bank scholarship (bilateral government-funded graduate scholarship)
scholarships.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanes

scholarships.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS)
scholarships.description: The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are awarded annually by the Swiss Confederation to encourage international exchange and research cooperation between Switzerland and more than 180 other countries. Recipients are selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS, also known as ESKAS), an independent decentralised federal body that is not bound by directives. The programme has two components: research scholarships for talented early career researchers from abroad who have already completed a Master's degree, and art scholarships for students from a limited number of countries wishing to pursue an initial Master's degree in an artistic field in Switzerland. Applicants are aged 35 or less and the scholarship pays CHF 2,450 per month.
eligibility: Maximum age 35 (date of birth after 31 December 1991 for the 2027-2028 cycle)
Master's degree or equivalent completed by 31 July 2027 (30 June 2027 for ETH Zurich)
Applicants from one of the 183 eligible countries of origin
For PhD scholarships at graduate schools only: confirmation of admission to a doctoral school must be submitted together with the application
Letter of support from an academic supervisor in Switzerland, with a short CV of that supervisor
Applicants already residing in Switzerland must have entered Switzerland no earlier than 1 August 2026, evidenced by the registration confirmation or residence permit
For art scholarships: initial Master's degree in an artistic field in Switzerland, and nationality of one of the limited number of eligible countries
scholarships.duration: Research fellowships: maximum 12 months (minimum 6 months), no extension possible, start 1 September 2027. PhD scholarships: 12 months, renewable twice for up to 36 months subject to academic progress, start 1 September 2027.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. Applications open on 20 August 2026, country-specific deadlines apply between August and December 2026, and the Federal Commission announces its award decisions by the end of May at the latest for the following academic year.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are submitted to the applicant's Swiss diplomatic representation. The Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students assesses applications against three criteria: candidate profile, quality of the research project or artistic work, and synergies and potential for future research cooperation. Art scholarships are reviewed in consultation with the Federal Office of Culture.
scholarships.program_type: Government research scholarship (Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students, FCS/ESKAS)
scholarships.name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS)

scholarships.title: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP)
scholarships.description: The Swiss-European Mobility Programme is Switzerland's national mobility programme for higher education and forms part of the Swiss solution to the EU's Erasmus+ programme. Funded by SERI and implemented by the Swiss agency Movetia, it enables officially accredited Swiss higher education institutions and colleges of higher education to send their students and staff abroad (outgoing) and to host students and staff from abroad (incoming). Students, including PhD students, spend one or two semesters at a partner higher education institution and keep their enrolment at home, earning ECTS credits; they do not pay study fees abroad and receive financial support for travelling and accommodation.
eligibility: Enrolled at a higher education institution (university, university of applied sciences, university of teacher education) or college of higher education in Switzerland or abroad; PhD students included
Stay lasting between 60 days and 12 months
Interinstitutional agreement between the home and host institutions
Follow courses at the host institution that count towards the student's degree (ECTS credits or equivalent)
For funding applicants: an officially recognised Swiss higher education institution, or a college of higher education with federally recognised courses at higher education level
Accreditation under the SEMP Charter or a European Charter for Higher Education (ECHE); partner institutions abroad must hold an ECHE or formally accept the SEMP quality principles
scholarships.duration: 2 to 12 months per mobility (a stay must last between 60 days and 12 months); one or two semesters for study mobility
scholarships.application_period: Annual institutional cycle: applications from accredited institutions each March, funding period from 1 June. Student-level applications run year-round through the home institution's own deadlines. Movetia expects the next call to be launched under Erasmus+ following Switzerland's planned association from 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Participants are selected by their home institution through fair and transparent selection procedures and criteria; each institution sets its own participation criteria, and some award SEMP grants only for mobilities within Europe. Institutions may also apply internal restrictions, for example no mobility to the applicant's country of origin for foreign nationals, language skills, or mobility duration.
scholarships.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+
scholarships.name: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP)

scholarships.title: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) - Incoming Mobility to Switzerland
scholarships.description: Incoming mobility to Switzerland is funded under the Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP), the higher education part of the Swiss Programme for Erasmus+ that Switzerland operates in place of Erasmus+ association. Students from abroad, including PhD students, can spend one or two semesters at a Swiss university or college of higher education, or do a traineeship in Switzerland, while remaining enrolled at their home institution and earning ECTS credits. They do not pay study fees at the Swiss host institution and receive a financial contribution towards travel and accommodation. Applications are coordinated by the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which is the only party that can receive and pay out the grant.
eligibility: Enrolled at a higher education institution (university, university of applied sciences, university of teacher education) or college of higher education outside Switzerland; PhD students included
Stay of between 60 days and 12 months
Interinstitutional agreement between the home institution and the Swiss host institution
Courses at the host institution count towards the student's home degree (ECTS credits or equivalent)
For traineeships placed at a Swiss company or NGO, a Swiss higher education institution must still coordinate the application and pay out the grant
The Swiss host institution must be SEMP-accredited; grants can only be paid out by Swiss higher education institutions, and not all institutions offer grants
scholarships.duration: 2 to 12 months per mobility (minimum 60 days); one or two semesters for study mobility; traineeships of at least 60 days
scholarships.application_period: Annual institutional cycle with applications each March and a funding period from 1 June; student-level applications run through the Swiss host institution's own deadlines. Movetia expects the next call to be launched under Erasmus+ following Switzerland's planned participation from 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is carried out by the home institution abroad (which runs the application and nominates the student) and then by the Swiss host institution, which coordinates the SEMP application and pays out the grant. Swiss SEMP institutions apply their own transparent selection criteria and may restrict SEMP grants to certain destinations.
scholarships.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+ - incoming mobility
scholarships.name: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) - Incoming Mobility to Switzerland

scholarships.title: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) - Turkish Government Scholarship
scholarships.description: Türkiye Bursları is the Republic of Türkiye's government-funded, competitive scholarship programme for international students, run under the coordination of the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Relatives of Overseas Citizens (YTB). It funds associate, bachelor's, master's, PhD and research places at the most prestigious Turkish universities and is distinctive in providing university and department placement rather than a fellowship to be spent at a chosen institution. The package covers tuition, a monthly stipend, health insurance, accommodation, a one-year Turkish language course, a once-off return flight ticket and free academic and cultural programmes. Applications are submitted online, free of charge, through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS).
eligibility: Open to citizens of all countries
Competitive and merit-based selection with a strong emphasis on candidates' academic excellence
Candidates can select between 12 choices in the online application through TBBS
Candidates can only choose from the universities and departments offered to them in the system, which vary by educational background
Türkiye Scholarships does not award scholarships in the field of health sciences
Before applying, candidates are advised to check the equivalence and validity of the chosen fields in their own country
scholarships.duration: One year of free Turkish language education before or alongside the degree programme; associate degree is a two-year programme, with bachelor's, master's and PhD programmes of standard length. Research Scholarships have their own application periods.
scholarships.application_period: One annual period each year: 10 January to 20 February for international applicants, for associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral scholarships. Research Scholarships run on separate, individually announced periods.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are received in one period each year, free of charge. Candidates are given the opportunity to select between 12 choices online, and the programme assigns university and department placement.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (YTB, Türkiye Scholarships)
scholarships.name: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) - Turkish Government Scholarship

International first-year students are eligible for five merit scholarships - the International Traina Scholarship, the International Achievement Scholarship, the International Jonas Clark Scholarship, the Presidential Scholarship and the Global Scholars Scholarship. scholarships.title: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT) — MAECI / ICE / Uni-Italia scholarship programme
scholarships.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy is a MAECI scholarship programme run with the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia that pays a nine-month scholarship to foreign students from 22 partner countries to attend a Master's or Postgraduate course at a participating Italian university, combined with a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association. Courses are taught entirely in English, and the programme includes study of Italian language and culture plus a mandatory gender-equality and anti-gender-violence seminar or module. The winner receives an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800, paid quarterly into an Italian bank account in the holder's name, and is exempt from enrolment fees and university contributions, but must still pay the regional right-to-education tax, stamp duty, accident and civil liability insurance and health insurance. The scholarship explicitly does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance.
eligibility: Citizens of Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Mongolia, Paraguay, Peru, People's Republic of China, Tunisia, Türkiye, Uruguay or Vietnam, permanently resident in that country
Hold an academic qualification valid for enrolment in a Master's/Postgraduate degree programme at the chosen institution; students who are about to graduate are not eligible

Have submitted, following each university's own procedures, an application for pre-admission to a course included in the IYT programme; no exceptions are made for courses or universities not in the project
May apply for only one course (with a second, binding preference permitted for courses with limited enrolment)
Born on or after 1 January 2000, except applicants for scholarship renewal
English language proficiency certified from level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference
Knowledge of Italian certified, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure
Not currently studying at an Italian university and not holding an Italian university degree
requirements: Applications must be submitted exclusively online through the programme's My-App registration page
Online applications submitted between 20 April 2026 and 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time for the 11th edition
Names and surnames must be entered exactly as they appear on the passport
Multiple applications using different email addresses are strictly prohibited and will be rejected
The scholarship only covers attendance at courses in Italy; participation in university international mobility programmes, company internships abroad and thesis research abroad are not possible

scholarships.duration: 9 months of study, starting 1 October 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year

The official site carries the banner 'NEW APPLICATION OPENS 2027!' / 'IL NUOVO BANDO APRE NEL 2027!', so the next edition is announced but no opening date, closing date or application window has been published.
scholarships.selection_notes: Examination and evaluation of applications is carried out by the Technical Committee of the IYT Program (MAECI, ICE and Uni-Italia), which may use an ad hoc commission. Scholarships are allocated in quotas defined for each country and awarded on the basis of a comparative evaluation of the applications against the requirements in Articles 3 and 5 of the call. scholarships.title: ARES Scholarships - Bourses de formations internationales (scholarships for study in Belgium)
scholarships.description: ARES, the Walloon agency for international cooperation and education, awards scholarships so that professionals from its partner countries can study in Wallonia, in institutions of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. The 'bourses de formations internationales' cover a one-year bachelor of specialisation (bachelier de spécialisation), a specialised master's degree (master de spécialisation) or a short continuing-education course of up to six months, with study programmes that address development-related issues. The scholarship is aimed at people who are permanent residents and working in one of ARES's partner countries and who already hold a higher education diploma. For the 2026-2027 call 200 scholarships were available; for 2027-2028 the call offered one bachelor of specialisation, eight specialised master's degrees and one continuing-education certificate. Applications are submitted through the GIRAF platform and the selection is run by a jury for each programme.
scholarships.deadline: For the 2027-2028 call, applications had to be submitted through the GIRAF platform by Friday 18 September 2026 at 12h (Belgian time). The call is now closed and the next call is announced for August 2027.
scholarships.deadline_display: For the 2027-2028 call, applications had to be submitted through the GIRAF platform by Friday 18 September 2026 at 12h (Belgian time). The call is now closed and the next call is announced for August 2027.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle: the call opens in early August and applications close in mid-September, with preselection and selection running from October to May and results in June
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship of the Walloon government, administered by ARES
scholarships.name: ARES Scholarships - Bourses de formations internationales (scholarships for study in Belgium)

scholarships.title: Boren Scholarships and Fellowships (National Security Education Program)
scholarships.description: The National Security Education Program awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service. Boren Scholarships fund study abroad by U.S. undergraduates and Boren Fellowships fund research and language study proposals by U.S. graduate students, in world regions critical to U.S. interests. Maximum awards are determined by duration abroad: $25,000 for 25-52 weeks (preferred), $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, and $8,000 for 8-11 weeks for STEM majors under the Scholarships programme. There are no minimum language requirements except French and Spanish, which require intermediate high [1+] proficiency for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America. The Boren Awards are an initiative of the Defense Language and National Security Education Office.
eligibility: Be a U.S. undergraduate (Boren Scholarship) or graduate student (Boren Fellowship)
Commit to long-term overseas study in a world region critical to U.S. interests
Pursue a career with the federal government and accept the one-year federal service requirement
For Boren Scholarships studying STEM, satisfy the additional criteria for the shorter 8-11 week award tier
requirements: Study or research abroad in a region critical to U.S. interests
Accept the one-year federal service requirement
Submit by the national deadline; campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that must also be respected
There are no minimum language requirements except French and Spanish, which require intermediate high [1+] proficiency for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle tied to the academic year. 2027-28 funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028.
scholarships.selection_notes: The homepage directs applicants to review the official selection criteria, and frames professional goals as critical: the Boren Awards invest in linguistic and cultural knowledge for aspiring federal government employees, so the national security implications of the study and career opportunities matter to a successful application.
scholarships.program_type: Federal overseas study and research scholarship for U.S. students in national security critical regions
scholarships.name: Boren Scholarships and Fellowships (National Security Education Program)

scholarships.title: Kyushu University Friendship Scholarship
scholarships.description: Kyushu University's own support programme for privately financed international students who come to Kyushu University on exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree status and who cannot afford to study in Japan solely at their own expense. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 80,000, and the total of all scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed that amount. Applicants apply through their prospective host department at Kyushu University, not directly to the university centre. There are two recruitment periods per fiscal year: Period I around February for students who will study from April to September, and Period II around May for students who will study from October to March. The period of stay must be 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters).

Currently a student at an overseas university

Acceptance in Japan must begin within the academic year, for a stay of 3 months, 5 months (1 semester) or 11 months (2 semesters)

Selection is carried out through the host department, and eligibility criteria are the eight main requirements published by the International Student Support Center.

scholarships.title: Max Weber Fellowships — European University Institute Max Weber Programme for Postdoctoral Studies

The current call is for a 1 September 2027 start with an application deadline of 16 October 2026.

scholarships.title: Doctoral Scholarships — Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes (German Academic Scholarship Foundation
scholarships.description: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany's largest scholarship foundation and funds around 350 new doctoral students each year with a monthly stipend of EUR 1,650 for three years. Since 2024 it has replaced regional application rounds with four fixed two-week calls a year, each opening about eight months before the selection meeting. Applications are accepted only by post and must be complete. The current call runs from 1 to 14 October 2026, with the selection meeting in May 2027 and the earliest possible scholarship start on 1 July 2027.

scholarships.title: ACIAR Pacific Agriculture Scholarships and Support Program (PASS)
scholarships.description: The Pacific Agriculture Scholarships and Support (PASS) Program funds postgraduate research scholarships in agriculture, forestry and fisheries at the University of the South Pacific (USP) and Fiji National University (FNU). It is an Australian Government programme delivered by ACIAR, an Australian Government statutory authority, and is described by ACIAR as part of the Australian Government's support to Pacific neighbours. Scholarships are for Pacific Islander nationals and are awarded for up to two years at Master's level and up to three years for PhD candidates, with study available from Semester 1 2027.
eligibility: Be a citizen of and currently reside in Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu
Meet the eligibility criteria for postgraduate study at USP or FNU
Directly align the research proposal with a research topic in the PASS compendium, or develop a unique research proposal aligned with the compendium's broader research themes
Be able to meet government and university mandated requirements for travel to Fiji for study at FNU or USP Laucala, or to Samoa for study at USP Alafua

USP route: relevant Bachelor's degree with a GPA of 4.0 or above for Master's entry, or relevant Postgraduate Diploma plus Bachelor's with GPA 3.5 or over for both; or a relevant Bachelor's with GPA 4.5, a Master's by research, or a Master's with 25% or more independent research and a mini-thesis for PhD entry
USP route: 35 years or below when applying for Master's and 45 years or below for PhD, with flexibility considered in exceptional cases
requirements: Prepare the research intent in consultation with the relevant USP supervisor and co-supervisor named in the compendium
Pre-select a compendium research topic or propose a unique topic aligned with the broader compendium themes
Complete the PASS/ACIAR scholarship application form
Attach the required documentation to the completed application form
USP advises checking 200-level and 300-level GPA with the ACIAR Graduate Officer before applying
scholarships.duration: Up to 2 years for Master's students; 3 years (or over, if applicable) for PhD candidates
scholarships.application_period: 2027 intake: applications open 20 August 2026 and close 21 October 2026, for scholarships available from Semester 1 2027. ACIAR states scholarships are advertised annually through USP and FNU for commencement the following year.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are aligned to regional priorities identified in the PASS compendium of research topics and themes and may also be associated with an ACIAR research project. USP states that projects addressing gender, social systems, youth engagement, food systems and climate adaptation are also welcome.

scholarships.deadline_display: Applications closed for the current round; the programme reopens annually

benefits: Masters by Research or PhD scholarship administered through the Australia Awards system
Pastoral care and development opportunities from ACIAR during the scholarship

Sign a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia agreeing to comply with the conditions of the scholarship

Must pass the medical examination set by the applicable regulations
Certificates and supporting papers attested by the authorities specified by the institution

Attach the Saudi Cultural Attache or Saudi Embassy in the country of residence where applicable

requirements: Apply through the educational institution where you wish to study by submitting an admission application
The institution reviews the application and issues an admission decision
Once approved by the institution, the application is processed by the institution and the Ministry of Education to complete final admission procedures
Complete your platform profile before applying to academic programmes

Accepted by a host department on the approved 2027/2028 list
Stay of 6 to 12 weeks, at least 5 days per week

scholarships.title: Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF) In-Country Scholarship Scheme (ISS) 2026/27
scholarships.funding: Scholarship (coverage not itemised in the published guidelines)
scholarships.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund is a Nigerian federal government agency mandated with developing indigenous human capacity and petroleum technology for the oil and gas industry. The Fund invites applications from qualified Nigerians for its 2026/27 Undergraduate, Master's and PhD scholarships, restricted to Nigerian public universities and to a published list of sponsored courses grouped into engineering, science, environmental science, renewable energy and management. Undergraduate applicants must already be at 200 level in a Nigerian public university and must hold a valid admission letter; MSc and PhD applicants must hold full-time admission letters and a minimum Second Class Lower (2:2) in an oil and gas-related field. Selection is merit-driven and explicitly weighted toward equitable representation of the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
scholarships.deadline: Friday 5 June 2026 (2026/27 cycle: applications opened Monday 27 April 2026 and closed Friday 5 June 2026, a six-week window)
scholarships.deadline_display: Friday 5 June 2026 (2026/27 cycle: applications opened Monday 27 April 2026 and closed Friday 5 June 2026, a six-week window)
eligibility: Be a Nigerian citizen applying to study at a Nigerian public university only
Possess a National Identity Number (NIN) and verify it before applying; NIMC verification charges apply
Not have previously held a PTDF scholarship at the same or a lower level of degree
Undergraduate: be presently at 200 level and have completed first-year examinations
Undergraduate: hold a valid admission letter into the university
Undergraduate: possess at least 5 credits in WAEC/SSCE/NECO including English Language and Mathematics
Undergraduate: hold a minimum CGPA of 2.4 on a scale of 5.0 (Second Class Lower)
Postgraduate: possess a full-time admission letter into a public university
Postgraduate: hold a minimum of Second Class Lower (2:2) in an oil and gas-related field
Postgraduate: possess a National Youth Service Corps certificate or letter of exemption
Study a course on the published list of sponsored courses
Study full time; admission for part-time studies is not considered in any category
benefits: Scholarship award for Undergraduate, Master's or PhD study in a Nigerian public university
Access to the full published list of sponsored engineering, science, environmental science, renewable energy and management courses
requirements: Apply through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng
Verify your National Identity Number before starting the application
Upload all documents as legible PDFs at the file sizes indicated in the portal
Undergraduates: upload WAEC/SSCE/NECO results, admission letter, signed and stamped first-year transcript, certificate of indigeneship and a 300-word personal statement
MSc applicants: submit a personal statement of at least 1,000 words covering reasons for the study, relevance to the industry and expected impact on national development

PhD applicants: submit a research proposal of no more than 6 pages covering topic, introduction, literature review, research questions, methodology, mode of data collection, expected outcomes, novelty, relevance to the industry and references
Postgraduates: upload first-degree certificate or statement of results, NYSC certificate or exemption letter, WAEC/SSCE/NECO results, admission letter and certificate of indigeneship
PhD applicants additionally upload a second-degree certificate or statement of results
PhD applicants: download the proposal template from the applicant's profile on the portal

scholarships.duration: Not published as a fixed award term; the scheme covers Undergraduate, Master's and PhD awards within Nigerian public universities, with undergraduate eligibility anchored to study at 200 level
scholarships.application_period: 27 April 2026 to 5 June 2026 for the 2026/27 cycle. No 2027/28 window is published as of 2026-10-04; PTDF publishes an annual cycle under the same scheme.
scholarships.selection_notes: The scholarship is described as highly competitive and merit-driven. Undergraduate final selection is based on grades on transcripts, which must be signed and stamped by the HOD, Exams Officer or other authorised university personnel. A selection panel assesses postgraduate applications on academic merit as evidenced by quality of degrees, full academic transcripts, other professional qualifications and relevant publications; membership of professional bodies; the viability of the study or research plan for PhD applicants; the statement of purpose for undergraduate and MSc applicants; and the research proposal for PhD applicants. Selection is based on equitable representation of the 36 states of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory, except where a state does not have the requisite number of candidates to fill its allotted slots.

scholarships.title: Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS)
scholarships.description: The Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme is the Government of Mauritius scholarship for African students, run by the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research and open to resident citizens of African Union member states and African Commonwealth countries. The 2026 edition funds Diploma, Bachelor's, MPhil and PhD study at public higher education institutions in Mauritius, paying tuition and course-related costs up to a published cap, a monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 and a return airfare, while requiring awardees to have already secured or applied for a place at a listed Mauritian public institution. Applications are routed through a nominating agency in the applicant's own country, so the Ministry does not accept direct applications.
scholarships.deadline: No central date is published: each nominating agency sets its own deadline and communicates it to prospective applicants. For the 2026 edition the Mauritian public universities opened their own application windows from October 2025 and closed them between February and March 2026, so the next edition is expected to follow the same annual cycle.
scholarships.deadline_display: No central date is published: each nominating agency sets its own deadline and communicates it to prospective applicants. For the 2026 edition the Mauritian public universities opened their own application windows from October 2025 and closed them between February and March 2026, so the next edition is expected to follow the same annual cycle.
eligibility: Be a resident citizen of an African Union member state or an African Commonwealth country
For undergraduate programmes, be above 18 and not yet 26 on 1 January of the intake year
For MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD programmes, not yet 40 on 1 January of the intake year
Have already applied for a full-time on-campus Diploma, Degree, MPhil or PhD programme at a listed public higher education institution in Mauritius for the intake year
Hold a qualifying examination result with an overall average of about 60% or 12/20, or the A-level equivalent, or an equivalent qualification
Provide TOEFL 550 (paper), 213 (computer) or 79 (internet), or IELTS 5.5, where the language of instruction in the qualifying examination was not English
Not already hold an undergraduate degree when applying for an undergraduate programme
Not be a self-financing African student already studying in Mauritius applying for the same programme level
benefits: Annual payment of fees and study-related costs up to MUR 100,000 for beneficiaries from SADC countries and MUR 160,000 for beneficiaries from non-SADC countries
Monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 credited monthly against evidence of attendance from the institution
Return airfare from the country of origin to Mauritius and back after successful completion of the scholarship period
Student visa and provisional entry permit arranged by the host institution
Refunded university application fee for successful applicants
requirements: Submit the application through the nominating agency in your own country; applications not processed through a nominating agency are not considered
Obtain either a conditional offer from your chosen Mauritian public institution or proof of having paid its application fee
Produce original educational certificates in Mauritius within two weeks of arrival

The final and binding decision on award rests with the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research, and the Government reserves the right to offer no scholarship at all following a call.

scholarships.title: Türkiye Scholarships - IsDB Joint Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: A Türkiye Scholarships programme co-funded by the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities and the Islamic Development Bank, enabling high-achieving students from IsDB member countries and Muslim communities in other countries to study at internationally recognised universities in Türkiye. Scholarships are offered at associate, bachelor's, master's and PhD level and cover a monthly stipend, accommodation support, tuition fees, health insurance, a one-year Turkish language course and a one-time round-trip airfare. Associate and bachelor degree holders are required to repay the loan to the IsDB Education Trust after graduation and employment.
eligibility: Successful international students from IsDB member countries
Students from Muslim communities around the world living outside IsDB member countries
Minimum academic achievement of 70% for associate and bachelor's degree candidates
Minimum academic achievement of 75% for graduate candidates
Minimum academic achievement of 90% for candidates of Health Sciences (Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy)
Under 21 years of age for associate and bachelor's degree programmes
Under 30 years of age for master's programmes
Under 35 years of age for PhD programmes
Not a Turkish citizen and not a person who has lost Turkish citizenship
Not currently enrolled in a programme in Turkish universities at the level of education applied for
requirements: Apply through the Türkiye Scholarships official website only
Select 'Yes' under the 'Joint Scholarship Programs' section on the application screen in order to be considered for the joint programme
Choose a programme and department from the published list of eligible fields of study and countries
Meet the Türkiye Scholarships minimum academic achievement and age criteria for the level applied for
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 application period ran 10 January to 20 February 2026. Türkiye Scholarships publishes a General Application Period of 10 January to 20 February in its Application Calendar, so the next window falls in January and February 2027.
scholarships.selection_notes: The programme aims to support promising students in fields aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals and to contribute to the academic, cultural, social, political and economic development of developing countries. Candidates are selected through the Türkiye Scholarships evaluation and selection process, which the awarding body publishes separately.
scholarships.program_type: Government-funded bilateral scholarship for developing countries, co-funded with the Islamic Development Bank
scholarships.name: Türkiye Scholarships - IsDB Joint Scholarship Program

scholarships.title: Errol Walton Barrow Scholarships
scholarships.funding: Tuition Fee Waiver, Living Allowance and Airfare (bonded)
scholarships.description: The Errol Walton Barrow Scholarships are a Government of Barbados award administered by the Ministry of Education Transformation for Barbadian students of the country's newer secondary schools studying marine studies, aeronautics or culinary arts at undergraduate and postgraduate level. The award covers full tuition paid directly to the university, a return economy airfare and a per-annum living allowance. Winners must enter a bond with sureties to return and work in Barbados for one year for each year of the award, so the 2026 applications closed on 6 August 2026 and the next annual round is expected in the same cycle.
eligibility: Be citizens of Barbados
Have been accepted at an accredited institution
Be students of the newer secondary schools on the Ministry's published list
Apply in one of the funded areas: Marine Studies, Aeronautics, or Culinary Arts
benefits: One (1) direct economy class ticket to the country of study at the commencement of the course, and one (1) return ticket to Barbados on completion of the programme
Full tuition fees, payable directly to the University
Living allowance of $6,300.00 per annum for studies in the USA
Living allowance of $5,880.00 per annum for studies in Canada
Living allowance of $7,560.00 per annum for studies in the United Kingdom
requirements: Submit the completed Scholarship_Fellowship_Application_Form obtained from the Ministry
Submit before the published closing date; incomplete applications will not be accepted
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 cycle closed on 6 August 2026. The Ministry publishes a new call each year on its Latest News page, so the next round is expected in the same annual cycle.
scholarships.selection_notes: Awards are made in three named fields only - Marine Studies, Aeronautics and Culinary Arts - and only for students of the Ministry's listed newer secondary schools.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.funding_type: Tuition Fee Waiver, Living Allowance and Airfare (bonded)

scholarships.title: Perimeter Scholars International (PSI) Master's Program - Full Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Perimeter Scholars International (PSI) programme is a one-year Master's in theoretical physics at the University of Waterloo, taught by Perimeter Institute faculty and visiting physicists, with coursework plus a supervised research essay. Perimeter's financial support page states that full scholarships are available to cover full tuition, accommodation, meals, a living stipend, health insurance, necessary IT equipment and learning materials, and a travel supplement. Consideration for a full scholarship is part of the admissions process rather than a separate application. The programme is funded by the Savvas Chamberlain Family Foundation, the Hellenic Heritage Foundation, the Marsland Family and members of the Emmy Noether Circle.
eligibility: Hold or be completing a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in physics or a closely related field
Be a citizen of a country other than Canada
Demonstrate strong academic preparation in mathematics and physics
For applicants with other degrees, demonstrate understanding of classical mechanics, electromagnetism, special relativity, quantum mechanics and statistical physics
Be willing to study in person at Perimeter Institute in Waterloo, Ontario for the full academic year
Agree to consider other funding sources such as the NSERC Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's, where eligible
benefits: Full tuition paid for the PSI programme
Necessary IT equipment and learning materials
Access to senior student and academic staff mentors, wellness initiatives and mental health support
Eligibility to be considered for Perimeter's PhD Residency Program Award progression route
requirements: Complete the PSI online application before the published deadline
Provide academic transcripts and evidence of degree completion or expected completion
Supply references as required by the application form
No application fee is charged
Canadian PSI applicants should apply to the NSERC Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's before December 1 and discuss the outcome with Perimeter
PSI students are expected to apply for any non-PSI scholarship funding for which they may be eligible
scholarships.duration: One year (one academic year) of full-time master's study
scholarships.application_period: Applications are open with a published submission deadline of Sunday January 24, 2027 at 11:59 pm ET. There is no application fee. Selected candidates may be contacted for a short oral interview.
scholarships.selection_notes: Consideration for a full scholarship is part of the PSI admissions process. Perimeter states it is committed to diversity within its community and especially welcomes applications from racialized persons, women, Indigenous or Aboriginal People of North America, persons with disabilities and LGBTQ2+ persons, and provides support and accommodations throughout the application and interview process for applicants with disabilities.
scholarships.program_type: Institute-sponsored fully funded master's programme
scholarships.name: Perimeter Scholars International (PSI) Master's Program - Full Scholarship

scholarships.title: Killam Fellowships Program (Fulbright Canada)
scholarships.description: The Killam Fellowships Program, administered by Fulbright Canada, lets exceptional undergraduates from universities in Canada and the United States spend one semester or a full academic year as an exchange student in the other country. Fellows receive a cash award of US$6,000 per semester, or US$12,000 for a full academic year, plus a health benefit plan for American Fellows, a three-day orientation in Ottawa and a three-day spring seminar in Washington. All Fellows may apply for a mobility grant of up to CAD 800 for an educational field trip. Fellows either pay their home university fees as direct exchange students or pay host tuition as self-placed visiting students, so the award is a stipend rather than a tuition scholarship.
scholarships.deadline: January 31 for the open competition; institution-set internal deadline for the direct exchange
scholarships.deadline_display: January 31 for the open competition; institution-set internal deadline for the direct exchange
eligibility: Be an undergraduate student at a participating American or Canadian university
For the direct exchange route, be registered at a participating American university and plan to visit a participating Canadian university, or the equivalent for Canadians visiting the United States
Spend either one semester or a full academic year in the host country
Apply through the direct exchange institutional process or the open competition
Meet the academic criteria set by the home and host institutions
benefits: Cash award of US$6,000 per semester
Cash award of US$12,000 for a full academic year
Health benefit plan provided to all American Killam Fellows
Three-day orientation in Ottawa each fall and a three-day spring seminar in Washington
Mobility or in-country travel grant of up to CAD 800
Alumni enrichment opportunities including the Fulbright Canada Alumni Internship Program, the Killam Community Action Initiative and the Local Ambassador Program
requirements: Apply during the annual competition window, which opens on August 15
For the direct exchange route, apply by the internal deadline of the home institution
For the open competition, apply by January 31
Be registered at, and plan to study at, a participating university in the other country
Choose direct exchange or self-placed visiting student status, which determines who pays tuition
scholarships.duration: One semester or a full academic year
scholarships.application_period: The competition opens annually on August 15. Applications are for placement in Fall or Spring of the next school year, submitted by the internal deadline of the home institution for the direct exchange route, or by January 31 for the open competition.
scholarships.selection_notes: The programme is described as providing an opportunity for exceptional undergraduate students. Fulbright Canada requires new Fellows to attend the fall orientation in Ottawa and offers a spring seminar in Washington.
scholarships.program_type: Binational undergraduate exchange fellowship
scholarships.name: Killam Fellowships Program (Fulbright Canada)

scholarships.title: Fulbright-Garcia Robles Graduate Degree Program (COMEXUS, Mexico)
scholarships.description: The COMEXUS Fulbright-Garcia Robles Graduate Degree Program funds US candidates to complete a master's or PhD degree at a qualified Mexican academic institution. COMEXUS will fund up to two academic years for a master's and up to three academic years for a PhD, with an initial academic year of funding and continuation subject to academic performance and availability of funds. Financial support comprises monthly maintenance, one round-trip international air ticket for the grantee, a Fulbright medical benefit plan, COMEXUS assistance with visa paperwork, and up to 50,000 pesos per academic year to cover tuition. Applications are accepted in all fields except medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry.
eligibility: Be a US citizen or US national eligible to apply
Have fluent Spanish at an advanced level
Hold a minimum of a B.S. or B.A. degree
Apply to a graduate degree programme at a qualified Mexican university or academic institution
Present an admission letter prior to the grant start date
Not be studying, living or working in Mexico during the application process
Not hold a temporary or permanent resident card for Mexico
Field of study must not be medicine, veterinary medicine or dentistry
requirements: Complete every required field and upload all required documents in the online application
Provide a Program Information section stating field of study, project title and an abstract or summary
Write a Statement of Grant Purpose explaining country and institution choice, programme options, academic background, language skills, community engagement and adaptation
Secure an affiliation letter from a Mexican university academic department and present an admission letter before the final grant offer
Submit a Language Self-Evaluation and a Foreign Language Evaluation completed by a qualified evaluator, with advanced Spanish required
Submit three recommendation letters from referees registered in the online system
Provide transcripts from all institutions where degrees were earned and from other institutions where 12 or more credits were taken
Obtain home institution IRB review for research involving human or animal subjects
Complete the short-answer sections on flexibility and adaptability, community engagement and impact of the Fulbright award
scholarships.duration: Up to 2 academic years for a master's degree and up to 3 academic years for a PhD, with the first academic year funded and continuation subject to performance and budget availability
scholarships.application_period: The 2026-27 cycle opened on March 31, 2026 and closes on October 6, 2026 at 5:00 PM EST. Shortlisted candidates are invited to interview in Spanish in March 2027, grantees with August or September start dates attend a mandatory orientation in Mexico City in the last week of August 2027, and the programme start follows the host institution's academic calendar.
scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants must explain their choice of country and institution, identify the programmes and institutions they are considering, demonstrate relevant academic background and language skills, and describe how they will engage with the host community and adapt to life in the host country. Grantees will not receive the award until admitted to a qualified programme, and deferral of the grant to a different year is not allowed.
scholarships.program_type: Binational government exchange scholarship
scholarships.name: Fulbright-Garcia Robles Graduate Degree Program (COMEXUS, Mexico)

scholarships.title: Posse Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Posse Foundation awards a full-tuition scholarship to each Posse Scholar to attend one of its partner colleges or universities in the United States. Students cannot apply directly: they must be nominated by their high school or a community-based organisation in one of Posse's more than 20 recruitment cities, and they take part in Posse's Dynamic Assessment Process nomination programme. Posse describes the scholarship as neither a minority nor a need-based award, and states that it is open to students of all backgrounds. Beyond tuition, Posse runs a Pre-Collegiate Training programme before college, a Campus Program with staff and faculty mentors once enrolled, Posse Plus retreats, a Career Program and a Fellowship Program for alumni.
eligibility: Be nominated by your high school or a community-based organisation
Be in the first term of your senior year in high school
Demonstrate leadership within your high school, community or family
Demonstrate academic potential
Apply on time, within your Posse city's nomination window
Be reachable through the Dynamic Assessment Process in your city
benefits: Full-tuition scholarship at a Posse partner college or university
Campus Program with regular meetings from Posse staff and faculty mentors
Fellowship Program and fellowship winners network for alumni
requirements: Be nominated by a high school or community-based organisation, since Posse does not accept direct applications
Participate in the Dynamic Assessment Process
Apply within the nomination window for your Posse city or programme
Contact your local Posse office for specific deadlines at the start of every calendar year
scholarships.duration: Four years of undergraduate study at a Posse partner college or university
scholarships.application_period: Posse states that nominations are accepted in the spring and summer before senior year begins, and that nomination timelines and deadlines vary by Posse city or programme, so applicants must contact their local Posse office for the specific dates at the start of every calendar year.
scholarships.selection_notes: Posse looks for leaders in their high schools and communities, students committed to their education who demonstrate academic potential, and students interested in teamwork and diversity, describing the ideal candidate as positive, motivated, talented and ambitious. The Posse Arts Program and Posse Veterans Program run separate nomination processes.
scholarships.program_type: Nominations-based college scholarship

scholarships.description: The Allama Muhammad Iqbal Scholarship is a Government of Pakistan initiative, administered by the Higher Education Commission, that brings students from Central Asian and other friendly countries to study in Pakistan. HEC describes the award as fully funded, covering tuition fees in full plus a monthly stipend, an accommodation allowance and airfare as per policy. Applicants apply online through the HEC scholarship portal, and several eligible Asian countries are named in the programme's eligibility list.

scholarships.description: The Allama Muhammad Iqbal Scholarships for Students from Bangladesh are the student component of the Government of Pakistan's Pak-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor, a bilateral initiative to strengthen ties between the two countries. HEC awards fully funded places to Bangladeshi citizens to study medicine, engineering, computer science, business administration, mass communication, media studies, and basic and social sciences at Pakistani public and private universities, across Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Coverage includes full tuition, a stipend, hostel and mess charges, a settlement allowance, an air ticket, and books and stationery. Recipients are contractually required to serve Bangladesh after completing their education in Pakistan.

scholarships.description: The Allama Iqbal Scholarships for Srilankan Students are the student component of the Government of Pakistan's Pak-Sri Lanka Higher Education Cooperation Programme, which HEC runs with the Pakistan High Commission in Colombo and Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. HEC describes the allocation as 800 fully funded and 200 partially funded places. Benefits are full programme tuition, an accommodation allowance, a study allowance, a books allowance and a one-time return air ticket, and HEC explicitly encourages women candidates to apply.

scholarships.title: HKUST Global Learners Scholarship
scholarships.description: The Global Learners Scholarship was established by HKUST to support the University's strategic objective of enhancing the diversity of its student community. Applicants do not apply for it: all undergraduate programme applicants from underrepresented nationalities are considered automatically, and the decision is normally communicated with the offer of admission. Awardees receive a full tuition waiver that is renewable for the normal duration of the study, subject to satisfactory academic performance, and a School or Programme Office may add a top-up as long as the combined limit of full tuition fee plus an HK$60,000 annual allowance is not exceeded. The University opened its online application system for 2027/28 entry in early October 2026, with a Priority Round deadline of 25 November 2026.
eligibility: Must apply to an HKUST undergraduate programme with international qualifications
Must hold a nationality the University treats as underrepresented, which is the basis on which HKUST targets this scholarship
Must be a non-local applicant seeking admission to HKUST
No separate scholarship application is required - consideration is automatic with the admission application
requirements: Apply to an HKUST undergraduate programme through the University's online application system
Hold a nationality that HKUST classifies as underrepresented
Do not rely on a separate scholarship application, since none exists
Maintain satisfactory academic performance to keep the waiver renewable
scholarships.duration: Renewable for the normal duration of the undergraduate degree, subject to satisfactory academic performance
scholarships.application_period: Open now for HKUST's 2027/28 entry: the online application system opened in early October 2026, the Priority Round deadline is 25 November 2026, applications are accepted on a rolling basis from 26 November 2026 onwards, offers are announced in late December 2026 and the application deadline is 30 June 2027. The scholarship itself requires no separate application.
scholarships.selection_notes: HKUST states that students do not have to apply for the scholarship and that all undergraduate programme applicants from underrepresented nationalities are automatically considered, with the decision normally notified when the offer of admission is received. The University states that the English version of the terms always prevails in case of any discrepancy with the Chinese version. Separately from this award, HKUST also runs merit-based admissions scholarships awarded to top students on academic merit and non-academic achievements, non-academic scholarships requiring separate applications (Future Leaders Award and Beyond Academic Admissions Scholarship), a University Admissions Scholarship for Other Qualifications Holders and a Scholarship Scheme for International/Asian Olympiad Medalists.
scholarships.program_type: University admission scholarship (needs-blind, diversity-targeted)

scholarships.title: ITB International Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.description: The ITB International Undergraduate Scholarship is a fully funded grant run through Institut Teknologi Bandung's financial aid office for selected young applicants from partner countries in ASEAN, the Asia-Pacific and Africa who want to study at Indonesia's leading technological university. The published package covers the whole S1 degree: full exemption from tuition fees for all eight academic semesters, a monthly living allowance of IDR 4,700,000, a one-time arrival settlement of IDR 10,000,000 to secure private off-campus accommodation, a round-trip economy air ticket at cost to Jakarta, basic health insurance and visa fee coverage. Applicants must hold a 12-year high school diploma with a GPA of at least 3.00 out of 4.00 and IELTS 6.0 or an accepted equivalent, and the university provides no dormitory support.

Must hold a 12-year high school diploma or equivalent official senior high school credentials; anyone already holding or pursuing an S1 degree is ineligible
Minimum cumulative high school GPA of 3.00 out of 4.00

Must provide a valid English proficiency certificate obtained within the last two years: TOEFL ITP 550, TOEFL iBT 63, IELTS 6.0, or an equivalent Duolingo English Test, or official school statements confirming English as the primary medium of instruction
Must submit a certified medical report
Must not be an active military service member
Must demonstrate a clean criminal record verified by home country authorities

Hold a legalized 12-year high school graduation certificate and transcript documentation
Achieve a cumulative high school GPA of at least 3.00 out of 4.00
Provide an English proficiency certificate obtained within the last two years meeting TOEFL ITP 550, TOEFL iBT 63 or IELTS 6.0, or an accepted equivalent

No 2027 intake window was published at the time of checking, so this is treated as a recurring annual award whose next cycle follows the same pattern.
scholarships.selection_notes: ITB describes the scholarship as a direct financial support programme for selected young talents from partner countries in ASEAN, Asia-Pacific and Africa, and states that the financial support applies exclusively to the individual awardee and does not account for any family dependencies. Selection is staged: document submission and online registration, a finalization stage, and an ITB academic qualification and English-language qualification simulation. The university states no dormitory or hostel accommodation support is provided, so recipients arrange private off-campus accommodation themselves using the arrival settlement allowance. A compulsory Indonesian language course is part of every undergraduate programme.
scholarships.program_type: University-funded scholarship (institution-financed, partner-country targeted)
scholarships.name: ITB International Undergraduate Scholarship

scholarships.title: John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship (Curtin University)

Not be enrolled in one of the excluded courses

Not be enrolled in secondary school at the time of applying, unless enrolled as an adult student

scholarships.title: Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund
scholarships.description: The Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund promotes initiatives that advance peace in New Zealand and is open to a woman, or a group led by a woman, developing an initiative at home, school, the workplace or in the community. It commemorates Sonja Davies, a New Zealand women's rights campaigner and politician, and includes work on family violence, inter-group understanding, mediation and conflict resolution. Awards are worth up to NZD 4,000, and the Trust publishes the 2026 application window as 12 to 30 October.

Be a New Zealand citizen, or hold a resident class visa, and currently live in New Zealand
Not have previously received a New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura Award
Be developing an initiative that will advance peace in New Zealand
